6 Tuesday 15                     DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                               May 2018
--- seg-e649fd9c2280abd1da7f3fa6 [needs-review] ---
Proceedings of the 108th Session of the Chamber of Deputies, Solem Non-Deliberative Morning Session, 4th Ordinary Legislative Session, 55th Legislature, on May 14, 2018.

Presiding Officers: Alberto Fraga, Izalci Lucas, in accordance with Article 18, §2, of the Internal Regulation.

At the 108th (eighty-eighth) Session of the Chamber of Deputies, Solem Non-Deliberative Morning Session, 4th Ordinary Legislative Session, 55th Legislature, on May 14, 2018, at 10:17, Mr. Alberto Fraga, presiding in accordance with Article 18, §2, of the Internal Regulation, opened the session and waived the reading of the previous session's minutes. The President requested a moment of silence in memory of the 4th Secretary of the Chamber of Deputies, Mr. Rômulo Gouveia. He then announced that the session would honor the Military Police of the Federal District, paid due respects, and invited to the presidium Mr. Izalci Lucas, author of the request; Colonel William Delano Marques de Araújo, Commander of the Community Police and Human Rights Center, representing Colonel Marcos Antônio Nunes de Oliveira, General Commander of the PMDF; Colonel Arnaldo da Costa Farias Filho, from the II Metropolitan Regional Command, representing Colonel Fábio Aracaqui de Sousa Lima, Deputy Commander of the PMDF; Colonel Edgar Cesar Rojas, from the II West Regional Command, representing Colonel Ricardo Yamazaki Santiago, Chief of Staff of the PMDF; and Colonel Marcylon Back da Silva, Chief of the PMDF Operational Department. The President invited everyone to listen to the National Anthem and the Military Police of the Federal District Song, performed by the Military Police of the Federal District Band, under the direction of Maestro Josael Albertino Moreira, General Bandmaster of the PMDF. He then invited everyone to listen to “The History of the PMDF,” told by teacher and storyteller Nyedja Gennari. After the institutional video, the President delivered the speech of Mr. Rodrigo Maia, President of the Chamber of Deputies, and granted the floor to Mr. Izalci Lucas, author of the request. During his speech, he presented an honor certificate to Mr. First Lieutenant Herison de Oliveira Bezerra; Sergeant Cleônio Rodrigues de Sousa; and First Sergeant Arizomar Pereira Gonçalves. In accordance with Article 18, §2, of the Internal Regulation, Mr. Izalci Lucas assumed the presidency and granted the floor to Mr. Alberto Fraga, author of the request. During his speech, he presented an honor certificate to Major Graziela Guedes Salgado; Sergeant Heitor Theodoro da Silva; Third Sergeant Marcelo Brito Magalhães; and Samantha Moreira da Costa Santos, widow of Corporal Luciano Pereira dos Santos. The President then granted the floor to the members of the presidium, William Delano Marques de Araújo; Arnaldo da Costa Farias Filho; and Marcylon Back da Silva. The President noted the presence of guests, reiterated the tributes, thanked everyone's attendance, and at 11:32, adjourned the session.
--- seg-f35e0ab847de261d816c5912 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Rodrigo Maia

President

PLS No. 350/2015
OFÍCIO nº 497/18 (SF)
--- seg-4b025f35087fb446cfbc45a8 [needs-review] ---
It concerns the defense of competition within the scope of action of financial institutions and other institutions. subject to the supervision or surveillance of the Central Bank of Brazil and on cooperation and sharing of competencies between the Central Bank of Brazil and the Administrative Council for Economic Defense (Cade) in competitive article and repeals § 2 of art. 18 of Law No. 4,595 of December 31, 1964.
--- seg-4b2c22c42047de8fbbeab9a6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
REFER TO PLP-265/2007.
--- seg-d2cd639a1ccce32221b3a5ea [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-5ceb240c461f90f49c3f2741 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The National Congress decrees:
--- seg-79f8bc8edf852088452b3722 [machine-unreviewed] ---
CHAPTER I

PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS
--- seg-118333102596f98dc2e93d2f [needs-review] ---
Article 1: This Supplementary Law provides for competition defense within the scope of financial institutions and other institutions subject to supervision or monitoring by the Central Bank of Brazil, and for cooperation and sharing of competencies between the Central Bank of Brazil and the Administrative Council for Economic Defense (Cade) in competitive matters. Art. 2º O The Central Bank of Brazil and the Competition Authority (Cade), within their respective jurisdictions, shall coordinate their activities to ensure the fulfillment of their duties with greater efficiency and lower costs for the regulated entities. Single paragraph. The Central Bank of Brazil and the Competition Authority (Cade) will maintain a permanent forum for communication, including through a technical cooperation agreement, to comply with this Supplementary Law.
--- seg-53b0651b8e51f49c24dce4a2 [machine-unreviewed] ---
CHAPTER II

OF ACTS OF CONCENTRATION
--- seg-982b04b1ecd11048e4c514cd [needs-review] ---
Article 3. It is the responsibility of the Central Bank of Brazil and the Competition and Consumer Protection Agency (Cade) to review concentration acts between financial institutions.

§ 1. Pleas related to concentration acts shall be submitted by the interested parties to the Central Bank of Brazil and Cade, in accordance with the deadlines and conditions established in a regulation to be jointly issued by the agencies.

§ 2. The review of the pleas referred to in § 1 shall be conducted in each agency through specific procedures and regulations.

§ 3. In conducting the review of concentration acts, the Central Bank of Brazil and Cade shall share information and studies regarding the operation, subject to legal confidentiality, with a view to aligning technical parameters, in accordance with the conditions set out in the joint regulation mentioned in § 1.

§ 4. Subject to the situation provided for in Article 4, the effectiveness of concentration acts involving financial institutions is conditioned upon the authorization of both agencies, in accordance with the deadlines and conditions established in the joint regulation referred to in § 1.

===== PAGE 27 [page-00eb9a605eb1bc6d12f0de5c] =====
--- seg-a5d7e7320e0e54350c0616a7 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                          Tuesday, May 15, 27
--- seg-65d290aa58b2829e0f2c8096 [needs-review] ---
conditions provided for in the joint regulation referred to in § 1.
           § 5. Without prejudice to the competence of the Cade, in accordance with the legislation in force, the Central Bank of
Brazil may conclude concentration control agreements with the interested parties.
           § 6º O The agreement provided for in § 5 may be signed jointly by the Central Bank of Brazil and
the Cade, in accordance with the joint regulation referred to in § 1. **Article 4º O** The Central Bank of Brazil may unilaterally approve concentration acts involving a financial institution whenever prudential aspects indicate significant and imminent risks to the solidity and stability of the National Financial System.

**§ 1st** An operation with prudential aspects is considered to be one that, in the judgment of the Central Bank of Brazil:

I. Involves a risk to the solidity of a financial institution or a segment of the National Financial System;

II. Compromises the maintenance of the stability of the National Financial System and the prevention of systemic crisis;

III. Impairs the effectiveness of a resolution regime applied to a financial institution;

IV. Impairs the effectiveness of measures necessary to mitigate the need for application of a resolution regime;

V. Impairs the effectiveness of measures necessary to reverse the trajectory of loss of solidity of a financial institution or a segment of the National Financial System with a business model identified as inconsistent, vulnerable, or unviable.

**§ 2nd** Upon approval of a concentration act by the Central Bank of Brazil, as provided in the heading, the Central Bank of Brazil shall notify the CADE of its decision within one (1) business day, indicating the grounds for its decision and informing whether the prudential aspects cover the entire operation or only specific relevant markets.

**§ 3rd** In the case of § 2nd, CADE shall approve the operation without restrictions, using the grounds of the Central Bank of Brazil's decision as a basis for recognizing economic efficiency and development, in accordance with Article 88, § 6, Item I, subitem “c”, of Law No. 12,529 of November 30, 2011.

**§ 4th** The CADE's analysis, as provided in § 3rd, does not prevent the immediate implementation of the concentration act, and the provisions of Article 88, § 3, of Law No. 12,259 of November 30, 2011, do not apply to this case.

**§ 5th** Without prejudice to the notification by the Central Bank of Brazil, as provided in § 2nd, the parties shall notify CADE, in accordance with Article 53 of Law No. 12,529 of November 30, 2011, under penalty of imposition of a monetary fine, of an amount not less than R$ 60,000.00 (sixty thousand reais) nor more than R$ 60,000,000.00 (sixty million reais), without prejudice to the initiation of an administrative proceeding, in accordance with Article 69 of Law No. 12,529 of November 30, 2011.
--- seg-b6b4ea9dedf235254955e41e [machine-unreviewed] ---
CHAPTER III

--- seg-a2ddabcd6e723ef2f1cfaff9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-39832e59fce78ae0dccd7d41 [needs-review] ---
This Draft Complementary Law reprises and deepens the intention that guided the elaboration of the very Law on Fiscal Responsibility - LRF, which it intends to amend. It is about establishing criteria and limits, as it was in 2000 when it was promulgated, to ensure that state management does not become a tool for the depletion of public assets. It is no coincidence, in fact, that the Fiscal Responsibility Law contains a chapter specifically dedicated to patrimonial management (chap. VIII) and, within it, a section dedicated to the preservation of public heritage (section II). Both the chapter and the section indicate that the legislator's concern was not limited to the protection of the administration's cash flow, but extended to the preservation of the State's patrimonial stock. In fact, ultimately, this second concern should be decisive, as it is there that the greatest depredations, the most demeaning expropriations of assets belonging to the Brazilian people can occur. It is in this sense that there is no exaggeration when, in the first line of this Justification, it is argued that the PLP not only reprises but also deepens the intentionality of the Law. The passage of time has only strengthened the perception that, in 2000, culminating a process that spanned the entire 1990s, the legislator's attention was overly focused on controlling spending, or at best, on

===== PAGE 32 [page-eb67f02bddd5389e07b346ae] =====
--- seg-952839f9267dadb7967dd599 [machine-unreviewed] ---
32 Tuesday, May 15                   DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-95b73c38e581bdcc00a32a96 [needs-review] ---
ensuring a balance in the short and medium term between revenues and expenses, given that the well-being of the population is more intimately linked to the preservation of the State's patrimonial capacity to respond to its legitimate aspirations for quality public services. This aspect of the issue has thus been placed partially in the background; deepening the intentionality of the Law means, therefore, giving it the appropriate prominence in the legal order, as this proposal aims to do. Certainly, none of this implies the irrelevancy of the effort to achieve the state's fiscal balance. On the contrary, when fiscal balance is not purely and simply understood as a reduction in social spending, which, surprisingly, sometimes happens, it turns out to be a condition for good governance and investment in better living conditions for the population. No defense is made here for the elimination of
the ability to manage public property when circumstances demand it. There is no reason to assume that the state must forever remain in the areas of action chosen in the past, due to purposes that may be obsolete. What is intended is to prevent hasty measures, running against the clock, to secure cash resources for immediate purposes or, worse, to please sectors that may favor those holding mandates in their eventual desire to remain in office. If Article 42 of the LRF (Law of Financial Responsibility) prevents the management from contracting, at the end of the term, an expenditure obligation that cannot be fully met within it (an obligation that, obviously, may have a character of squandering, but it can also represent an investment of relevance to the population), then the Law should be even more concerned with the possibility that the same management, just before its end, disposes of a hard-earned asset by the country, often resulting from the effort of generations. It is noteworthy, indeed, that the LRF expresses particular concern about measures taken in the last year of the terms of office of those in power. This is the case, for example, with the restriction on increasing
expenditure on personnel (art. 21, § unique) and the prohibition of credit operations by anticipation of revenue
(art. 38, IV, b). In this regard, it aligns with Law No. 9,504 of September 30, 1997 (Electoral Law), which dedicates a chapter to prohibited conduct by public officials during electoral campaigns. In both cases, the norm is perceived as being particularly susceptible to government initiatives driven by the interests of groups or sectors with which the rulers have a privileged relationship, to the detriment of general public interests. It is precisely because this Complementary Law Project does not conflict with the concerns that led to the approval of the Fiscal Responsibility Law, but rather extends and deepens them, that we count on your approval, in the short term, from you, ladies and gentlemen, parliamentarians. Session Room, on May 02, 2018.

JUSTIFICATION

The protection of bank secrecy is a consequence of the fundamental guarantees of privacy and intimacy, ensured by the 1988 Constitution. It derives from these guarantees the legal mandate, established in Complementary Law No. 105 of January 10, 2000, that information relating to transactions conducted by financial institutions not be disclosed.

===== PAGE 36 [page-439e7628173ac44e0bde087c] =====
--- seg-54dd80a485355ea064abebb0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
36 Tuesday, May 15                   JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-8a30a18d66caf616d7236ade [machine-unreviewed] ---
The fact is that privacy and intimacy protection may give way to other interests, notably the preservation of other fundamental guarantees and clauses.
--- seg-4084f2858fbf3046eac8bcfd [needs-review] ---
When it comes to credit operations contracted by legal entities of public law, it seems to us that the republican principle takes precedence, which recommends maximum transparency regarding measures that involve public administration debt. It is not even logical to speak of privacy or intimacy of entities within the Federation or their public autonomous agencies and foundations.
--- seg-be741ea8f4799cb5e4e5feb9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
For these reasons, we present this draft law, which amends the legislation on bank secrecy, to stipulate that the duty of secrecy imposed on financial institutions does not apply to transactions they enter into with public law legal entities.
--- seg-de7f12f989bedcae39de8f73 [machine-unreviewed] ---
We count on the support of our Colleagues to debate and approve this proposal.

Article 1. This Complementary Law amends Complementary Law No. 116 of July 31, 2003, as modified by Complementary Law No. 157 of December 29, 2016, which concerns the Tax on Services of Any Nature, under the jurisdiction of municipalities and the Federal District, and provides for other measures.       “Article 3-A. The following entities are considered service users as per article 3, section XXIII of this Supplementary Law:

"III – In the case of portfolio managers for clients, pre-dated checks, and similar services, the service provider is considered the administrator itself."

"Article 3-C." The customer's domicile, in the case of services covered by article 3, paragraph XXV of this Supplementary Law, shall be:
       I – in the case of commercial lease (leasing), the customer of the service is the lessee. II - in the case of franchise services (franchising), the service recipient is the franchisee. III - in the case of factoring services, the service recipient is the one being invoiced."
Article 3 - This Law enters into force on the date of its publication, repealing contrary provisions. JUSTIFICATION

       The proposed Complementary Law presented here aims to clarify ambiguities arising from the
amendments made to Complementary Law No. 116/2003 by Complementary Law No. 157/2016 regarding

===== PAGE 38 [page-f7796fe8b93003b051bc0476] =====
--- seg-5b0a70694e1ee511415e9da5 [machine-unreviewed] ---
38 Tuesday, May 15                   JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-546766e734a4a4e4903440af [needs-review] ---
The location of service provision and subsequent collection of the Service Tax (ISS).

With the amendment brought about by LC 157/2016 in LC 116/2003, the collection of ISS for credit and debit card services, leasing, health plans, merchant leasing (leasing), franchising, and factoring became due in the municipality of the service recipient's domicile, rather than the municipality where the establishments in question are headquartered.

Therefore, some services that underwent a change regarding the location of ISS payment require identifying the legal entities capable of receiving them, as this municipality will be the one holding the collected ISS.

In this regard, the approval of this Complementary Law Project is necessary to determine who the service recipients are for specific activities, thus eliminating any discrepancies in municipal legislation that could lead to double taxation of the aforementioned tax.

For instance, let's consider the activity of merchant leasing (leasing). This is one of the activities affected by the change in LC 157/2016. Previously, when an individual purchased a good in a specific city through the leasing modality, the ISS was due to the municipality where the lessor's headquarters were located. Now, with the amendment introduced by LC 157/2016 in LC 116/2003, the tax will be collected by the municipal entity where the lessee resides.

The new ISS Law demands significant changes and adjustments in the respective laws of each municipality. Thus, the municipal administrator must stay vigilant regarding these new changes and adapt the Municipal Tax Code to accommodate the alterations brought about by LC 116/2003.

However, due to the uncertainty surrounding who the "new" taxpayers should pay, it is necessary to approve this Complementary Law to prevent distortions regarding who should collect the ISS in the cases addressed here.

Indeed, taxpayers affected by the change in LC 116/2003 have filed actions at the Supreme Federal Court (STF), one of the arguments being to define who is the recipient of services impacted by this amended Complementary Law.

The urgency and necessity of approving this law project are evident, as thousands of municipalities have been experiencing a decline in revenues year after year, to the point that many are compromising essential services to the population.

Moreover, given the doubt as to which municipal federal entity taxpayers should pay the ISS under the new legislation, it is imperative to approve this law project swiftly, enabling Brazilian municipalities to benefit from these funds.
--- seg-018baa5ad284a5574bfdaf51 [needs-review] ---
Committees Room, May 08, 2018.
--- seg-24cd0706b8f409bbea748077 [machine-unreviewed] ---
HILDO ROCHA

FEDERAL DEPUTY

JUSTIFICATION

      Violence is one of the main concerns of Brazilians, but despite its gravity, the problem has not been adequately addressed by the public power.

       As a result, in 2014, we were among the twelve most violent countries in the world, with 28.2

===== PAGE 41 [page-98fd79f8b4a6d7106d69facf] =====
--- seg-0db96215c181fa748f837bcc [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                          Tuesday 15 41
--- seg-e9840e8ff09b80436ae79d60 [needs-review] ---
violent deaths per 100,000 inhabitants,1 a figure that rose to 28.6 in 2015 and jumped to 29.7 in 2016.2 The country also ranks as the 7th most violent country in Latin America. And there are no indications of improvement on the horizon. Reducing lethal violence requires, in addition to effective prevention and repression policies, strengthening homicide investigations. As indicated by the research "Where Does Impunity Live?", by the Sou da Paz Institute3, despite targeted investments in some capitals to create specialized homicide delegacies and improve forensic bodies, surveys show weak performance by Brazilian police in solving homicides. In some states, the Public Ministry reports less than 15% of violent deaths, due to the fragility of evidence, the lack of forensic structure, and the excessive delay in conducting police inquiries, among other factors. According to the research mentioned, a significant portion of violent deaths that have been clarified in the country are crimes within domestic contexts between couples or that preceded arrests in flagrante, typically involving close and easier-to-investigate individuals. Many cases involving organized crime often end up stalled in police stations or drag on for years between the police and the state attorney general's office without resolution, fueling impunity and complicating the development of targeted public policies. Not without reason, the Brazilian states that achieved the best rates of reduction in their lethal violence indices were those that implemented qualified prevention projects and physical, technological, scientific, and methodological restructuring actions in their specialized police units for homicide investigation. The more information about the phenomenon, authors, and victims of the intentional homicide, the better the subsidies for programs directed at its containment. Based on this study, we have developed this proposal, which aims to create a National Homicide Clarification Indicator that allows safely measuring the performance of criminal investigations in each federal unit. This indicator aims to demonstrate the proportion of homicide investigations in the Federal Units that result in a criminal action, the outcome of this action, and the existing structure to promote the investigation of lethal crimes. With this, it will be possible to provide transparency and enable social control over the allocation of material and human resources for public security, allowing us to assess whether public managers are prioritizing the investigation of crimes that cause the most suffering to society or if they are allocating existing resources to meet other demands. The creation of the National Homicide Clarification Indicator will enable the setting of goals and the consolidation of best practices in criminal investigation and prosecution, measure the progress achieved in each Federal Unit, and foster the exchange of successful experiences among police officers, experts, and prosecutors, allowing for joint strategic planning among the bodies that make up the security and justice system. As highlighted by the study from the Institute Sou da Paz: the investigation and processing of homicides by the institutions that make up the criminal justice and security system in Brazil is ineffective and inefficient. In 2012, the National Public Ministry Council, in monitoring work of Goal 2 of the National Strategy for Justice and Public Security, pointed to very low rates of homicide clarification in Brazilian states. Of the 43,123 inquiries monitored by the goal and concluded between March 2010 and April 2012, 78% were archived due to the impossibility of reaching the authors, mainly due to the long

In Rio de Janeiro, a study conducted by professors Michel Misse and Joana Vargas of the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro in 2007 found a mere 14% clarification rate for homicides registered between 2000 and 2005, while public security expert Luís Flávio Sapori reported a 15% clarification rate in Belo Horizonte in a 2005 homicide study. In São Paulo, the Sou da Paz Institute published a survey in October 2017 on a representative sample of homicide inquiries, from which 34% resulted in criminal complaints and only 5% were actually tried. As indicated by the study, it is impossible to compare the results of the investigative systems of the states, as there is no national indicator that allows for uniform data collection. Furthermore, the low rates of homicide clarification and excessive delays in case processing are attributed to the predominance of public investments in overt policing, the scarcity of personnel in civil and technical-scientific police, and poor working conditions, which lead to the inadequacy of key technical-expertise procedures, such as the delimitation, isolation, and preservation of crime scenes. In most cases, homicide investigations ultimately rely primarily on witness testimony and have a documentary character. The expertise, fundamental for the production of technical evidence, tends to confirm the criminality, but not point to the authorship, illuminating "what happened, but not who killed." Adding to these deficiencies the limited institutional coordination among the bodies that make up the criminal justice system, the low quality of the criminal procedure instruction for homicide cases is among the drivers fueling impunity in Brazil. The creation of a National Homicide Clarification Indicator composed of data related to the entire investigation and trial process of these crimes, as well as the structure provided for the performance of these activities, will allow assessing how and in what way each government deals with this situation, enabling social control over the prioritization given to homicide investigations.

JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-ed5fdc046bd5d17915856987 [needs-review] ---
As this is of fundamental importance to the Brazilian population and for the moralization of economic activity, this bill aims to improve the fight against corruption and money laundering and ensure the transparency of economic activity, following the trend of Law 8,021 of April 12, 1990, which prohibits the issuance of bearer or negotiable endossable shares by condominium funds; and the issuance of securities and the collection of deposits or applications bearer or negotiable endossable; the project aims to establish an effective obstacle to "off-the-books corporate acts and contracts" and "the use of straw men," ultimately ending clandestinity in business, by introducing a concrete and efficient measure to combat corruption, prevent tax fraud and evasion, and prevent the use of the economic system for the purposes of money laundering, capital laundering, and the financing of organized crime, through the assurance of transparency in economic activity, by subjecting the respective acts and legal transactions to a Notary Public. When submitted to a Notary Public, legal acts and transactions in general will no longer be able to coexist with secrecy, and the record of their occurrence will always be available to the public. With the amendment of Article 44 of the Civil Code, there will be a concrete and effective obstacle to frauds or secrecy in the core of private law entities, especially regarding "off-the-books" acts concerning corporate and constitutive acts of private law entities in general, including their

===== PAGE 45 [page-0b16106caf6e0de5ba987217] =====
--- seg-11db0b98cfd2178944d09bd6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                           Tuesday 15 45
--- seg-cb27bc0ff02434bfca0d9729 [needs-review] ---
modifications and for their own extinction; as well as to the "use of oranges", since in the first case there can be no "slip of paper", as it is formalized by a public deed; and in the second, there is a great obstacle for the defrauder in making the "orange" appear before the Notary Public. And why would the public deed have this power to deter these criminal acts?

(a) The person intending to establish a society will have to be identified and qualified in the presence of the Notary Public;

(b) The Notary Public, in addition to performing the correct and secure identification and legal capacity of the parties, will examine if the parties' will is in accordance with the law and will verify if there is a tax incidence;

(c) The Notary Public is a legal professional, invested with public faith, therefore all acts performed by him are presumed to be true and constitute full proof;

(d) Article 425, paragraph II, of the Civil Procedure Code, provides for the possibility of obtaining a new certificate, in the event of loss of the document, with the same value as the original. The Commercial Board and the Civil Registry of Legal Entities will be required to register the notarial acts referred to in this bill within a maximum of 2 (two) days after the delivery of the complete documentation, with a view to simplifying procedures and de-bureaucratizing. With this, the opening of companies in Brazil will gain a lot in agility, as users will have a skilled public instrument for the constitution, modification, or extinction of the company, drafted by a legal professional with public faith, registered in a fairly short time. On the other hand, the entire population, and particularly low-income individuals, will gain access to a high-quality technical service with extremely reduced costs, given that there will be a 50% deduction in the fees charged for registration of microenterprises and small businesses. The study conducted by the Doing Business of the World Bank attested that the cost of Notarial Services in Brazil is the second lowest cost in the global ranking. The Notary or Public Officer is not exclusive to Brazil; it is present in over 120 (one hundred and twenty) countries members of the UINL – International Union of Latin Notaries, of which Brazil is a signatory, representing 2/3 of the world's population, distributed across five continents, and operating in the economy of 60% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The UINL has representation in over 40 global organizations, such as the UN – United Nations, where it performs investigative and technical advisory tasks for governments worldwide. It is also noted that in various countries with a tradition of Roman-Germanic civil law, such as Brazil, there is an obligation to establish companies and other legal entities through public deeds. We can cite as an example highly developed countries such as Germany, France,

===== PAGE 46 [page-c157ea3c802c9e645bd91b94] =====
--- seg-ae6de96e16fd69fcbe107acc [machine-unreviewed] ---
46 Tuesday, May 15                     DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-9ad2db17257d8b45015e4320 [needs-review] ---
Italy and Spain, which use the notarial system as a means of preventing money laundering and corruption.

Spain stands out for its ease of company registration1, being renowned for the speed and security of establishing these legal entities, and also has a robust cartorial system for preventing money laundering.

Germany is also a country with a strong notarial tradition, and, like Brazil, has constitutional provisions for notarial institutions2. In Germany, the creation and dissolution of companies by public deed is also seen as a significant facilitator of company registration, as parties receive impartial and qualified assistance from a Notary, also appointed through a contest, as in Brazil3.

These are the reasons we will draw upon the numerous and successful European experiences, particularly those of Germany, France, Italy, and Spain, which use Notaries in the fight against corruption, fraud prevention, and tax evasion, and in preventing the economic system from being used for money laundering, capital laundering, and the financing of organized crime.

Another factor that led us to adopt urgent and fundamental measures was that the Laws Nos. 9.613/98, 12.683/2012 and other measures taken by the Government to combat corruption were not able to stop money laundering crimes, thus failing to meet the ancient and, at the same time, current desire, and perhaps despair, of the population to combat crime.

Another advantage of making it mandatory is the high-level legal oversight that Notaries will provide during the company registration process, which will prevent errors in drafting social contracts, their modifications, and the dissolution of companies.

The project brings together the best of both worlds; it facilitates company registration for entrepreneurs pursuing lawful goals while controlling illegal activities carried out by criminals, who often use companies to achieve their shady purposes.

The establishment of companies through private contracts creates a lot of uncertainty and does not meet societal expectations. Regulation through public deeds aims to provide legal security to parties, in addition to preventing corruption and money laundering, effectively contributing to the construction of a fair, swift, and efficient legal system, as exists in many highly developed countries.

Furthermore, it opens the possibility for the public and judicial powers to have effective control over company registrations in a definitive manner, as the Notarial College of Brazil - Federal Council - has a Central Organization for Money Laundering Prevention (OCPLD), saving time and resources.

**Article 1:** This law assigns to the Housing Guarantee Fund (FGHab) the purpose of subsidizing the renegotiation of contracts concluded within the scope of the My House, My Life (PMCMV) program.

**Article 2º O:** Article 20 of Law No. 11,977 of July 7, 2009, is amended to read as follows:

"Article 20. ...

...

III – subsidize the renegotiation of contracts concluded within the scope of the PMCMV in cases defined in its statute."

**Article 3:** This law enters into force on the date of its official publication.

**Justification:**

The My House, My Life (PMCMV) program is one of the most important instruments at the disposal of the federal government to ensure the enjoyment of the right to housing for a significant portion of Brazilians.

However, sometimes the rules of the loans contracted within the PMCMV cannot be met by the beneficiaries due to their precarious economic conditions.

In such situations, it is essential to create a mechanism that ensures the fulfillment of the purposes of this important public policy, a kind of safety valve that guarantees the acquisition of the property by those who cannot effectively meet all the requirements set out in laws and contracts.

The objective of this law project is to create such a mechanism, assigning to the Housing Guarantee Fund (FGHab) an additional purpose: to subsidize the renegotiation of PMCMV contracts.

Given the relevance of this topic, we seek the support of our colleagues to discuss and approve this proposal.

JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-edefea38dc50e711b459a7fb [needs-review] ---
The resocialization of the prison population is a significant challenge to be addressed by the Public Administration. The facts show that the difficulty of reinsertion of those who are in
restraint of liberty into the labor market is a factor that contributes to
recidivism, which ultimately fuels the chronic problems of our criminal
system. In light of this, I propose this present Bill aiming to create workshops in Brazilian prisons for the recovery of ambulances and police vehicles, with the support of the private initiative (workshops, dealers, insurance companies, Senai, for example), and with the Public Power. In this way, in addition to providing inmates with the opportunity to learn new skills that will enable their future reintegration into the labor market, it also allows for the reduction of their term of private deprivation of liberty. This is, therefore, a necessary measure to address the prison chaos that exists in our country, which is why I count on the support of the distinguished colleagues for the approval of this present Bill.

===== PAGE 57 [page-bd3df489834ab905ab43c74d] =====
--- seg-5aa79f70a22a2a4eb43534d5 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                           Tuesday 15 57
--- seg-5a1e286c11d223fce878b8cb [machine-unreviewed] ---

JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-b93621608bdd52efa8eb15a8 [needs-review] ---
The main objective of this proposal is to ensure the freedom of choice for legal entities and natural persons in registering acts provided for in Article 167 of Law 6,015 of December 31, 1973. These
changes, in line with new times, are based on two premises: a) the technological revolution, which enables the digitization and online dissemination of any type of document; and b) the autonomy of individual and legal entities' will, which now have the option to choose where, within the municipality, they wish to register their documents. The guarantee of unrestricted and free access to property registration documents will be provided by the search system whose rules will be regulated by the National Justice Council. This factor will make the search for existing documentation in the thousands of notarial services for property registration in Brazil more agile and efficient. Moreover, the guarantee of freedom of choice in registration services will stimulate the improvement of public services, as these changes introduce a fundamental factor for continuous service enhancement: competitiveness. Through this competitiveness, individuals and companies will no longer be dependent on the service of a single land registry, which can sometimes be of poor quality due to an abstract legal provision. Therefore, this proposal is in line with the society's demands, which seeks high-quality and efficient services, and with the real estate records' own aspirations, as they always strive for excellence in their work.

--- seg-d4e01dd0353817384e3106d1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
62 Tuesday, May 15                          DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                                         2018
--- seg-4a1e4d369e07ec7de73913cb [needs-review] ---
BILL NO. 10,128, 2018
                                                    (Mr. Bacelar)
--- seg-7853c19ecba090a1854cfe1b [needs-review] ---
Amend the Brazilian Traffic Code, established by Law No. 9,503 of September 23, 1997, to provide
for the substitution of privative punishment of liberty with restrictive punishment of rights for crimes
committed while driving motor vehicles.
--- seg-564992ad3c7299083582a04b [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
REFER TO PL-9823/2018.
--- seg-f408d62490a3a4ffd373527a [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-4ae1027144695c59475452bd [machine-unreviewed] ---
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS DECREES:
--- seg-313362332fd7aaab7e823d2b [needs-review] ---
Article 1. This Law adds a new §5 to Article 291 of Law No. 9,503 of September 23, 1997, Brazilian Traffic Code, to provide for the substitution of privative of liberty penalty with restrictive of rights penalty for crimes committed while driving motor vehicles. Article 2. Add the following §5 to Article 291 of Law No. 9,503, of September 23, 1997, Brazilian Traffic Code.

                       "Article 291. ..............................................................................
                       .............................................................................................
                       §5. The substitution provided for in item I of the head of Article 44 of Decree-Law No. 2,848, of
                       December 7, 1940 (Penal Code), subject to the other conditions provided for in items II and III
                       of the head of the aforementioned article, shall only apply in the cases provided for in §3 of
                       Article 302, §2 of Article 303, and §§ 1 and 2 of Article 308, all of this Code, provided that a
                       privative of liberty penalty of not more than five years and six months is applied." (Amendments)

Article 3. This Law shall enter into force one hundred and twenty days after its official publication.
--- seg-09d360b237e0253c3c2fc879 [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-3ee0f45875a79eb311d3c422 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The present proposal aims to prevent the perpetuation of impunity in traffic on Brazilian roads and highways.

In a recent legislative change, the National Congress approved increased penalties for drivers who commit crimes while driving motor vehicles under the influence of alcohol and other drugs, as well as during illegal street races, competitions, or automotive events.

Law No. 13,546 of 2017 was more than worthy in raising penalties for drivers who, in an irresponsible and reckless manner, put the lives of other drivers and pedestrians at risk, causing losses.

===== PAGE 63 [page-5e502781453296d3730911ef] =====
--- seg-7e58b85829bf31c578e77296 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                           Tuesday, May 15, 63
--- seg-161e3148b2a87119fb82ca01 [needs-review] ---
irreparable harm to entire families. Thus, by amending Articles 302, 303, and 308 of the Traffic Code, the aforementioned law increased the penalties of privative freedom for the respective criminal types. However, even though we have stiffer penalties for traffic offenses committed under conditions of intoxication, drug use, or illegal racing, the criminal legislation, specifically Article 44 of the Penal Code, provides for the possibility of substituting the privative of liberty penalty with a so-called restrictive of rights penalty in all these situations. The forms of restrictive penalties are: pecuniary compensation; community service or service to public entities; temporary interdiction of rights; and weekend limitation. In other words, even if the result of the reckless driving is a serious bodily injury or even a homicide, regardless of the sentence imposed in the specific case, the driver may leave the process without spending a single day in prison. We are not against the possibility of replacing prison sentences for traffic crimes. However, this possibility cannot be considered independently of the penalty applied in the specific case, as provided by the current wording of Article 44, Item I, of the Penal Code, for negligent crimes. We understand that, as in felonious crimes, the possibility of applying substitution of penalty in traffic crimes committed under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or without authorization, should consider the penalty applied in each case and have a limit. Therefore, we propose that – in the cases provided for in §3 of art. 302 (homicide while driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs); §2 of art. 303 (bodily injury while driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs); and in §§ 1 and 2 of art. 308 (bodily injury and homicide in a motor race, contest, or competition without authorization) – the substitution of the privative of liberty penalty for a restrictive of rights penalty is only allowed when the applied penalty is not superior to five years and six months. Not only in cases of homicide, but also in cases of bodily injury, the driver who consumes alcohol or another intoxicating substance acts in a negligent and condemnable manner, taking the risk of causing traffic accidents with victims. Thus, this bill aims to contribute to a stricter and more effective legislation that can change the behavior of these drivers. The sense of impunity, so prevalent in various segments of Brazilian society, cannot prosper, especially when we are talking directly about actions with such high potential harm. Such a feeling leads many drivers to disregard the damage they may cause with reckless driving. This situation needs to be combated. In light of the above, we request the support of our esteemed colleagues for the approval of this proposal. Session Room, April 25, 2018.

Article 1. This Law amends Article 3, Section VII, of Law No. 8,009 of March 29, 1990, to exempt, from the rule providing for the pledge of family property for obligations arising from a surety given in a lease contract, the case where the surety is a woman who is the sole provider for a family unit.
--- seg-462ae6885dcd1d80e5a89942 [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-abe8f148691e85d5a85d4a21 [needs-review] ---
"Article 3 .........................................................................................
                       ..................................................................................................... " VII - by obligation arising from a surety granted in a lease contract, subject to the hypothesis
   where the guarantor is a breadwinning woman supporting a family unit. (Amendments)

--- seg-01ada9d13b94b4131d97fb44 [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-0cea86fba3a0f13dffd7566e [machine-unreviewed] ---
The possibility of garnishing the family property, in the case of an obligation arising from a surety given in a lease contract, currently provided for in Article 3, paragraph VII, of Law No. 8,009 of March 29, 1990, has been heavily criticized by legal scholars and, in some cases, by national case law.
--- seg-cd9a609adf6a48a4330bf756 [machine-unreviewed] ---
A significant part of this criticism lies in the fact that the tenant's property – which is an active party in the contract – can be the recipient of legal protection through the inalienability of family property. However, the guarantor's property, which only has an auxiliary function in the contract, does not enjoy such protection.
--- seg-8662b6ae209972ff96073857 [machine-unreviewed] ---
In order to correct this inequality, but also taking into account the widespread use of the bail bond system in the real estate rental market, we now propose a measure that aims to exempt from the rule of penhorability (garnishment) of the sole residential property of the guarantor in a lease agreement, individuals who find themselves in situations that require a differentiated treatment by the legislator.

===== PAGE 65 [page-77de96482a6ac09fce726949] =====

May 2018                       CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                       Tuesday, May 15, 65
--- seg-4901387a0a90bb6f5a86ad55 [machine-unreviewed] ---
In this vein, we understand it to be plausible and important to exclude women who are the primary breadwinners for a family from the expropriation of family property due to an obligation arising from a guaranty provided in a lease agreement.
--- seg-3c0ec7a7dea3a3a70422ba45 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The importance of the proposal becomes evident. It is not reasonable to remove women responsible for the sustenance of a household, along with their families, from their residence due to the non-fulfillment of obligations by the tenant.
--- seg-1a5abca23f6ef4faf0e1e58e [machine-unreviewed] ---
In fact, when considering the guarantee of hygiene in a lease agreement versus the preservation of the dignity of those who most need a normative framework to protect them, there is no doubt that the latter option should prevail.
--- seg-28636caacd7d7dfce33e4d58 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Certain that this draft law will provide an important guarantee for women who present vulnerabilities requiring protection, we count on the necessary support for its approval.

Revokes §8 of Article 57 of Law n.º 213/91 - Social Security Benefits Law.
--- seg-25209851bd9a1e2c25b03f6a [machine-unreviewed] ---
MEMORANDUM:
TO:
COMMITTEES ON:
SOCIAL SECURITY AND FAMILY, AND
CONSTITUTION, JUSTICE, AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 RICD)
--- seg-ceb484bd6132ef0351f703f1 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposal Subject to Final Review by the Committees - Art. 24 II
--- seg-c380af44928e7f380137e181 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The National Congress decrees:
--- seg-5f6d6bd7b68317de65066d2b [needs-review] ---
Article 1. §8 of Article 57 of Law No. 213/91 is hereby repealed, which was included by Law No. 9.732 of December 11, 1998.
--- seg-e32f1b8262a275588b3109ca [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-ab1f355437195d075cabd03f [needs-review] ---
Section 8 of Article 57 of Law No. 213/91, as included by Law No. 9.732 of December 11, 1998, stipulates that:
--- seg-86d81ea835046c40cbfa381f [machine-unreviewed] ---
§ 8. The provisions of Article 46 apply to a retiree under the terms of this article who continues to engage in or perform activities or operations that expose them to the harmful agents listed in the relationship referred to in Article 58 of this Law.
--- seg-2bd96f73d28044440955e653 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 57, as mentioned, deals with special pensions for workers exposed to conditions harmful to health or physical integrity. On the other hand, Article 46, to which the provision refers, provides, when dealing with invalidity pensions:
--- seg-90bdfa5a76d9b9c3556e2ceb [machine-unreviewed] ---
Art. 46. A retired person due to invalidity who voluntarily returns to work will have their retirement automatically canceled as of the date of return.
--- seg-17645bd453149cdc759b9362 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Thus, the paragraph to be revoked is equating a special, contributive, and programmable retirement to a disability retirement that has a security and unpredictable nature, reserved for those who are no longer able to work.
--- seg-c2ec4147a40e6392b203af74 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The fact is that retirement for workers exposed to harmful conditions is only granted to those who meet all the requirements, such as contribution time and proof of special labor. Once the requirements are met, the insured retires and should be able to decide whether or not to remove the risk condition. If the special worker, already retired, chooses to stay in the job, under the guarantee of a social security benefit, they should not be prohibited. There are several reasons for this:
--- seg-4514bf0a8073925550910bd9 [needs-review] ---
a) Special retirement is defined by the Federal Constitution (Article 201, §1) and there is no provision for mandatory removal in the article, and ordinary law cannot innovate or restrict the constitutional benefit so significantly.

===== PAGE 67 [page-c354ac99b907a7ecaa1cb6c1] =====
--- seg-5b0526d4498bf85ef9b1655c [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                          Tuesday, May 15, 67
--- seg-57e1f8ef8690b51f11772822 [needs-review] ---
b) TRF4 declared the unconstitutionality of the provision in the Constitutional Challenge Incident
no. 5001401-77.2012.404.0000, Rel. Fed. Judge Ricardo Teixeira do Valle Pereira,
decided on 05/24/2012;
--- seg-6cf8527d912fafe020609537 [machine-unreviewed] ---
c) The retirement of the disabled and the retirement by sum 85/95 do not require removal from work and, in a certain way, are equalizations to special retirement, including in the calculation format (without a social security factor). On the other hand, the insured who converts their special time into common and reaches the points of the sum 85/95, would be benefited compared to the insured who does not, since one can remain in work and the other cannot, violating the principles of equality and equality.
--- seg-463f7ef2a54875bff335eedb [machine-unreviewed] ---
d) It is interesting for the social security system that a special retiree continues to work, if they choose,
as they will be contributing to social security even after retirement.
--- seg-fc88d3f8eb989bb33ed7f9ce [machine-unreviewed] ---
e) It is in society's interest that professionals with experience and high specialization be able to
maintain their jobs, contributing to good service delivery and social well-being in the communities they serve;
--- seg-cc1716a1270ca4d26622f5ce [needs-review] ---
f) It is not possible to force a non-invalid, specialized worker to give up their food and salary benefits; on the contrary, the right of the insured to choose to remain in the workplace, if they so wish, must be guaranteed, valuing the principle of individual freedom, which in this case does not harm, but rather points in the same direction as the collective interest.
--- seg-323bb428533a14155db1aa96 [machine-unreviewed] ---
g) The Federal Supreme Court, when ruling on issue 888 in general repercussion, allowed public servants to
receive the retention bonus for special retirees, that is, the continuation of special labor.
It would be discriminatory to deny the same to private sector workers.
--- seg-d50a44b31ad0f1db1db78f4f [machine-unreviewed] ---
h) The repeal of the provision will bring greater legal security and reduce the number of court actions, as it will be clear, by legal means and not judicially, that staying in the special labor is lawful.
--- seg-704e868314c94798b6061f9f [machine-unreviewed] ---
In light of these arguments, we request that honorable colleagues approve this matter.

Add devices to Law No. 13.105 of March 16, 2015, and provides for other measures.
--- seg-99b6c4289f4e66a85e48c3ef [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
REFER TO PL-10010/2018.
--- seg-677bbe7af24d92acec91892f [needs-review] ---

Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-1b60ee21bcb0b04ab0c34eed [machine-unreviewed] ---
The National Congress decrees:
--- seg-4622d9a3c620eef21833c479 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 1. Article 554 of Law 13.105 of March 16, 2015, is amended by adding paragraph 4:

       Article 554. ...
       §4. In the case of collective possession action, as provided for in paragraph 1, no removal
       may be carried out without ensuring a new, adequate, and dignified place to live, under the
       penalty of constituting a grave violation of human rights.
       Article 2. This law takes effect upon publication.
--- seg-fdd6be1ed120a1223cb1404c [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-72a2bad2bad45403f7ec9b0b [needs-review] ---
The right to dignified housing is a social right explicitly established in Article 6 of the Federal Constitution, necessitating not only a sector-specific public policy for social housing but also the obligation to prevent people displaced by various factors from being compulsorily reduced to homelessness.

Furthermore, Brazil has internationally committed to protecting the right to dignified housing at the United Nations Conference on Human Settlements (Habitat). The Conference recommends to countries that they prohibit the legal practice of forced collective evictions, which involves the involuntary relocation of people, families, and groups from their places or communities, exacerbating the housing problem, intensifying conflicts, and worsening existing social inequality in our country.

Daily in Brazil, we witness situations where communities face repossession of areas they have occupied for a long time, with all the violence of the state apparatus. The resistance of these people is, of course, due to the fact that they have no other place to go. The bill aims to ensure cooperation from all public entities to guarantee that no forced collective removal takes place before ensuring that the housing right of those families is preserved. In other words, in the preparatory tasks for a collective eviction, there must also be a guarantee of dignified housing for relocation, and only after this verification can a repossession order issued by the judiciary be carried out without violating the Federal Constitution and International Human Rights Treaties.

Therefore, given the urgent humanitarian nature of the approved bill, we call on our esteemed colleagues to pass it.

Amend the Law No. 7,565 of December 19, 1986 - Brazilian Aeronautics Code, to prohibit the charging for advance seat selection under the conditions specified.
--- seg-badf2496f5a3b27df850e648 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
REFER TO PL-4262/2012.
--- seg-d4716ff00c3b5bf58c7ee356 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-538aadc579e3868c2b1fdeac [machine-unreviewed] ---
The National Congress decrees:
--- seg-4141ab4f5e3148db15cf9894 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 1. Law No. 7,565 of December 19, 1986, shall be in force with the following additional article:
--- seg-a391f036fc95c136e1184d6c [needs-review] ---
“Article 233-A. The consumer is guaranteed the right to advance and free marking of a seat on a flight operated within Brazilian territory, with the airline being prohibited from charging any additional value.

(Unique Paragraph) The prohibition provided for in the heading does not apply in the case of a seat that confers on the consumer a special advantage, not provided for in standard seats.” (NR)

Article 2. This law enters into force on the date of its publication.
--- seg-bdef77448c7f2757058b4e65 [needs-review] ---
JUSTIFICATION

As members of the legislative body, we have witnessed the continuous decline in the quality of passenger air transport services in our country. Since the issuance by the National Civil Aviation Agency (ANAC) of Resolution No. 400/2016, Brazilian consumers have had their basic rights violated and have been subjected to increasing prices for air travel tickets and related services, such as bag check-in.

Recently, airlines have announced that they will begin charging for seat selection, even for seats that do not provide any particular advantage to the passenger, such as larger seats, better-located seats, or seats with more legroom.

This is an abusive and unreasonable practice, directly contradicting fundamental principles of consumer law, including the prohibition of unjustified price increases for services.

The practice is particularly harmful when considering individuals who wish to travel together or need to sit next to each other, or those who, for other reasons, have a preference for aisle or window seats.

We believe that this House should actively work to prevent the erosion of consumer rights in passenger air transport services.

For the reasons stated, I request the support of my colleagues to thoroughly discuss this issue and promptly approve this proposal.

--- seg-dc09aeb7fc84b83a00c1ceda [machine-unreviewed] ---
Most Excellent Sir President of the Republic,
--- seg-5fddda9424c647ba714840ba [needs-review] ---
We submit for Your Excellency's high consideration a draft law that amends Article 12 of Decree-Law No. 1,593 of December 21, 1977, which regulates cigarettes intended for export.

Brazilian cigarette exports are governed by Decree-Law No. 1,593 of 1977.

===== PAGE 73 [page-a2f850b4858c480388a7d6a5] =====
--- seg-7d59692ef41105bf8ecff3cf [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                               HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                  Tuesday, May 15, 73
--- seg-dc9bf52602aeae2ed8e49e36 [needs-review] ---
The objective of this legislation is to prevent these products from being irregularly directed to the Brazilian market. For that, the law stipulates that specific markings must be on the packaging to identify the products as exports and thus prevent their destination to Brazil. However, these requirements apply to packages containing twenty cigarettes, as implied by the reading of the device:

"Article 12." Cigarettes intended for export cannot be sold or displayed for sale in the country and must be marked on each pack or 20-unit holder with the equipment referred to in Article 27 of Law No. 11,488 of June 15, 2007, using codes that enable identification of their legitimate origin and prevent the clandestine introduction of these products into the national territory.

Therefore, it is implicit that the export limitation applies only to packages containing twenty cigarettes. While the twenty-cigarette pack is the standard configuration for the domestic market, certain foreign markets practice distinct packaging, such as packs containing 18 (United Kingdom), 25 (Australia), or even 40 cigarettes (China), found in some countries. It is thus noted that Brazilian legislation imposes a barrier to access to markets that demand packages of quantities distinct from the national standard. It is clear that the main objective of the current legal device is not to limit the type of packaging
of the exported cigarettes, but simply to prohibit the display for sale in Brazil of products
destined for export and to require that the packaging presented to the consumer be properly
marked to identify its origin. The reference to the pack or wallet of twenty cigarettes serves here to delimit the type of packaging to be marked, considering the existing standard for Brazil. That
because the same marking was used for the fiscal control of cigarettes intended for the domestic market, which, in fact, is done for packages containing twenty units. However, this limitation had the undesirable effect of restricting the packaging presentation to foreign consumers to that of twenty cigarettes, preventing export to countries with different standards. It is then suggested to amend the legislation to allow cigarettes to be exported in packages of different formats from the Brazilian standard, while still prohibiting their sale in the domestic market and requiring marking of the consumer presentation packages. Preserve central measures to combat the diversion or irregular return of these goods to the internal market. Given the above, the following text proposal is presented to reformulate the opening of Article 12 of Law Decree No. 1.593 of 1977:

            Art. 12. Cigarettes intended for export may not be sold or displayed for sale in the country and must be marked on each pack, wallet, or other presentation format to the consumer with equipment as provided in Article 27 of Law No. 11,488 of June 15, 2007, using codes that enable identification of their legitimate origin and prevent the clandestine introduction of these products into the national territory.
--- seg-fa0377ea2e23462d49527b0f [needs-review] ---
These are, Mr. President, the reasons that lead us to propose to Your Excellency the attached draft bill.

JUSTIFICATION
           The agonizing review of the harms attributed by the Collor government to numerous civil servants and employees of agencies and entities in the public administration was marked by a series of comings and goings. Established by former President Itamar Franco, the process was interrupted in the subsequent period because there was no disposition, during the eight long years that the country was under the administration of Fernando Henrique Cardoso, to redress the grave injustices caused by the temerity of the removed official. Due to this circumstance, several individual cases ended in a truly tragic manner, as numerous potential beneficiaries of the amnesty sought by Law No. 8,878 of 1994 passed away before obtaining from the public authorities the proof that they had been affected by unjust measures. Since the law contained no provisions to address situations like this, the dependents of these individuals continued to endure the torment they experienced in life.

Amend the Law Decree No. 2,848, of December 7, 1940 - Brazilian Penal Code, to classify the act of photographing, filming, or recording, by any means, in a public or accessible place, the intimate parts of the victim, without their consent.
--- seg-937fd5736407460209efed1a [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
REFER TO PL-9717/2018.
--- seg-1dac9cc1a8e430b4423c1c33 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-da670c1012f95d56d85ba704 [machine-unreviewed] ---
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS DECREES:
--- seg-59e60544461c551093043f56 [needs-review] ---
Article 1. This Law amends Law No. 2,848 of December 7, 1940 – the Brazilian Penal Code, to classify the act of photographing, filming, or recording, by any means, in a public or accessible place, the intimate parts of the victim without their consent. Article 2. Title VI of Law Decree No. 2,848 of December 7, 1940, is hereby amended to add the following Chapter III-A:
--- seg-6cf65af99b39a730422da8b9 [needs-review] ---
"Chapter III-A
                             OF CRIMES AGAINST PERSONAL DIGNITY"
--- seg-8ccd5790cceecf996aae00ec [needs-review] ---
Article 222-A. Photographing, filming, or recording, by any means, the intimate parts of the victim without their consent to satisfy one's own or another's lust. Penalty: imprisonment, from six months to two years, or fine. Single paragraph. Those who make available, transmit, distribute, publish, or disseminate, by any means, including through an information system or telematics, a photograph, video, or any other record containing the content mentioned in the first paragraph, shall be subject to the same penalties.

Article 3. This Law shall enter into force on the date of its publication.
--- seg-d6698b6268e3401032ccf4a9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-c367535740f7e599593f0cd8 [needs-review] ---
There has been an increase in Brazil in the practice of photographing or filming intimate parts of people in public or accessible places, with these images subsequently shared on social networks or WhatsApp groups. This behavior flagrantly violates the sense of dignity of individuals, who may eventually come across records of their intimate parts captured without their knowledge. In cases where the victim observes or is warned by others that they have been covertly filmed or photographed in such a situation, and if they are able to retain or identify the perpetrator, they are typically punished under Article 61 of the Penal Contravenion Law (with only a fine) for the offense of "outraging public decency." Internationally, the practice has come to be known as upskirting, which refers to the fetish where an individual derives pleasure from looking up skirts and dresses, at the expense of privacy and consent.

===== PAGE 78 [page-c8022a80abe23b1aa7811a7c] =====
--- seg-f01bcc5852efd68da7cd444e [machine-unreviewed] ---
78 Tuesday, May 15                  DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-73cfeeb5c4ffc2337d8c73ae [needs-review] ---
privacy of their victims. It is not uncommon for such images to be made freely available or even sold online, accompanied by photos of the person's face that was disrespected. As the incidence of these cases increased, the Japanese market regulator for the sale of smartphones issued a regulation in 2015 that prevents the sound of the camera shutter of these electronic devices from being muted, as a way to prevent upskirting. In another line, which is being adopted by an increasingly number of countries, Scotland, Australia, and New Zealand, for example, have criminalized the practice. It is absolutely necessary that this nefarious conduct also be classified as a sexual crime in Brazil, and not merely as harassment, which is incapable of generating any deterrent effect.
--- seg-235bfb9a6c0d0b9f987a846f [needs-review] ---
It is with this intent that I present this Draft Law, and in view of the importance of the proposed legislative measure, I request the support of the distinguished Members for its approval.

JUSTIFICATION

Authorized by Law No. 8,029 of April 12, 1990, and established by Decree No. 100 of April 6, 1991, the National Health Foundation (FUNASA) is an agency under the Ministry of Health responsible for promoting basic sanitation for the population. For purely political reasons, FUNASA established programs to serve municipalities with up to 50 (fifty) thousand inhabitants, which makes it difficult for municipalities with a population not much larger than that determined by the Foundation to access basic sanitation. In this regard, following the suggestion of Mayor Zelito Tringuele, I present this bill, which aims to enable FUNASA to prioritize municipalities with up to 60 (sixty) thousand inhabitants. It's worth noting that in the state of Rio de Janeiro, this measure will only benefit three municipalities, namely Cachoeiras de Macacu, Guapimirim, and Rio Bonito. Both are in the range between 50 and 60 thousand.

--- seg-2e90036c5825939d63c32f6e [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-6fc7270c6dc21e9e9b528e79 [needs-review] ---
Traffic violence has reached alarming levels in Brazil. One person dies
on public roads every twelve minutes, and the number of injured is even much higher, reaching ten times as many. In an attempt to combat this critical situation, the Brazilian Traffic Code establishes a list of
equipment considered mandatory for vehicles in circulation in the country, always focusing on
safety. We understand, however, that this list can be improved by including two devices that we believe are essential to achieving the goal of reducing traffic accident victims. The first of these devices is the recorder of data relating to the vehicle's movement - in English, this device is called an Event Data Recorder, or simply EDR. Popularly known as a black box, this equipment is fundamental for forensic activity and traffic accident investigations, as it allows the recovery of important vehicle data, such as the speed at the moment of a collision or the identification of any potential mechanical or electronic failure. This facilitates the investigative work, allowing to reconstruct the dynamics of the event and, thus, establish the cause of the accident. In addition to holding accountable those at fault, understanding the determining causes and contributing factors of traffic accidents allows traffic managers to implement prevention programs for future events. Thus, the data extracted from the recording devices will also serve to propose strategies to reduce the alarming accident rates, such as the development of preventive campaigns, driver education, advancements in vehicular and road safety, among others. The installation of this device is extremely simple, and the increase in the selling price of the vehicle will be small, as all vehicles equipped with airbags (an optional equipment already listed in Article 105, Paragraph VII of the CTB) already have a control module (on-board computer) that measures the vehicle's deceleration and decides if it is an accident that requires the activation of the airbag. Thus,
when activating the bag, various information can be recorded in the memory of the control module, such as:
speed at the moment of impact and in the immediately preceding seconds, the force of the impact, whether the
seatbelt was fastened, whether the brake was applied, whether the anti-lock brake system (ABS) activated, and
even identifying mechanical defects in the vehicle.

===== PAGE 86 [page-bb721fcc72624a96bdf69f4d] =====
--- seg-8251cf603cd7344b1d9c88e4 [machine-unreviewed] ---
86 Tuesday, May 15                  DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-f5914a3b5d06447050604dda [needs-review] ---
In practice, the accident data recorder is no more than a memory space within the airbag module where software collects and records information from various electronic sensors available. The data obtained by the data recorder is very useful for the manufacturers themselves for their protection and defense in case of lawsuits for vehicle failures, as well as for collecting data for product development. In Brazil, some vehicles with this device are already in circulation, for example, the GM/Onix, the country's best-selling car in 2017. It is pertinent to remember that we are in the Decade of Action for Safe Mobility (2011-2020), during which governments worldwide, including Brazil, are committed to taking new measures to prevent and reduce the severity of traffic accidents. The improvement of the investigation process and subsequent accountability of those responsible is one of these measures, both to enhance the effectiveness in punishing traffic offenders and criminals, and to assist in the implementation of preventive actions. This thus demonstrates the importance and feasibility of demanding that all vehicles leave the factory with this device. Furthermore, manufacturers must provide decoded data in a format that can be easily read and analyzed by the police authority in charge of investigating the accident. Another important device to enhance the safety of occupants in school buses and public collective transportation vehicles is the one that prevents these vehicles from moving with the doors open. Although it may seem absurd, it is not difficult to observe buses and minibuses traveling with doors open, under the pretext of cooling the vehicle's internal temperature and providing greater comfort to passengers. There are still cases where vehicles move with doors open due to overcrowding. In fact, situations like these put the lives and physical integrity of the passengers at risk. It is not rare for accidents to occur under these conditions, especially in urban traffic, including fatalities or permanent injuries. The proposal, therefore, aims to eliminate the possibility of a driver neglecting the safety of the passengers, requiring the installation of a device that prevents the vehicle from moving with the doors open. However, since current vehicles will not be required to install this device and considering that it can be tampered with later, it will be necessary to provide a penalty for the driver of a vehicle that travels with doors open, putting the safety of passengers at risk. It is worth remembering that in most cases, this public transport is carried out with people standing up, without using the seatbelt, which increases the risk of accidents. As the behavior of driving with doors open can encompass any vehicle, we differentiate public transportation of passengers and school bus transportation from other vehicles, with the former being more severe. In light of the above, we request the support of the distinguished Senators so that this proposal may be approved and that we may provide greater security for traffic on Brazilian roads.

JUSTIFICATION

      The expiration date of medications is essential information, and its inclusion on the packaging is mandatory. The use of treatments past their expiration date may pose a greater risk of adverse effects and, primarily, of reduced effectiveness. However, studies have questioned the expiration dates reported by the industry, suggesting that medications could generally be used for periods longer than shown on the packaging. A study by the University of California, for example, analyzed a stock of medications stored for decades, some of them 30 to 40 years past their expiration date. The result was surprising. Twelve of the fourteen compounds evaluated remained as potent
      as when they were manufactured1. Another study, conducted in 2006, examined 122 different expired medications, with an average expiration date of over four years. Two-thirds of these remained stable
      in every test conducted. Addressing this issue has the potential to generate significant savings. The U.S. Department of Defense, in partnership with the FDA, created a program to manage the shelf life of its vast stockpile of disaster reserve medications2. The extension project's deadline led to a savings of two billion dollars in 2016 alone that would have been wasted through the destruction of still-effective medications. In Brazil, pharmaceutical manufacturers are currently responsible for
      providing the permitted use period for drugs, but the choice of the deadline does not always follow scientific criteria. The pharmaceutical industry tends to opt for placing a short deadline to
      avoid future questions about effectiveness. The expiration and early disposal of
--- seg-b1d427c9b98d3e6b5a0bcf76 [needs-review] ---
1. The Myth of Drug Expiration Dates. On: https://www.propublica.org/article/the-myth-of-drug-expiration-dates
2. Expiration Dating Extension. U.S. Food & Drug Administration. On: https://www.fda.gov/EmergencyPreparedness/Counterterrorism/MedicalCountermeasures/MCMLegalRegulatoryandPolicyFramew/ucm411446.htm

===== PAGE 96 [page-3bbd6682dfd3176670d7e751] =====
--- seg-57c9c3a7b49c5855ef755df2 [machine-unreviewed] ---
96 Tuesday, May 15                  DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-7692abc469ff333bcc29150f [machine-unreviewed] ---
medicaments, leading to new purchases, ends up being beneficial for the manufacturers as well.
--- seg-f01de11226e6e25916847289 [machine-unreviewed] ---
It is important to note that disposing of expired but still effective medications in the trash creates two problems. Firstly, it results in losses for citizens, healthcare institutions, and the unique healthcare system, as they have to pay for the same product again. Secondly, this disposal is a serious environmental issue, as it is often handled by the regular urban waste or sewage collection system. These substances, many of which are dangerous, are then released into the environment, contaminating water and animals.
--- seg-d3eb36fc80d75ab689e9b6f4 [needs-review] ---

Additionally, the pharmaceutical industry is now required to inform, during the registration of medications, what scientific criteria were used to define the validity period.

Amend the Law No. 8,080 of September 19, 1990, to establish transparency in waiting lists for consultations, examinations, and treatments, and to disclose clinical protocols or therapeutic guidelines for diseases used in establishments providing services to the SUS.
--- seg-859e0c1443454bcec2709cd6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
REFER TO PL-5170/2013.
--- seg-e5bd923727f8e50acb3dd7c3 [needs-review] ---
