Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-735cacd28197952a7fd4f66f [machine-unreviewed] ---
The National Congress decrees:
--- seg-d4bd6bd8b455544101758f34 [needs-review] ---
Article 1: This law amends Law No. 8,080 of September 19, 1990, to establish transparency in waitlists for consultations, examinations, and treatments, and to disclose clinical protocols or therapeutic guidelines for diseases used in facilities providing services to the National Health System (SUS).

Article 2º O: In addition to Article 7 of Law No. 8,080 of September 19, 1990, a new unique paragraph is added:

"Article 7: ...

Unique Paragraph: The right to information for users of the National Health System includes the clear and easily accessible disclosure, including electronically, of waitlists for consultations, examinations, or treatments within the National Health System."

Article 3º O: In addition to Article 19-Q of Law No. 8,080 of September 19, 1990, a new paragraph is added:

"Article 19-Q: ...

§ 3º O: Clinical protocols or therapeutic guidelines for diseases used in health facilities providing services to the SUS shall be disclosed on their electronic website, in accordance with regulations, and any deviations from national standardization should be justified."

Article 4: This law shall enter into force one hundred and eighty days after its publication.

**Justification:**

The National Health System (SUS) was a significant achievement for the Brazilian population, becoming the world's largest universal health care system. However, inequality in access to its services remains one of its biggest challenges.

There have been frequent reports from SUS users having to wait lengthy periods for examinations or surgeries. In some cases, these waits can last for months.

===== PAGE 98 [page-e951bfa3defc052ac15ba3c8] =====
--- seg-0bfb14099a74a721d8c423aa [machine-unreviewed] ---

--- seg-a41c8f1b040fcebac6e99e42 [needs-review] ---
several years1. These patients suffer greatly from this situation, often going through the anguish of waiting for a phone call confirming the date of a treatment. Sometimes, this waiting can lead to worsening of the clinical condition, preventing surgery or even resulting in death. At a public hearing of the Special Commission aimed at studying the process of innovation and technological incorporation in the health production complex in Brazil and around the world (CETECSAU), the guest Tiago Farina Matos cited the importance of increasing the transparency of waiting lists for treatments in the SUS (Brazilian Public Health System) to allow patients some ability to plan and have an idea of how long the procedure will take. Another problem that harms SUS users is the difference in therapeutic approach among its different units. Law No. 12,401 of April 28, 2011, included in the organic law of health provisions regarding clinical protocols and therapeutic guidelines, types of guides for the treatment of diseases, taking into account scientific evidence. The protocols and guidelines are of great importance so that patients receive recognized effective treatments, and that SUS users receive good care in all locations. However, health facilities in Brazil that serve SUS patients may have their own protocols, developed by their professionals. This can lead to
       significant differences between hospitals, which is not ideal. In addition, there is little transparency in the disclosure of these protocols, making it difficult for control agencies and users of the public system to monitor. This bill aims to establish the mandatory disclosure of waitlists for tests, consultations, and treatments, as well as create transparency in clinical protocols and therapeutic guidelines. We request the support of our esteemed colleagues in the legislature to approve this bill to enhance transparency in the SUS, facilitating oversight and social control. Session Room, on May 04, 2018.

Amend the Law Decree No. 2,848 of December 7, 1940 - Penal Code, to provide for the crime of illicit enrichment committed by a public official.
--- seg-3aa854652f32458d3bd0f3c3 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
REFER TO PL-5363/2005.
--- seg-d2d53898a4982cd60eb37aed [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-3ce3de4b514015bbaac7894a [machine-unreviewed] ---
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS DECREES:
--- seg-a1706dd0b169e53bc1db4d9e [needs-review] ---
Article 1. This Law amends Law No. 2,848 of December 7, 1940 - the Penal Code, to establish as a crime
the illicit enrichment committed by a public official when the public official has under his or her control,
possession, and ownership, on a non-occasional basis, assets, rights, or values whose value is incompatible
with their revenues obtained due to their position, employment, or public function.
--- seg-b6368a3afc3e13ede68f0516 [needs-review] ---
Art. 2º Add article 312-A to Law Decree No. 2.848 of December 7, 1940 - Penal Code, with the
following text:
     Illicit Enrichment
     Art. 312-A. To have under one's control, possession, or ownership, on a non-occasional basis, goods,
     rights, or values whose value is incompatible with the revenues obtained, due to one's office,
     employment, or public function:
     Penalty – imprisonment, from 4 (four) to 8 (eight) years, and a fine.
     § 1. The same penalty applies if there is a discharge or extinction of the agent's debts, even
     by a third party.
     § 2. The penalties shall be increased by one-half if the ownership or possession of the goods and
     values is fraudulently attributed to third parties.
--- seg-94aee81946997775c2ea2051 [needs-review] ---
Art. 3. This Law shall enter into force on the date of its publication.
--- seg-719cbe362c8cf3ba97d3e735 [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-1e8cb108419a9c49f15b6e3d [needs-review] ---
The illicit enrichment of a public official is indirect evidence of corruption and related crimes, and particularly in Brazil, it has been reported almost daily by the media. In light of this well-known fact, we propose to present this bill to consider as a crime under the Penal Code the illicit enrichment of a public official.

Therefore, we propose to criminalize having a public official under their domain, possession, or ownership in a non-occasional manner of goods, rights, or values whose value is incompatible with their earnings obtained due to their position, employment, or public function. Similarly, it is intended to punish with the same penalty if

===== PAGE 100 [page-80500449b20bc087cd516cc7] =====
--- seg-ddd8b0bd71958ab7a525b68f [machine-unreviewed] ---
100 Tuesday, May 15                                     DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                                         2018
--- seg-b32ff3b007bcffd51080dec3 [needs-review] ---
There is amortization or extinction of public servant debt, or that which is equivalent to him, including by a third party. To that end, it is proposed that the penalty of imprisonment, from four to eight years, and a fine be applied, which can be increased by half if it is proven that the ownership or possession of the goods and values was fraudulently attributed to third parties, a practice known as the use of "front men." In this regard, it is important to highlight that the United Nations Convention against Corruption, internalized by Brazil, "exorts States Parties to criminalize in their legal systems the crime of illicit enrichment, defined as a significant increase in the wealth of a public official resulting from income that cannot be reasonably justified by him or her." In the administrative sphere, behaviors that give rise to the illicit enrichment of a public official are outlined in Law No. 8.429/1992, which "establishes the sanctions applicable to public agents in cases of illicit enrichment during the exercise of a mandate, position, employment, or function in direct, indirect, or foundational public administration, and provides other measures." We can refer to this as another legislative mechanism to combat corruption, particularly within governmental institutions that inevitably cause harm to the treasury and society. The illicit enrichment of the public official is presumed when the public official manifests signs suggestive of administrative improbity, a fact arising from the flagrantly incompatible patrimonial increase with the corresponding remuneration. This is as described in Article 9 of Law No. 429/92:
          “Article 9. Administrative improbity consists in obtaining any type of illegal patrimonial advantage
          through the exercise of a position, mandate, function, employment, or activity in the entities
          mentioned in Article 1 of this law, and specifically:
          .................................................................................................................... VII - Acquiring, for oneself or for another, in the exercise of a public office, post, employment, or function,
          property of any nature whose value is disproportionate to the growth of the patrimony or to the income of
          the public official;”
--- seg-086862103e2de7a5b3748ccf [needs-review] ---
In turn, the disproportionate asset cannot be considered evidence of illicit enrichment that is impossible to prove otherwise, although it allows for a legal presumption. It is inferred that disproportionate assets to income or the normal patrimonial evolution of a public official, acquired during the performance of their duties, represent the acquisition of an undue advantage due to that performance (art. 9 caput) and, therefore, constitute an act of improbity. Of course, the server will always be able to prove the legitimacy of the increase in assets, such as an inheritance, or a prize, or a lawful activity outside of business hours. The configuration of this type of act of administrative improbity is subject to sanctions such as loss of public office, suspension of political rights, payment of civil fines, prohibition from contracting with the public sector, etc. (Article 12, paragraph I1), all of them applicable by the Judiciary. In turn, it will be up to the Administration
to apply, based on the Statute of Civil Servants of the Union, the penalty of dismissal (art.
132, item IV). A very practical example of this situation would be in the case of a server whose remuneration is in the order of R$5,000.00 (five thousand reais), but whose wealth is composed of boats, luxurious properties, vehicles, and other assets.
--- seg-a1bdb7c5a23fdace551a82a6 [needs-review] ---
"Article 12." Regardless of the criminal, civil, and administrative sanctions provided for in specific legislation, the person responsible for an act of improbity is subject to the following penalties, which may be applied individually or cumulatively, depending on the severity of the act: I - in accordance with Article 9, loss of assets or values illegally added to the patrimony, full restitution of any damage, loss of public office, suspension of political rights for eight to ten years, payment of a civil fine of up to three times the value of the patrimonial increase, and prohibition from contracting with or receiving public benefits or fiscal or credit incentives, directly or indirectly, even through a legal entity of which they are a majority shareholder, for a period of ten years;

Unique Paragraph. In determining the penalties provided for in this law, the judge shall take into account the extent of the damage caused, as well as the patrimonial benefit obtained by the agent. (I emphasized)

--- seg-6cd379b95ae66eb494ecf405 [needs-review] ---
In luxury, etc. Your wealth will undoubtedly be considered disproportionate to your income. There is a presumption that the wealth is due to the practice of acts of improbity, although it is up to you to prove the legitimate origin of these assets. The legal precept of illicit enrichment as an act of administrative improbity is precisely to allow the punishment of the dishonest servant against whom the original illegal act cannot be pointed out, however, under the penalty of nullity, opportunities will always be given to the servant to clarify the origin of his wealth.

In this context, it is important to note that Decree No. 5,483/05, which "regulates, within the Executive Branch, Article 13 of Law No. 8,429 of June 2, 1992, establishes patrimonial scrutiny and provides for other measures," clarified that the analysis of the public servant's patrimonial evolution can be carried out by the General Control of the Union whenever it deems necessary, and if a patrimonial inconsistency is detected, the scrutiny procedure should be initiated. This is what Article 7 of the decree stipulates.

‘’The General Control of the Union, within the Federal Executive Branch, may analyze, whenever it deems necessary, the property evolution of the public official to verify the compatibility of this with the resources and availabilities that make up their property, as provided for in Law No. 8,429 of 1992, in accordance with the special provisions of Law No. 8,730 of November 10, 1993. This is a crime committed by a public official of immense gravity that reflects the efficiency of corruption, however, we must combat it for the good of the Administration and society. In light of the above, we count on the support of our esteemed colleagues for the approval of this bill, in these terms. Session Room, May 8, 2018.

--- seg-741abe8ef27baaec995b7b65 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPACH:
TO THE COMMITTEE ON CONSTITUTION AND JUSTICE AND CITIZENSHIP (MERIT AND ART. 54, RICD).
--- seg-3d7c126ee5029c7010d7a496 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposal Subject to Final Review by the Committees - Art. 24 II
--- seg-03cd58a6cb7b2aeea63e8830 [needs-review] ---
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS decrees:

Article 1 - This Law adds a provision to Law No. 8,935 of November 18, 1994, which regulates Article 236 of the Federal Constitution, providing for notarial and registration services. Article 2 - Law No. 8,935 of November 18, 1994, shall be effective with the following amendments:

                       Article 37-A. Natural or legal persons designated by the competent authorities of the states and the Federal District, in accordance with state and district legislation, to manage the collection and transfers of resources intended for the compensation of free civil registration acts and for the complementation of the minimum revenue of deficitary offices, as well as those responsible for resources allocated to the pension funds of registrars and notaries, are required to account for these funds as public resource managers. They must document all corresponding acts and submit them to oversight, providing a detailed documentary report to the respective Courts of Justice and Courts of Accounts on a semi-annual basis.

§ 1 - The duty to account as stipulated in the preceding paragraph is independent of any additional regulations in place for its implementation, even if operational rules are established within the competence of the oversight bodies. Article 3. This Law enters into force on the date of its publication.
--- seg-1ea3a438f47fd71f9207000e [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION

Law No. 8.935/94, which regulates notarial and registration services, should also aim to ensure transparency and integrity in the management of public resources. Despite the obligation of any manager of public funds to account, since the issuance of the relevant norm, as well as those that followed regarding emoluments, there is a gap to be addressed, whether because it would not be justified in the face of public law imperatives, or due to the need to adapt this normative instrument to the current reality and the society's desire, making this accounting obligation clear and unquestionable. Thus, in accordance with the relevant regulations on the matter and aiming to adequately address the gap, it was deemed necessary to include the aforementioned normative device to ensure that both the funds allocated for the compensation of registrars related to free acts and the minimum revenue complement for deficitary offices, as well as the funds for the registrars' and notaries' pension portfolio, as public resources, are clearly and formally subject to oversight.

===== PAGE 107 [page-fa59e9d3113f9386faa99c35] =====
--- seg-9e9bdf7ee625aa4978a6a9b2 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                         Tuesday, May 15, 107
--- seg-b02ea66f948173cfe7af1f02 [needs-review] ---
by the competent courts of justice (as already provided for other cases in Article 37 and following of the same Law No. 935/94), and to the review of their respective audit courts, fulfilling the "end mission" of supervision. There is currently no specific determination regarding the management, allocation, and oversight of these resources, nor is there any obligation to submit them to the review of the competent authorities. In the absence of explicit legal forecasting, we end up supplying it with this present Bill. Even the Federal Constitution, in particular Article 71, Section II, in conjunction with Article 75, charges these Tribunals with the oversight of "accounting, financial, budgetary, operational, and patrimonial" matters, as well as the judgment of accounts of any individuals responsible for public funds, assets, and values, as in the present case. In fact, considering that our legislation must be in line with the Magna Carta and that, when it comes to public resources, there is no exception that allows any non-compliance with the proposed directives, it becomes imperative to include the aforementioned legal command, which, in truth, is not innovative, but merely aligns with the Superior Norm, as it should have been this way long ago. Furthermore, given the current economic and financial situation, in the face of the scarcity of public funds, we have a duty to ensure efficiency in legislative drafting, regulating the allocation and proper oversight of available resources. In this way, we will meet the growing demand of society for an efficient and regular management of public resources, eliminating, as much as possible, any margin for possible deviations or arbitrariness regarding the matter. For the reasons stated herein, I request the support of my esteemed colleagues for the approval of this important bill.

Article 1º O of Law 9.503 of September 23, 1997, is amended to include the following single paragraph:

"Article 338. [...]" UNIQUE PARAGRAPH. The owner's manual should contain accurate information about the maximum volume the fuel tank can hold, as well as the maximum volume of the reservoir, considering the model and year of the respective vehicle, and stating the acceptable volume variation during refueling. (NR)

Article 2: This law enters into force 180 days after its publication.
--- seg-ddf4427e7a4e6328d09090e8 [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-7cef013f1ae90518f09df7a4 [needs-review] ---
Law No. 9.503/1997 requires automobile manufacturers, bodybuilders, importers, and vehicle manufacturers to provide, at the time of sale, a manual containing traffic regulations, infractions, penalties, defensive driving, first aid, and annexes of the Brazilian Traffic Code. This driver's manual is accompanied, in the same volume or in a separate volume, by the owner's manual, containing information about each particular vehicle model. The fact is, it can sometimes be difficult, or even impossible, to find information about the fuel volume the tank can hold. To make matters worse, the volume indicated in the manual may be incorrect. A report published by Sindicombustíveis Resan1 details the common inconveniences at fueling stations across the country, where drivers question the volume measured by the pump upon filling their tanks, confronting retailers with their vehicle manuals and claiming it would be impossible to fuel the volume indicated by the pump. To assess the situation, the National Federation of Fuel and Lubricant Commerce (Fecombustíveis) commissioned a study that compared the information in the manuals of 13 vehicle models with the actual capacity of their respective tanks2. A single model had a volume measured identical to the manual, while others reached a variation of up to 36.5% higher. In other words,
--- seg-3d028045fa58abd0a084a453 [needs-review] ---
1 Union of Retail Dealers of Petroleum Derivatives, Natural Gas and Biofuels, and Stores Convenience, and Quick Car Wash Companies and Parking Lots in Santos and Region. http://www.resan.com.br/news-full/33299-car-x-tank-capacity-manual/ 2     http://www.fecombustiveis.org.br/revendedor/estudo-da-fecombustiveis-comprova-capacidade-maxima-dos-tanques- above-the-vehicle-manual/

===== PAGE 109 [page-787e855b5e2316de404e2c17] =====
--- seg-f6bd05bd2875e9c34e362295 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                       HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                      Tuesday, May 15, 109
--- seg-699cf9f07785240fe9fb913e [machine-unreviewed] ---
While refueling at a reserve, a driver will be surprised to find a third more fuel than expected, and may question the attendant, perhaps even unfairly accusing the gas station of fraud. This situation leaves both parties as victims of misinformation.

For this reason, we present the above bill. It is not justified that an industry with such advanced technological sophistication as the automotive sector, be negligent in assessing the capacity of the fuel tank. We count on the support of our esteemed colleagues for the approval of this minor amendment to the law.

JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-1299209be780ffc125540ad1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The modernization of consumer relations has driven diversification not only in the way products and services are offered but also in the expansion of payment instruments, especially in retail trade.
--- seg-074120b68a089b34d054f382 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The use of debit and credit cards has moved beyond mere convenience and has become a reality for many consumers, who choose this technology for various reasons: security, convenience, speed of transactions, obtaining advantages, controlling expenses, among others.
--- seg-0fe0610e527714a2572db68d [machine-unreviewed] ---
In the case of people with visual impairments, "plastic money" (as credit or debit cards are known) serves as an accessibility tool, as it allows autonomy in payment operations and avoids carrying and constantly handling large amounts of paper money, which poses a security risk.
--- seg-391b93ca2b50eceaf56cb5ed [machine-unreviewed] ---
However, despite the technological dynamism of so-called "point-of-sale terminals" that process payments made with cards, suppliers of products and services have not made available models that effectively meet the needs of this consumer public.
--- seg-e12d9a71e23dab48bcca7b63 [machine-unreviewed] ---
A note released in 2015 by the National Organization for the Blind in Brazil – ONCB1 criticizes this
disparity. It points out that “the traditional models of machines for payments through credit and debit cards
that featured raised-relief signage of the number 5 and on the main keys are rapidly being replaced by touch-screen debit card machines.”
--- seg-c597c0c7767e7efdfd91276f [machine-unreviewed] ---
It also emphasizes that, "due to their flawed and restrictive design, these machines deprive people with visual impairments of the use of touch, subjecting them to significant embarrassment during financial transactions, such as repeatedly trying to enter a password until it blocks the use, having to pass their card PIN to a known person to enter, or, more seriously, if alone, having to disclose the PIN to a stranger to enter."
--- seg-d73d91edbdccbdf5b8637fc6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
There are also reports that certain establishments force people with visual impairments to use their personal mobile phones as a payment terminal, or offer optical character recognition (OCR or QR code) technology, which is also not a solution for this consumer group's access to payment information.
--- seg-f027e2f4cb8fcf7a18b8b2f5 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Without any doubt, these are unimaginable situations in the current stage of accessibility discipline, whose efforts are directed towards promoting and ensuring social inclusion and the exercise of rights.
--- seg-855a730f31fe5187f9c6ba6c [machine-unreviewed] ---
1 http://www.oncb.org.br/node/103. Accessed 03/05/2018.

--- seg-b945c933a5b596718ffebf3a [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-dac49f414fbefe8fea2bc3e9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
"Taiada is a typical sweet from the Brazilian city of Caçapava, in the state of São Paulo, made from
garapa (cane juice), with cassava flour and ginger, providing a crumbly texture and enhancing the pungent
spice flavor."
--- seg-1c3e0dabd97f5bc4dd0521b0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The production of taiada is artisanal and a family tradition passed down from father to son, primarily in the rural areas of this municipality. As the sweet is made with high nutritive, caloric, and easily transportable ingredients, it was taken by rural workers to the fields and by army soldiers on marches to be used as an energy source during work and effort, as well as to sweeten drinks like coffee with milk.
--- seg-1c83f2824ed20b7f409416b0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The name "taiada" is a corruption of "talhada," the participle of the verb "talhar," which affectionately gained a rural accent, becoming popularly known as "taiada."
--- seg-8bdf32189e599de598e5cc0a [machine-unreviewed] ---
After the sugarcane is cut, manually, where the best ones are selected, they are transported to the mill where they are crushed. The resulting cane juice from the grinding process is then poured into a copper pot, and the juice is boiled for approximately 90 minutes until it reaches the desired consistency (it should be stretchy when dropped in cold water); remove from heat and mix in the grated cassava flour and ginger; pour the mixture into a traditional wooden mold in a square shape, and let it sit for an hour until it hardens, cools, and takes its shape, after which it can be removed from the molds. In the book "Miçangas Folclóricas" by folklorist Francisco Pereira da Silva, known

===== PAGE 119 [page-9e0c646e9da3a432c4ef679f] =====
--- seg-23fd36a708941b1bfd375219 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                         Tuesday, May 15, 119
--- seg-a05e6de0da29f0f0314fd02f [machine-unreviewed] ---
As Chico Triste, there is a recipe dictated by Benedito Martins.
--- seg-0d02d24da86a4a61be2d6e13 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Those born in Caçapava, or living in the municipality, are affectionately called "taiadas," in reference to the sweet found in that city. There are several versions of the origin of this nickname, but almost all are related to young people who completed their mandatory military service at the Brazilian Army barracks and, when they left, would stop at a bar and, among other things, buy the sweet. Those from other cities would bid farewell to the Caçapavenses, addressing them as "taiada," and despite the sweet no longer being as popular as it once was, the nickname is still widely used.
--- seg-42e5fea2a894c62bebbeab2a [needs-review] ---
This justification, extracted from the free encyclopedia, Wikipedia, https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiada, It clearly demonstrates the importance of the sweet to our country's popular culture, which is why I propose the present project in line with the impeccable work of rescuing popular culture formulated by Caçapava City Secretary of Culture, Sport and Leisure, Professor Fabrício Correia, in compliance with formulations for culture developed by mayor Fernando Cid Diniz Borges.
--- seg-362a01737af701197f59cfd6 [needs-review] ---
In light of all the above, we call on the Honorable Members of this House to support the approval of the bill in question.

BILL NO. 10,206 OF 2018
                                    (By Mr. Dr. Sinval Malheiros)
--- seg-c0035eb6cba242ce08bfc097 [needs-review] ---
Elevate the Bastos Egg Party/SP to the status of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Brazil.
--- seg-671b5341aee7871be833dce9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
MEMORANDUM:
TO:
THE COMMITTEES OF:
CULTURE; AND
CONSTITUTION AND JUSTICE AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 RICD).
--- seg-aed30a4cd8903e69de8b7394 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposal Subject to Final Review by the Committees - Art. 24 II
--- seg-1af5bc6ca6921c5b2ede6d8a [machine-unreviewed] ---
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS DECREES:
--- seg-ab82a33fb43d85b9bfcfaa7a [needs-review] ---
Article 1: This Law aims to recognize the importance of the Egg Festival in Bastos/SP as the main event promoting the significance and trade of eggs in Brazil.
--- seg-68ed0026e5fc7ea54afa7abc [needs-review] ---
Article 2. The Bastos Egg Festival/SP is hereby established as intangible cultural heritage of Brazil, for all legal purposes.
--- seg-d9d83431cd0d93faeec4c07c [needs-review] ---
Art. 3rd This Law enters into force on the date of its publication.
--- seg-57c0f5af2b47309aa28dbced [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-f461bd5f11c09bcd77eef32c [machine-unreviewed] ---
Bastos is a Brazilian municipality, located in the interior of the state of São Paulo, with a population of approximately twenty thousand inhabitants. It is known, above all, for its egg production, being known as “the national capital of eggs.” And as one of the reasons that underpin its importance in domestic egg production, there is the egg festival of Bastos.
--- seg-f2f5ed98d0064de6763db82b [needs-review] ---
The city, founded by Japanese immigrants, turned to egg production after World War II as a way to revive its local economy. Thanks to tireless and excellent work, the activity gained strength and the city became a reference pole in the area, with over seven decades dedicated to the practice, considered the main exponent of the segment since the 1960s.
--- seg-081f633519a4cb2a6e21bf35 [needs-review] ---
The municipality has over 33 million birds intended for egg production, and according to the local Rural Syndicate president in 2017, avicultor Katsuhide Maki, the municipality's farms produce 216 units per second, with 18.7 million eggs per day. Annually, Bastos produces around 10 billion eggs, which represents about 25% of Brazil's annual production of 40 billion.
--- seg-7cc8a96d791523013d92021a [machine-unreviewed] ---
Therefore, with less than 0.01% of the national population, Bastos produces alone 25% of a
food of immense nutritional value and fundamental importance to the Brazilian, being a rich protein
and vitamin source at a price generally more accessible than red meat, for example.
--- seg-2c11b83ac8bff7b38bfef6bc [needs-review] ---
In the face of such a redemption brought about by egg production, Bastos began to hold his Egg Festival. The event was born in the year 1948 and gained importance over time. Before

===== PAGE 125 [page-c18fe739c47e6dca6b7a8a4b] =====
--- seg-9b271b47f3ef34e6456118d6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                        HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                        Tuesday, May 15, 125
--- seg-1496e32e4c71d0206cf2144f [needs-review] ---
held every five years, the festival became annual and today is on its 59th edition, highlighting the
importance of the site and its dedication to egg production.
--- seg-6fa9ca90b2d0b43379e436c1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
It is an event of extreme importance and attractiveness to the surrounding regions, attracting the interest of numerous producers linked to the sector. In 2017, for example, eighty-two companies were exhibitors at the event, demonstrating its magnitude, and its importance is growing steadily. From 2016 to 2017, for instance, there was a 30% increase in the number of exhibitors.
--- seg-068044946fcaf8c549c44789 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The event has a little bit of everything: recreational activities related to the egg (competitions on who eats the most), contests aimed at assessing the quality of eggs and concluding with the best one, workshops and lectures intended to disseminate information about the food, its production and techniques, and even serving as a pole for technological discussions on the topic.
--- seg-04737cc078c86a674dd517c6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
It is undeniable that the festival functions as a true driving force behind egg production in Brazil,
with characteristic aspects of cultural diffusion, informational, educational, and commercial, which evidences
a cultural and intangible heritage. The tradition and quality of what is produced there are of fundamental
importance not only for Bastos, or even for the large state of São Paulo, but for Brazil, as it is the greatest
exponent of the production of one of the main national foods.
--- seg-3d43aab87e2afee6c33e14bd [needs-review] ---
For all these reasons, we understand that the Bastes Egg Festival/SP requires formal recognition from this National Congress and, subsequently, from the Executive Power, to sanction its existence as a cultural and intangible heritage of our nation.
--- seg-317a3ce81869a96796b87b03 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Brazil needs to learn to value and perfect its traditions of great importance, which transmit good customs,
something that Bastos has set an example for. This is because he has transformed this recreational event
into a chance for commerce, knowledge and technology dissemination, without losing the joy and leisure
the festival provides.
--- seg-1d334b5db38993ebbcd8fc28 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Thus, we submit this proposal to the consideration of our distinguished colleagues and urge them to
approve it. For taking care of cities (and their traditions) is taking care of people.
--- seg-57ebea080cd36f2f0da6d151 [needs-review] ---
Session Room, May 9, 2018.
--- seg-59d5fbb9046285053206c05c [needs-review] ---
Dr. Sinval Malheiros
                                  Doctor and Federal Deputy (PODEMOS/SP)

LEGISLATIVE DECREE PROJECT No. 923, 2018
                                      (by Mr. Jerônimo Goergen)
--- seg-75b681830ae0244f0425398d [needs-review] ---
Suspends the effects of Instruction Normative MP nº 2, of January 24, 2018, which establishes rules and guidelines for the execution of a service provision contract to be concluded between the Union and financial institutions federal officials, acting as agents of the Union, in the operational management of transfer contracts, in accordance with Decree 6,170 of July 25, 2007, and all subsequent acts derived from the aforementioned. instruction normative.
--- seg-bbfb663856538c5c0bda6e13 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
REFER TO PDC-905/2018.
--- seg-a30f5027162d5b19828e6d54 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-dbc0bd09438ff58744fa9d0a [machine-unreviewed] ---
The National Congress decrees:
--- seg-a193697f3fe942df7639917e [needs-review] ---
Article 1: The effects of MP Instruction No. 2 of January 24, 2018, which establishes rules and guidelines for the execution of a service contract to be concluded between the Union and official federal financial institutions, to act as agents of the Union in the operational management of transfer contracts, in accordance with Decree 6,170 of July 25, 2007, as well as all derivative acts of the aforementioned instruction, are hereby suspended.
--- seg-f4ee60ba57dc523f6f746a02 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Art. 2° This legislative decree enters into force on the date of its official publication.
--- seg-80269d92851939c20fd78462 [needs-review] ---
JUSTIFICATION

We received with undeniable dissatisfaction the news that the Ministry of Planning, in response to complaints from the Federal Savings Bank, issued the 2/18 Normative Instruction, a new legal framework for the execution of service contracts to be concluded between the Union and federal official financial institutions, as agents of the Union, for the operational management of transfer contracts. The government's decision to increase the administration fees charged for agreements signed with ministries and funded with parliamentary allocation resources was taken unilaterally and without any prior dialogue with this House, members of parliament, and municipalities directly affected by the measure. The traditional administration fees, typically charged at 2.5% of each individual grant value over the past years, have been catapulted to percentages that can reach around 12% of the total amount to be disbursed. Legally, morally, and constitutionally highly questionable, the measure damages the execution of vital works and services for the poor population of the country, already so abandoned by federal public policies. Therefore, as it is the competence of this National Congress, according to article 49, item V, of the Federal Constitution, "to revoke normative acts of the Executive Power that exceed the regulatory power or the limits of legislative delegation", I present this Legislative Decree project to revoke the effects of Instruction Normative MP nº 2, of January 24, 2018, and I count on the support of my Parliamentary colleagues in the approval of this matter. Session Room, on May 02, 2018.

The participation of state-owned companies in economic activity should be guided by significant collective interest or national security imperatives to achieve goals such as ensuring national development and reducing social and regional inequalities, among others, as established by our Federal Constitution.
--- seg-78a2798545d864c4ca8e9ba9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Indirect public administration, which includes state-owned enterprises, must adhere to the constitutional principles of legality, impersonality, morality, publicity, and efficiency. The general need to bid is indispensable in this regard, even for public enterprises and mixed-economy societies.
--- seg-0a352b3cf04cceda44a7ce84 [machine-unreviewed] ---
According to Article 173, §1, of the Federal Constitution, the law will establish the legal status
of the public company, the mixed economy society, and its subsidiaries that engage in economic
activities related to the production or commercialization of goods or the provision of services,
including provisions on bidding and contracting for works, services, purchases, and alienations.
--- seg-d320eef4b79312aa0a19009d [needs-review] ---
Law No. 13.303 of June 30, 2016, known as the Legal Framework for State-Owned Companies, regulated Article 173, §1, and established the legal framework for public companies, mixed economy companies, and their subsidiaries, within the scope of the Union, states, Federal District, and municipalities.

===== PAGE 129 [page-e05b2f84e68686364ff7bc92] =====
--- seg-ad73a0e0bbc6b04cc62cd1d0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                         Tuesday 15 129
--- seg-5bbe59d88f0e1603fb434f63 [needs-review] ---
Section 5 of Article 1 of Law No. 13.303/2016 is clear in defining that for the public company and the mixed economy society that participate in a consortium as the operator, they are subject to the bidding rules provided in the Legal Statute of State-Owned Enterprises, as follows:
--- seg-3e13f1e284aedae32d647268 [machine-unreviewed] ---
§ 5. Public companies and mixed-economy societies that participate in a consortium, as provided in Article 279 of Law No. 6,404 of December 15, 1976, shall be subject to the regime established in this Law, in the capacity of operator.
--- seg-4997785bfce5ea501cb64051 [needs-review] ---
In accordance with Article 28 of Law No. 303/2016, contracts with third parties for the provision of services to public companies and mixed-economy societies, including engineering and advertising, the acquisition and leasing of assets, and the alienation of assets and assets forming part of their respective patrimony, shall be preceded by a bidding process.
--- seg-c067766974fa84f3b8feb4ce [machine-unreviewed] ---
Thus, the procurement of goods and services by consortia operated by Petrobras and the cession by the state-owned company of rights to explore, develop, and produce oil and natural gas must be preceded by a bidding process, and the bidding process must comply with the requirements established by Law No. 13.303/2016.
--- seg-da00df8929fa91d80e43a018 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 1 of Decree No. 9,355 of April 25, 2018, establishes a special procedure for the cession of rights for exploration, development, and production of petroleum and natural gas by Petrobras, as provided for in Article 29, Article 61, paragraph 1, and Article 63 of Law No. 9,478 of August 6, 1997, and in Article 31 of Law No. 12,351 of December 22, 2010.
--- seg-033a390329a5e47238bd115e [machine-unreviewed] ---
It is important to note that: Article 29 of Law No. 9.478/1997 only allows the transfer of the concession contract; Article 61, caput and § 1, essentially deals with preventing favoritism to Petrobras in the acquisition of rights related to petroleum activities; and Article 63 only authorizes Petrobras to form consortia. Article 31 of Law No. 12.351/2010, on the other hand, is generic and applicable to all companies, except for the sole paragraph, which does not allow Petrobras to cede rights related to its minimum participation. It is also noted that all these legal devices precede the promulgation of Law No. 13.302/2016.
--- seg-fd5e7ac6b70175c545204c97 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Thus, Decree No. 9.355/2018 exceeds the regulatory power and limits of legislative delegation by establishing a special procedure for the assignment of exploration, development, and production rights for oil, natural gas, and other fluid hydrocarbons by Petrobras.

THE NATIONAL CONGRESS, in the exercise of its powers and on the basis of articles 49, paragraphs V, X, and XI of the Federal Constitution, decrees:
--- seg-3fb92770d65f5770901c1386 [needs-review] ---
Article 1 - This Decree Suspends the effects of Item 09 of the minutes of the 364th (three hundred and sixty-fourth) Ordinary Meeting of the Brazilian Urban Trains Company (CBTU) Board of Directors, held on February 26, 2018, which approved the increase in metro fares in several Brazilian capitals.
--- seg-9b106533d58a4a99af60e23c [needs-review] ---
Art. 2 - The Executive Branch shall take the necessary measures to implement this Legislative Decree.
--- seg-ae684e9441c274cd28ea8986 [needs-review] ---

--- seg-5382857c0567aa018e97efb8 [needs-review] ---
JUSTIFICATION

       The Brazilian Urban Train Company (CBTU) announced significant increases in the prices of
metro fares in five capitals of the country. The metro fares in Belo Horizonte, Recife, João Pessoa, Natal, and Maceió will have new values starting on May 11, 2018, with increases reaching nearly 90%. Such an increase was formalized through Item 09 of the minutes of the 364th Regular Meeting of the Board of Directors of Companhia Brasileira de Trens Urbanos – CBTU –, held on February 26, 2018, whose transcription follows below:

"Item 09." Tariff Recomposition. Based on a Technical Note from the General Management of Planning and Budget, previously presented to the Council, this collegiate body approved Proposal No. 003-20181DP issued by the Planning, Expansion, and Marketing Directorate, which received a favorable opinion at the 605th Executive Board Meeting on February 21, 2018, regarding tariff recomposition based on the financial rebalancing of the operational revenue of CBTU's systems."1

In a note2, CBTU justifies the significant and abrupt adjustment by arguing:
--- seg-276d8cc034ecc41a95ac6a02 [machine-unreviewed] ---
1
    Report available at https://www.cbtu.gov.br/images/relatorios/conad/364_2018.pdf. Accessed on 10/05/2018.
--- seg-263843acd02a90ef8db2fbe4 [machine-unreviewed] ---
2
Available at https://www.cbtu.gov.br/index.php/pt/?option=com_content&view=article&id=6972&itemid=1322. Accessed on

===== PAGE 133 [page-3263e1b65d741e22c0fd8377] =====
--- seg-4708d2fd54d21c54466b7900 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                       CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                       Tuesday, May 15, 133
--- seg-c2eeadecb21a54b4ff79873c [needs-review] ---
"Strictly across the country, public transportation fares undergo adjustments based, typically, on inflation indices. CBTU therefore claims mere recompensation for inflationary losses." However, in the specific case of Recife, to stay with an example, the tariff correction will be much
higher than the accumulated inflation during the period since the last adjustment. Such adjustment occurred in
February 2012, when the fare was set at R$ 1.60. With the monetary update based on IGP-M (FGV), this value would be R$ 2.27 today, therefore well below the proposed adjustment of R$ 3.00. A CTBU
adjusted the rate by incredible 24.3% above mere monetary correction. In addition to the inconsistency of the justification that claims monetary correction while there was a readjustment above the accumulated inflation, the readjustment is abusive and sudden, generating a high degree of uncertainty and economic and financial instability for public service users. Access to public transportation is a social right guaranteed in the Federal Constitution (art. 6). The purpose of this proposal is to protect the fundamental rights of the population, preventing setbacks in sensitive areas related to the basic rights of the Brazilian citizen. Section V of Article 49 of the Federal Constitution (CF) attributes an extremely important exclusive competence to the National Congress, namely, the power to invalidate normative acts of the Executive Branch that exceed its regulatory power. Furthermore, articles X and XI confer upon said body the competencies of "inspecting and controlling, directly or through any of its houses, the acts of the executive power, including those of indirect administration" and of "ensuring the preservation of its legislative competence in light of the normative attribution of the other powers." It is therefore observed that the aforementioned increase, authorized through the Administrative Council of CBTU - CONAD, exceeds, by far, the regulatory power granted to the Executive Branch, being absolutely incompatible with the guiding principles of the 1988 Federal Constitution. Thus, considering that such a tariff increase represents a clear disrespect for the constitutional order – characterizing, therefore, a blatant "excess of regulatory power or the limits of legislative delegation", as per Article 49, V of the Magna Carta – it is up to the National Congress, hearing the just concern of the population, to guarantee access to public transportation through this legislative decree, revoking Item 09 of the minutes of the 364th (three hundred sixty-fourth) Regular Meeting of the Board of Directors of the Brazilian Urban Trains Company – CBTU –, held on February 26, 2018, which approves the tariff increase for the subway in various Brazilian capitals. Session Room, May 10, 2018.

RESOLUTION DRAFT

No. 314, 2018
(from Mr. Rodrigo Garcia and others)
--- seg-5a5563a05691a5a5c51dc66e [needs-review] ---
Designates as space named after Deputy Joaquim Nabuco and provides other measures.
--- seg-e15b79832a5a4e24726ee286 [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
TO THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES
--- seg-2e67229d9420f984a2c0e526 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposition Subject to Review by the Plenum
--- seg-4a07e3f21ede1e8fe0bde9df [machine-unreviewed] ---
The House of Deputies' Table resolves:
--- seg-f18b460ebfe76323cb6ec241 [needs-review] ---
Article 1. A space in the Noble Hall of the Chamber of Deputies shall be designated as "Deputy Joaquim Nabuco," which will house a bronze bust of the personality and a corresponding identifying plaque. Art. 2° The technical bodies of the House will indicate, after study, an appropriate location within the Noble Hall,
for the designation of the space and the placement of the bust. Article 3° The Desk of the Chamber of Deputies will provide for the manufacture of the plate with the inscriptions corresponding to the tribute and designate a date for its unveiling. Art. 4: This Resolution shall enter into force on the date of its publication.
--- seg-5734e06d8359981cfc3820e8 [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-e4b070bc17616ec82e88f5a1 [needs-review] ---
The purpose of this project is to honor – by placing his bust in an appropriate location – the extraordinary figure of Joaquim Nabuco, known and admired as an intellectual, writer, social scientist, jurist, diplomat, and above all, as one of the icons of the abolitionist movement in Brazil. Joaquim Nabuco (J. Aurélio Barreto N. de Araújo (born in Recife on August 19, 1849) is the son of Senator Nabuco de Araújo and his wife, Ana Benigna de Sá Barreto. He died in Washington,
USA, on January 17, 1910. He grew up within the influential families of Pernambuco's politics. On the father's side, "the Nabuco de Araújo" - father and grandfather - were senators of the Empire; on the mother's side, "the Paes Barreto". He entered the diplomatic service and served from 1876 to 1879 in London and Washington. He was drawn,
a little later, into the field of politics, captivated by the abolitionist campaign, a cause to which he dedicated his entire life. Between 1879 and 1889, he served as a Federal Deputy, representing the state of Pernambuco, elected by the Liberal Party, where he stood out as the main parliamentary leader in the abolitionist struggle. Ahead of his time, Joaquim Nabuco not only advocated for the end of slavery; he particularly championed the access of newly freed slaves to basic rights, such as education and fair employment. He also fought firmly for agrarian reform and the consecration of a secular state. When the Republic was proclaimed in 1889, he defended the monarchy with pride and withdrew from public life to dedicate himself to studies and his literary works. During that period, he practiced law and journalism; he established close relations with the most prominent figures of Brazilian literary life, such as Machado de Assis, José Veríssimo, and Lúcio de Mendonça. It is believed that the establishment of the Brazilian Academy of Letters in 1897 is due to the gatherings of these privileged minds.

===== PAGE 137 [page-8f9e3311d61b152ae5b58351] =====
--- seg-7f2c29e9f784aff48bf96725 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                       CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                       Tuesday, May 15, 137
--- seg-19029e0245ba3eab526ea116 [needs-review] ---
His intellectual collection includes essays, articles, books, and speeches; the work is intricate and widely consulted in the present day. Among his works, we would highlight "Abolitionism (1883)," which depicts the social evolution of Brazil and the racial question; and "My Formation (1900)," a classified autobiographical creation, in which his famous phrase is recited: "Slavery will remain for a long time as the national characteristic of Brazil." In 1889, after numerous appeals, Nabuco returns to public life and accepts an invitation from the government to defend Brazil in the issue involving the borders with then English Guiana. In 1905, he becomes the first
ambassador of Brazil in the United States. His story and his legacy of ideas have been repeatedly recognized and honored. In
2010, for example, in partnership with the Brazilian Academy of Letters (ABL) and with the support of the Joaquim Nabuco Foundations (Fundaj) and Armando Álvares Penteado (Faap), the Chamber of Deputies paid a well-deserved tribute to Joaquim Nabuco on the centenary of his death. At the time, the focus of the celebrations
highlighted his life as a parliamentarian. The year 2018 marks 140 years since the election of Joaquim Nabuco to the Chamber of Deputies. Nothing more
than just that the Chamber should honor this great figure in our history once again, this time by placing the already existing bust
in a prominent position inside the Noble Hall. It is with this objective that I submit to the noble peers this present Resolution Project, for which I request special support in its approval, in memory of Joaquim Nabuco's history, his contribution to social causes in the country, and his brilliant performance as a parliamentarian in this House.
--- seg-158b217f4b4517641a6bb0c8 [needs-review] ---
Session Room, May 08, 2018.

JUSTIFICATION

The proposal for the Maria da Penha Medal, to be conferred by the Chamber of Deputies, aims to honor individuals, institutions, and social movements, both national and international, that, with the same spirit of struggle as Maria da Penha, have distinguished themselves through significant initiatives in the fight against violence against women.

Above all, it is a recognition of the historical role played by Brazilian Maria da Penha in the struggle for women's rights. In 1983, Maria da Penha was victimized by her then-husband with a gunshot wound to the back while she slept, resulting in her becoming paraplegic. After further violence from her ex-husband, Maria da Penha initiated a lengthy and exhausting legal process that lasted 19 years and 6 months until her ex-husband was convicted in 2002 to eight years in prison.

Beyond her aggressor's conviction, Maria da Penha's struggle led the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights of the Organization of American States (OAS) to condemn Brazil in 2001 for negligence, omission, and tolerance regarding domestic violence against women, and to recommend the adoption of public policies aimed at preventing, punishing, and eradicating violence against women. As a direct consequence of this condemnation, the National Congress made new efforts to enact legislation aimed at preventing and punishing domestic violence in Brazil.

After years of debate, the National Congress enacted and the President of the Republic sanctioned Law 11.340 of August 7, 2006, rightfully known as the "Maria da Penha Law," which establishes mechanisms to combat domestic and family violence against women, in accordance with Article 226, § 8 of the Federal Constitution, the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, and the Inter-American Convention to Prevent, Punish and Eradicate Violence against Women; it provides for the establishment of Domestic and Family Violence against Women Courts; it amends the Criminal Procedure Code, the Penal Code, and the Penal Execution Law; and it takes other measures.

Despite the landmark represented by the Maria da Penha Law, the sad reality is that Maria da Penha's history of domestic violence is still repeated daily in thousands of Brazilian homes. Some data from the Maria da Penha Institute highlight this dramatic picture: (i) every 2 seconds, a woman is a victim of physical or verbal violence in Brazil; (ii) every 2.6 seconds, a woman is a victim of verbal abuse; (iii) every 6.3 seconds, a woman is a victim of a threat of violence; (iv) every 2 minutes, a woman is a victim of a firearm; (v) every 22.5 seconds, a woman is a victim of

===== PAGE 140 [page-1b7ef725094c52340e531d30] =====
--- seg-6fd0fb3d102efb29b0506386 [machine-unreviewed] ---
140 Tuesday, May 15                  DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                          2018
--- seg-a2ab59301b8d34a841cb9426 [needs-review] ---
beating or attempted strangulation; (vi) every 1.4 seconds, a woman is a victim of harassment; (vii) every 4.6 seconds, a woman is a victim of harassment at work; (viii) every 6.1 seconds, a woman is a victim of physical harassment in public transportation. In turn, the 11th edition of the Brazilian Public Security Annual, released in 2017,
records 49,497 cases of rape and 4,657 murders of women in 2016. From another perspective, the
research “Visible and Invisible: The Victimization of Women in Brazil,” conducted by Datafolha in 2016,
found that: (i) 73% of the Brazilian population believes that violence against women has increased in the
last 10 years; (ii) 66% of the population has witnessed a woman being a victim of some form of violence;
(iii) 29% of women reported having experienced at least some form of violence in the last 12 months; (iv)
the majority of perpetrators (61%) are known individuals to the victim, particularly spouses/partners/boyfriends
and ex-spouses/ex-partners/ex-boyfriends; (v) 43% of cases of violence against women occurred at home; (vi)
in most cases, women do not take action against the violence they suffer, with 52% reporting that they did
nothing; (vii) 40% of women reported having experienced some form of harassment, with the most common
type being receiving disrespectful comments while walking on the street. In the context of this persistent violence against women, we understand it is the duty of this House of Representatives to recognize and amplify initiatives relevant to combating violence against women. That is precisely the goal of the Maria da Penha Award: to effectively contribute to the wide dissemination, recognition, and multiplication of successful actions to combat violence against women throughout the national territory.

May 2018                        HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                        Tuesday 15 151

INDICATION No. 5.187, 2018
(From Mr. Weliton Prado)
--- seg-c25d9bc60b18976b9226aee6 [needs-review] ---
Suggest to the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Supply (MAPA) through the Supply Centers of Minas Gerais S.A (Ceasa/MG) urgent measures to resume the sales schedule of small producers' and family farmers' products held on Fridays in the afternoon at the Uberlândia unit in the Minas Gerais Triangle.
--- seg-8b613dc6eb8c02daa72ca68e [machine-unreviewed] ---
DISPATCH:
PUBLISH. FORWARD.
--- seg-32b9577adf007c93542bae72 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Most Excellent Sir,
--- seg-4bfd79948e31e1064f93f399 [needs-review] ---
Small producers and family farmers were surprised by another arbitrary and undiscussed decision by Uberlândia's Ceasa, which now aims to change the product sales schedule from Friday afternoons to mornings.

Sales have always taken place in the afternoon to ensure producers from Uberlândia and the surrounding region have enough time to travel and organize their products. Indeed, most of them harvest their crops in the morning and bring them to Ceasa in the afternoon to offer fresh, new, and high-quality produce to consumers over the weekend, as reinforced to our office by Zezinho Mendonça.

The schedule change to morning hours should only occur after extensive discussion and consensus. The change drastically impacts the lives of many people, the quality of products, and the economic impact could lead to reduced purchases by the population and safety concerns for everyone with early morning travel.

It is unbelievable that Ceasa, instead of addressing issues within the unit, simply decides to change the product sales schedule without wide-ranging discussion, justification, or consensus.

I am the author of House Bill No. 59/2015, which establishes the National Plan for the Supply of Horticultural, Fruit, and Grain Products – PLANHORT – and is currently being reviewed by the Senate after being approved by the Chamber of Deputies. Therefore, we are aware of and fight for the improvements and valorization of producers who sell at Ceasa. The suffering is immense and repeats every year.

According to UN data, family farming produces approximately 80% of the food consumed and preserves 75% of the planet's agricultural resources. In Brazil, family farmers are responsible for most of the food that reaches the population's tables, ensuring food security, rural family permanence, and environmental preservation. Such disrespect cannot be tolerated, and the consequences of this measure will be negative for the budgets of families who rely on Uberlândia's Ceasa for product sales; for consumers who may experience reduced product quality; and for the economy of Uberlândia and the region.

Chamber of Sessions, May 8, 2018.

WELITON PRADO
                                  FEDERAL DEPUTY – PROS/MG

In pursuit of public opinion mobilization and the creation of a favorable environment for privatization, the company outlined as its strategy the dissemination of a scenario of miseries and problems of the state-owned enterprise. To do this, it was necessary to activate so-called opinion formers,
       the press, release notes in newspaper columns, arm economic commentators,
       set the media agenda by showing a scenario that made the privatization urgent,
       accelerated by the federal government's haste to finalize the deal. The company denies such bias and
       states that the contract emphasizes the need to "preserve the company's positive image," although it admits that the disclosure "does not omit negative data such as financial losses or gross debt exceeding R$ 45 billion" (see "the other side at the end of the report"). According to the plan outlined in the contract, a "scenario analysis" was conducted, followed by the so-called "stakeholder mapping," that is, identifying the strategic target audience for the messages to be sent. At a later stage, there was the so-called "influencer mobilization," detailed with a cost of R$ 170,000.00 (one hundred and seventy thousand) within the total project amount of one million and eight hundred reais. One of the 10 items included in the FSB action plan and presented in the contract was the
       conduct of an opinion poll to assess the popularity of the plan to privatize Eletrobras, with a
       specific cost of R$ 120,000.00 (one hundred and twenty thousand).

===== PAGE 173 [page-d60726c4320b0e2840158bb3] =====
--- seg-51755ae44a146b633a3b6797 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                       HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                       Tuesday 15 173
--- seg-635e301ca9458aa731d2831d [needs-review] ---
The contract between Eletrobras and FSB also stipulates in item 7.1 that payments between the contracting entity and the contracted party will be made upon the "delivery of the monthly reports prepared by the contracted party corresponding to the consolidation of the achieved results." The report requested these reports through another access to information request law, but although the contract itself was made available via LAI, access to the reports was denied.

A third access to information request was made to Eletrobras regarding information about the alleged bidding process for the relevant contract, ECE-DJS 1252/2017. The request sought the names of the bidders, the proposals, the process documents, and the final result. It was also denied at both the first and second instance.

In justifying the secrecy surrounding the bidding process, Eletrobras claims that it is a "democratization of social capital" strategy, stating that "it concerns a strategic Eletrobras information, as the requested documents are directly linked to the company's performance in the competitive market." It continues: "This is because the information regarding the contract with RP Brasil Comunicações (FSB Comunicação) is a fundamental pillar in the democratization of social capital process of Eletrobras." The report also highlights the strategic importance of the contract between Eletrobras and FSB: "Indeed, it is worth noting that the disclosure of information regarding the Contract with RP is so sensitive that it could cause harm to the so-called democratization process."

The report appealed to the General Control of the Union (CGU), arguing the contradiction between having access to the contract but being denied access to the reports and bidding process, as well as other LAI issues that guarantee such access. The CGU has not responded yet.

Despite Eletrobras' denial of transparency in the access to the bidding process, the report investigated, through various sources, how the competition unfolded—or, rather, how it did not.

In the midst of the Temer government's rush to privatize Eletrobras, a "price taking" was conducted to determine who would win the ECE-DJS 1252/2017 contract. Price taking is a crucial moment in a bidding process where the price threshold for the final auction is determined, and market price parameters are demonstrated. It is also, in a general and generic sense, a moment in the bidding process where prices can be inflated.

The book "An Analysis in the Face of the Vulnerabilities of Public Tenders in Brazil" (José Luciano de Oliveira, Descartes Almeida Fontes, Rodrigo Alexandre, and Bruno Andrey) shows that, again in a general sense, "in this phase, various types of fraud can occur, such as bid rigging, pre-agreement, price fixing, overcharging, and qualification of non-existent companies."

Typically, three budgets from different companies are used. When contracting the services in question, the institution conducts the tender procedures in accordance with specific legislation, and both companies that were budgeted in the price taking phase and any other company can participate, as long as they observe market values. Thus, whenever the price taking stage is won, the tender is conducted.

The unusual is what happened at Eletrobras regarding the ECE-DJS 1252/2017 contract, according to various sources interviewed by Sportlight Investigative Journalism Agency. The reports, which complement each other, state that some of the country's largest companies in the advisory and communication sector participated in the competition. In addition to FSB, proposals were submitted by Noticias Company (CDN) and Informe Comunicação. The three occupy the podium

===== PAGE 174 [page-4712a972dac3487d77e17c18] =====
--- seg-090e8040a969fc44d7557f26 [machine-unreviewed] ---
174 Tuesday, May 15                JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-694d17150dd2919b95d1e7fa [needs-review] ---
in accounts of the federal government with recognized special expertise in communication strategy. According to the investigation by the report, Informe Comunicação had presented the lowest financial cost proposal, ranking first. The FSB would have finished second. However, after the result of the "bidding process" of the companies called for a tender, the rules of the game changed: Eletrobras decided to select the winning company through the "inability" modality, where a competition is dispensed and a direct contract is promoted. The law grants the contractor the right to choose the supplier if there are reasons justifying the waiver of bidding. In the contract in question, Eletrobras argued that "due to its complexity and uniqueness, as well as confidentiality, as it involves the company's strategic information, it could only be achieved through the impossibility of a bidding process, which makes it impossible to establish objective criteria, requiring a company with notable specialization in communication strategy" as stated in Eletrobras' response at the end of the report in "Another Side." The other parties involved in the "bid process" have contracts with other entities within the same federal government to develop communication strategies. On October 17, 2017, nearly a month after the signing of the contract between FSB and Eletrobras, the company published the result in the Official Journal of the Union, announcing the result with FSB as the winning bidder due to "inability to bid."
--- seg-0f227d76eb727168ee10f530 [needs-review] ---
The behind-the-scenes of the non-competition point to a decisive hand in choosing, after the price-taking by "unavailability of bidding" that declared FSB's victory: Wilson Pinto Ferreira Junior, appointed by Michel Temer to head the state-owned company.

Wilson Pinto Ferreira Júnior, 58, took over Eletrobras with a specific mission given by Michel Temer: to lead the privatization process. He started his professional life at the São Paulo Energy Company (CESP) and was promoted to distribution manager of the company during Mário Covas's first term as governor of São Paulo (1995). In 1998, he moved to the private sector as the first president of Rio Grande Energia, created after the partial privatization of electric power distribution in the state of Rio Grande do Sul by then-governor Antônio Britto. He took over the presidency of the CPFL company in March 2000 and has been presiding the holding since 2002.

The appointment of Wilson Pinto Ferreira Júnior by Michel Temer was on July 22, 2016.

Requests information from the Minister of State for Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation regarding the measures taken
after the collapse that occurred in the works of the BR-040 highway in Petrópolis/RJ in November 2017.
--- seg-a887bd1dc44f75e5f58807b8 [machine-unreviewed] ---
MEMORANDUM:
--- seg-094918be1a3f32ea2264c1c2 [needs-review] ---
Approval by the President, Dep. Rodrigo Maia, "subject to the approval of" the Desk, of the opinion of Dep. Fábio Ramalho, First Vice-President, for transmission.
--- seg-e8d0160e3de25995ce938079 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Mr. President:
--- seg-a6cbd82db415b3e0fed761dd [needs-review] ---
I request from you. For example, based on Article 50 of the Federal Constitution, and in accordance with Articles 115 and 116 of the Internal Regulation, after consulting the Desk, information should be requested from Mr. Minister of State for Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation, with the aim of clarifying this House regarding the problems that occurred on the outskirts of the BR-040 highway in Petrópolis/RJ, particularly concerning the actions aimed at ensuring the life, security and housing of the citizens affected by the disaster that occurred in November 2017.
--- seg-274a3ada2f5a056148c32ac8 [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-69235f53e1bf55979cd34c3f [needs-review] ---
A landslip caused the opening of a crater on the side of kilometer 81, heading to Rio de Janeiro, of the BR-040 highway on November 7, 2017. This incident immediately destroyed dozens of homes, others had to be demolished later due to irreparable damage, and over fifty were closed, leaving over a hundred people homeless in the region known as Vale da Escola. A municipal school was also affected, leading over seventy students to be unable to attend classes.
--- seg-e0f3a8ee66cc2ef5167f9e28 [needs-review] ---
The affected people, even after more than five months, still lack adequate assistance and demand a definitive solution. Despite the efforts of the Civil Defense of the Municipality of Petrópolis, the Federal Public Ministry, and the orders of the 4th Civil Court of Petrópolis, the highway concessionaire, Concer, remains inactive on the matter and has contributed little to solving the problem.
--- seg-66e3384eb972286b14236170 [needs-review] ---
An inspection report by IBAMA identified that the cause of the incident is related to problems in the construction of a tunnel. According to the report, signs that the structure could collapse were already noticeable long before the event, and the lack of rainfall in the state of Rio de Janeiro was what prevented the collapse from occurring earlier.

===== PAGE 181 [page-d2102051061fce3b459dd9d8] =====

--- seg-2e995467b574fabf96b1d76f [needs-review] ---
However, the fact that the work had been halted since the previous year contributed both to the
inability to identify the problem in a timely manner and to the degradation of the already completed parts of the work.
According to the report, continuing the work would prevent water accumulation, which is decisive for the collapse.
--- seg-18040f737fa07812571f98bd [needs-review] ---
Even more concerning is the fact that the problem could recur in the same location if the drainage and containment measures recommended in the Technical Report by the Civil Defense Secretariat and Voluntary Actions of the Municipality of Petrópolis are not implemented. Regarding these works, the Federal Public Ministry requested a conciliation hearing in February 2018, aiming to have Concer carry out these actions.
--- seg-03c8d0cdfe52c8c9068bf95d [needs-review] ---
The construction of a new ascent of the Petrópolis mountain range was considered the most important improvement to the BR-040 highway by the Highway Exploration Program, as per the concession contract signed in 1995. However, the start of the works, initially planned for the first year of the concession in 2011, was rescheduled for 2013 and 2014.
--- seg-b17fa8149a36f2c86402e177 [machine-unreviewed] ---
In addition, the implementation cost, estimated at R$ 80 million in April 1995, which today would correspond, in updated values, to approximately R$ 330 million, jumped to R$ 897 million after the concessionaire presented the basic project in 2012, a threefold increase.
--- seg-b61e8765d19d267d9b8ed415 [machine-unreviewed] ---
In 2015, the National Bank for Economic and Social Development – BNDES – approved a loan of R$ 420 million for investments in the aforementioned project.
--- seg-05d0c06e8ed19d33326efe85 [needs-review] ---
The Federal Public Ministry, however, points out irregularities on the part of the Agency. National Land Transport Agency – ANTT – in approving the start of the implementation of the works regarding the requirements set forth in Law No. 8.666/93, commonly known as the Law on Tenders, and in the release of resources through contractual addendum in violation of the Annual Budget Law of 2014 and the Federal Constitution of 1988.
--- seg-d0dca02dd10848045236760a [needs-review] ---
The Union Accounts Court – TCU – through processo nº 023.204/2015-0 in 2016,
identified irregularities in the implementation of the concession contract, such as overvaluation of the value
required for economic and financial rebalancing, overpricing in the work budget, and outdated and deficient
basic and executive projects.
--- seg-ea06faefa750dc3315ce930a [needs-review] ---
Administrators of the Triunfo Group – controller of Concer – were recently denounced by the Public Ministry in Operation Integration, the 48th phase of Lava Jato, which investigates irregularities and frauds in bidding processes at the Department of Roads and Highways of Paraná.
--- seg-8c5e3953d59d42cd07fd8049 [needs-review] ---
Thus, the scenario is extremely concerning, and the situation of the involved families demands urgent and definitive solutions. It is not acceptable that citizens have their right to housing restricted due to successive failures of the Public Administration and the concessionaires to whom public services are granted. In this particular case, we refer to the citizens affected by the incident that took place on the outskirts of BR-040 in Petrópolis, almost six months ago.

particularly the missionaries, following the recent closure of hundreds of evangelical churches and the
arrest of Protestant pastors by the government of that country.
--- seg-96f6ad873eab5cf309f9a9c0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
MEMORANDUM:
--- seg-f7f25ee97af31ee159aa804b [needs-review] ---
Approval by the President, Dep. Rodrigo Maia, "subject to the approval of" the Desk, of the opinion of Dep. Fábio Ramalho, First Vice-President, for transmission.
--- seg-5afa5b9ce25f6aa36bb84b8f [machine-unreviewed] ---
Mr. President,
--- seg-dac316a6b1265816631189f2 [needs-review] ---
I request Your Excellence, based on Article 50, § 2 of the Federal Constitution, in conjunction with Article 115, I, and 116 of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, that, after consulting the Desk, a request for information be sent to His Excellency, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Aloysio Nunes Ferreira, regarding the situation of the Brazilian Evangelical Community in Rwanda, particularly the missionaries, following the recent closure of hundreds of evangelical churches and the arrest of Protestant pastors by the government of that country.
--- seg-8f763f3082b586381d618a1b [machine-unreviewed] ---
JUSTIFICATION
--- seg-823810b2cb39da98416c6498 [machine-unreviewed] ---
In recent days, the media has reported that the Rwandan government has closed hundreds of churches and dozens of mosques. The government has banned more than 6,000 churches and around 100 mosques. Most of the closed churches are Pentecostal.
--- seg-7164e26e6cb3cae14b31e7f5 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The government claims that closed churches and mosques are in violation of safety and noise pollution standards set by Rwandan legislation. The move followed a catastrophe at a church where 16 worshippers died and 140 were injured after lightning struck the building. According to the government spokesperson, churches and mosques can resume their activities if they meet the standards established by law.
--- seg-cfd11314c29f56e005b0f4ac [machine-unreviewed] ---
According to the press, the closure is actually aimed at greater control over the growing religious community in the African country3. According to Rwanda's President, Mr. Paul Kagame, the number of

Regarding Committed Operations and their impact on public debt
--- seg-b3b7e1e531a42d4d253ed9bc [needs-review] ---
1) Why has the volume of committed operations increased so much (from 3.2% of the General Government's Gross Debt in November 2002 to 24.7% in August 2017)?
2) Why, instead of significantly increasing the balance of committed operations, were these operations not combined with the definitive sale of public securities held by the Central Bank, thereby reducing its stock and contributing to the National Treasury's efforts to lengthen the public debt profile?
3) Why does the Central Bank hold in its portfolio an amount of public securities exceeding 20% of GDP, while the international average is below 5%?
4) What is the need for the Central Bank to maintain such a high volume of public securities in its portfolio, given that Law No. 11,803 of 2008 provides for the possibility of transferring public securities from the National Treasury to the Central Bank whenever necessary to cover the latter's negative results or to meet the needs of monetary policy, with prior authorization from the Minister of Finance and without financial counterparty?
5) It is observed that a significant portion of the effort conducted by the National Treasury to lengthen the average maturities of public debt and reduce the percentage of securities indexed to the Selic rate has been "offset" by the increase in the stock of committed operations, which are characterized by extremely short maturities and interest rates that, although fixed, reflect the current Selic rate. How is coordination established between the actions of the National Treasury and the Central Bank to improve the public debt profile?

6) By maintaining a stock of committed operations exceeding R$ 1 trillion, which need to be constantly renewed, how vulnerable does the Central Bank (and consequently, the Brazilian economy) become to a speculative attack by the financial market? Justify.

7) In what way does the separate management of the two essential components (on one side, public securities managed by the National Treasury; on the other, committed operations administered by the Central Bank) compromise the effectiveness of public debt management?

8) Why do committed operations not appear in the Annual Financing Plans (PAFs), an instrument for planning the management of public securities drafted by the National Treasury Secretariat, if they fall under both the Net Public Debt (DLSP) and the Gross Government Debt (DBGG)?

9) What should be the limit for the amount of federal debt securities referred to in Article 48, paragraph XIV of the Constitution?
   a. Should this limit be set for gross debt, net debt, or both? Justify.
