JUSTIFICATION
        Two Information Requests from the Chamber of Deputies, authored by this federal deputy, are related to the issue at hand: the access of the Brazilian citizen to classified information regarding the registration and study of unidentified flying objects (UFOs) and their crew, a field known as ufology: 4470/2009 and 679/2011. Both answered in part by the three Armed Forces, in representation of the Ministry of Defense and within what the Forces claim to be the truth reported in the archives of their subordinate bodies, they confirmed not only the existence of such information, but also some occurrences involving alleged UFOs and their crew, as well as the seriousness with which at least the Brazilian Air Force (FAB) handles the matter. We have, today, over 10,000 pages of documents and other types of information in various formats, in batches collected and in possession of the National Archive, in Brasília and Rio de Janeiro, entirely sent by FAB. That without counting the procedures of this Force, regarding the process of collection, registration and archiving, with subsequent retrieval of the material to public archives. Such procedures are outlined in the Portaria 551/GC3 of August 9, 2010, published by the FAB and known among scholars of the subject and in specific media as the “OVNI Law.” However, despite the efforts demonstrated by the Brazilian Air Force, many issues raised by previous requests remain pending. Over time, seven years have passed since the responses to the last RIC-, and there is no longer the same willingness from the other branches, the Army and Navy, to provide data to interested citizens, as the same phenomenon that led FAB to adopt and publish its procedures for recording and filing occurs not only in the air space but also over and under Brazilian territorial waters, and its activities are also recorded on land, in the over 8.5 million km² of Brazilian territory, making it a matter to be addressed not by one but by the three branches of defense of the national territory. In particular, the justification for this Request is based on the pursuit of information regarding a specific case of significant national impact and global resonance, known in the media as "The Varginha ET Case" or, among ufologists, as "The Varginha Case," due to its occurrence in that Minas Gerais city in early 1996 and its press coverage that lasted for at least another year. This case is of unparalleled importance for several reasons, but two are of paramount importance to scientific knowledge and the transparency of public acts. First, because, according to ufologists,
it involves the crash of an unknown-technology UFO and the capture of at least two of its crew members
and, second, by the impressive operation to cover up the facts, for reasons that are still not very clear. Suspicions also lead to another serious conclusion, due to a possible breach of national sovereignty, embodied in the final destination of the wreckage of the crashed ship and the seized bodies, which, according to ufologists, according to the military involved, were taken to the United States of America, against the wishes of several officers, for obvious reasons. The lack of public information about the case, considered genuine by a large part of the population of Varginha, results in prejudice, ridicule, embarrassment, pain, and doubt among witnesses and relatives of those directly involved, such as the family of military police officer Marco Eli Chereze, who is said to have been a fatal victim of direct contact with one of the crew members. Under the LAI, which was sanctioned after the aforementioned RICs were answered, new questions about the procedure, especially from the Army, were raised. Since 2012, numerous requests have been made to the Electronic System of Citizen Information Service (e-SIC) of the Federal Government, all of which have been denied or fulfilled in a way that does not reveal what may remain classified. It is the case, for example, of the
strange absence to date, on the Army's website, of the Document Indexing Codes (CIDICs) containing Secret Information that were generated in the years 1996 and 1997. Provide Article 45, Section II of
Decree No. 7.724, one of the decrees that emerged to complement and give effect to LAI, that all
still classified documents have their identifications in code format made available in a specific list,
on the electronic pages of the public bodies responsible for them, by June 1st of each year. If these documents do indeed exist and were generated between 1996 and 1997, they show us a

an abundance of circumstantial and witness evidence; to remain classified, they must have been categorized at the time as ULTRASECRET, with a 25-year secrecy period. By the way, one of the main military witnesses in the Varginha Case categorically stated in a recorded deposition that the operation to transport the unknown biological entities, crewmembers of the crashed UFO, from the ESA to Campinas (Unicamp) on January 23, 1996, was treated as ultra-secret by the commanders and thus classified in that category. Thus, their records could only be available for public consultation on January 24, 2021, although the CIDIC that identifies it should already exist and be available to those interested. Now, if Decree 7,724 entered into force on May 16, 2012, why has the Army not yet made available in its "list of ultra-secret information" the CIDICs of this and other occurrences of the Varginha Case, six years after the LAI came into effect? In addition to this issue, it is noted that at the location designated for publishing the "list of classified and declassified information of the Army," with the address informacoes-classificadas-versao-3.pdf http://www.eb.mil.br/informacoes-classificadas-desclassificadas, there is no adherence to the suggestions outlined in the "Guide for Publishing the List of Classified and Declassified Information and Statistical Reports on the Access to Information Law," available in the e-SIC of the Ministry of Transparency and Control General of the Union (CGU), accessible at: http://www.acessoainformacao.gov.br/lai-para-sic/sic-apoio-orientacoes/guias-e-orientacoes/guia-informacoes-classificadas-versao-3.pdf. "classified information" area, it clearly states: "It is also recommended that the agency or entity
disclose the subject matter of the classified document, with the aim of increasing transparency regarding
its content, as well as allowing social control. It should be noted that the inclusion of the subject in the list of classified documents aids in identifying future references, as provided for in Article 30, II, of Law No. 12.527/2011. For that, the agency must inform the content of the document in the most comprehensive way possible, without, however, revealing the nature of the restricted information. This recommendation is simply ignored by the Army. It also draws attention to this list of classified documents as ultra-secret, where only those whose confidentiality periods have expired or in the previous year, or in the year of the list's publication, up to June 1st, are made public. Thus, as of June 1, 2017, the last update having been made in 2016, all ultra-secret documents were about to have their secrecy period expire, that is, those whose origin was recorded up to 1992, twenty-five years prior. There is none in this space that has been classified as top secret after 1992. It is also noted that all those classified in this category already have the suggested reclassification approved, that is, with twenty-five years of secrecy. There is no known classified document of the highest level of secrecy that has not been reclassified, let alone declassified after the LAI came into effect. If this logic persists, prioritizing the exception over the rule for the sake of secrecy, rather than the transparency recommended by the LAI, the first documents on the Varginha Case will only have their CIDICs (Confidentiality Identification Codes) released when their secrecy expires in 2021, and then reclassified, remaining hidden from society until 2046. Once again, we demand that public entities adhere to the Constitutional Principle of Publicity of Official Acts, Article 37 of the CF, particularly noting that maintaining secrecy around information regarding the events revealed here, this Request is of great public and scientific interest.
--- seg-9d68aa02beb036ba90551126 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Brasília, May 2, 2018.

JUSTIFICATION

===== PAGE 207 [page-41cf98968b78fa7eebf2c672] =====
--- seg-f065336a88b7b0a181d7db1d [needs-review] ---
May 2018                       DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                       Tuesday, May 15, 2018
--- seg-251ca1d34d4fe50303facacd [needs-review] ---
On the last day 21/03, parts of Brazil went dark due to a technical issue in the National Interconnected System – SIN, which, as investigated, resulted in the country's largest blackout in history.

This problem raises a necessary discussion about the process of privatization of the State Electric Sector. Various headlines failed to convey the issue, opening the door to all sorts of speculation, including by the then-mining and energy minister, Fernando Coelho, who, as we know, has little knowledge of the sector, see the news below: Mining and Energy Minister Fernando Coelho Filho stated that the blackout occurred after a failure at the Belo Monte power plant in Pará.

The Pará Electric Centers (Celpa) reported that a problem with energy generation at the Tucuruí power plant, in the northeast of the state, may have caused the blackout. (g1.globo.com - 21/03/2018 4:56 PM) According to information from industry representatives, the problem occurred at the Xingu Substation, at the output of the CC bipolar of the Belo Monte Transmissora de Energia - BMTE, which, contrary to what was initially reported, does not belong to Eletronorte and is not in Tucuruí.

Investigations revealed that during testing on the transmission line carrying 4GW of load, a failure occurred, causing the line to go offline, triggering a chain reaction. According to the National Operator of the Electric System (ONS), on its website, at 3:48 PM on 21/03/2018, a circuit breaker failed at the Xingu Substation in Pará. Consequently, several 500 kV transmission lines, components of the North/Northeast/Central-West trunk lines, Tucuruí/Manaus, Tucuruí/Vila do Conde, Xingu/Estreito 800 kV CC, and the Belo Monte UTE, among others, were automatically shut down, resulting in a total load reduction in the SIN of approximately 18,000 MW.

As seen, the state-owned company Eletronorte had no responsibility for the issue, as the Xingu Substation is operated and maintained by the Xingu Transmissora de Energia Lines concessionary (controlled by the Spanish group Isolux). The Xingu/Estreito 800 kV CC line is under the responsibility of BMTE (which built or is building a converter station at the Xingu Substation), BMTE is a concessionary of the State Grid group that aims to buy Eletrobras.

In light of this, we question the Ministry of Mines and Energy and the National Operator of the Electric System:

1. What was the extent of the incident?
2. What were the causes of the blackout?
3. Was the company conducting equipment tests at this time?
--- seg-496ec09b673487e4a54333a3 [needs-review] ---
4. What was the State Grid company's involvement in the mentioned blackout?
       5. What are the damages caused by the blackout in the affected cities?
       6. What was the duration of the blackout and the time for the system to return to normal?
        7. Has an investigation been initiated by ONI? Has it been completed? What is the result of the investigation?
       8. Which company is responsible for the Xingu substation? What is the date of the concession?
       9. I request from the National Electric System Operator the IPDO – Preliminary Daily Operation Report files for the years 2014, 2015, 2016, and 2017.
--- seg-1655d28703532208079be3c8 [needs-review] ---
Meeting Room, on __may_018__.

--- seg-abf87b68255698442508f833 [needs-review] ---

--- seg-8746f5698cefda2509f1be5d [machine-unreviewed] ---

Mr. President:
--- seg-07ffba184a3ca35fa1102389 [needs-review] ---
I request that Your Excellency review the decision that attached the Law Projects n° 6.814 and 7.228, 2017, to the Law Project n° 1.292, 1995, for the reasons outlined below.

===== PAGE 225 [page-2e79644b6f214bfaa986ca27] =====
--- seg-bcb20f3a177ae11193bea633 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                          HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                         Tuesday 15 225
--- seg-e625168e0328e58525b5c706 [needs-review] ---
In August 2017, the Presidency decided, in accordance with Article 34, II, of the Internal Regulation, to establish an Ad Hoc Committee to issue a report on Senate Federal Project of Law No. 6,814, 2017, which proposes “rules for public procurement and contracts and repeals Laws No. 8,666 of June 21, 1993, No. 10,520 of July 17, 2002, and certain provisions of Law No. 12,462 of August 4, 2011.”
--- seg-76b81e5f0b4608593beec7b2 [machine-unreviewed] ---
At that moment, the PL n° 7.228, 2017, which "regulates Article 37, XXI of the Federal Constitution, to establish general norms for the conduct of tenders and the conclusion of contracts in the scope of the Union, the States, the Federal District and the Municipalities, and provides for other measures," was already attached to the aforementioned bill. Both proposals share the objective of providing new regulation to Article 37, XXI of the Constitution and promoting a profound change in the norms on public tenders and contracts.
--- seg-ce8f3107a5299a7e62bc5b57 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Subsequently, in February of this year, the members were designated and the Commission was established, which came to be known in this House as the Commission for the New Procurement Law.
--- seg-ab802a18713e7c1c2aa9f940 [needs-review] ---
However, after the deliberative meetings of the Commission had begun, the Presiding Officer granted a request made by Dep. José Guimarães to attach the Bills n° 6.814, 2017 and n° 7.228, 2017 to Bill n° 1.292, 1995, and to change the name of the Commission as follows:
--- seg-1ba3a3e6c057dcdabd217bed [needs-review] ---
Attach Project Law n. 6.814/2017 to Project Law n. 1.292/1995. I therefore revisit the initial dispatch attached to Project of Law n. 292/1995,
                       to include examination by the Commission on Environment and Sustainable Development
                       and by the Commission on Economic Development, Industry, Trade, and Services. Also, change the name of the Special Commission of the Bill Project n. 6.814/2017 to refer to Bill Project n. 1.292/1995, which will head the block under consideration.
--- seg-d6208575f5b76c50fdb89a0b [machine-unreviewed] ---
Publish.
--- seg-e3448c2720903f96666c6a69 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Report it.
--- seg-c0a7dab099b2781f1cdfa50c [needs-review] ---
The joint processing of the proposals turns out to be inappropriate and does not meet the procedural assumptions. In fact, as decided in Order Issue No. 640, 2010, the Special Commissions provided for in Article 34, II, of the RICD, "are established with the specific purpose of issuing an opinion on a particular proposal or set of proposals appended to a legislative initiative, based on the matter contained therein, and it is not within the jurisdiction of these bodies to examine other proposals, besides that for which they were created."
--- seg-5bdc3084a0d234a4bf6bbf3e [machine-unreviewed] ---
The decision further added that admitting the attachment of other proposals "would constitute a measure tending to perpetuate the operation of a Special Commission, which is not compatible with its nature as a Temporary Commission, as classified in Article 33 of the RICD."
--- seg-325d79e4efff39e27840ae18 [needs-review] ---
The risk of becoming perennial is exactly what occurs in the hypothesis at hand. In fact, PL
no. 1,292, 1995, has 223 other proposals appended to it, and the joint processing of the matters could
become a significant obstacle to this Legislative House's proper consideration of the relevant and
urgent content of the New Procurement Law proposed by PL no. 6,814, 2017, so eagerly awaited by all involved sectors.

===== PAGE 226 [page-23a25ae99310143d60f159c1] =====
--- seg-6299a9145591292e8b4b26f0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
226 Tuesday, May 15                  DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-07170e2ca4e590542769e8e1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
On the other hand, it should be noted that the PL n° 1.292, of 1995, and its 223 appended documents, address specific issues within the broader topic of procurement and contracts, aiming to amend particular provisions of the existing legislation.
--- seg-ef3c65bc61f142b3208c61ec [needs-review] ---
Thus, the object and scope of the proposals are different: while the Law Project (PL) No. 1,292 of 1995 and its appended projects aim to amend specific points of procurement regulations, the Law Project (PL) No. 6,814 of 2017 presents a New Law on Procurement and Contracts, replacing the three main existing laws on the subject – namely, Law No. 8,666 of 1993 (Procurement Law), Law No. 10,520 of 2002 (Auction Law), and Law No. 12,462 of 2012 (Differentiated Contract Regime) – with a single, comprehensive norm, which will also introduce important innovations, such as the possibility of resolving disputes through arbitration and conciliation.
--- seg-bcfb549d136d1deb1de88d11 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Therefore, the fact that they have as a connecting element the reference to the generic term of public tenders and contracts should not, in itself, lead to the joint processing of the proposals.
--- seg-c2ad7bd094bcb9defb031118 [machine-unreviewed] ---
At this point, it is necessary to clarify that the Board of the Chamber of Deputies has already authorized requests for disassociation in similar situations, as seen in the acceptance of Request n° 4.763, 2012.
--- seg-1dab9ed0b42233376ac5ea44 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The repeal of PLs 6,814/2017 and 7,228/2017 will also ensure the much-needed speed in the handling of the matter, especially this year when lawmakers will also need to focus their efforts on elections.
--- seg-3e838f7ba8c4b51fb7a6c134 [needs-review] ---
For these reasons, supported by what was decided by the Presidency in the Order Issue No. 640, 2010, as well as in the Request No. 4,763, 2012, I request that the disassociation of the Bills No. 6,814 and 7,228, 2017, and Bill No. 1,292, 1995, be determined, and that the commission's name be changed to the Special Commission to Issue a Report on Bill No. 6,814, 2017.

BILL NO. 1.145-A, 2011
(Mr. Carlos Bezerra)
--- seg-c5ab96884b2b16c0826d1ca8 [needs-review] ---
Add Article 392-B to the Consolidation of Labor Laws to provide for maternity leave for women who work on crews of merchant marine vessels, river and lake navigation, port traffic, and fishing; with the opinion of the Commission on the Defense of Women's Rights, for approval with an amendment (relator: DEP. ANA PERUGINI).
--- seg-b9e5022aeac3218461f29e52 [machine-unreviewed] ---
NEW DISPATCH:
TO THE COMMITTEES OF:
WOMEN'S RIGHTS DEFENSE;
SOCIAL SECURITY AND FAMILY; AND
CONSTITUTION AND JUSTICE AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 OF RICD) -
--- seg-265103ae7be8ea83d1dfa816 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposal Subject to Final Review by the Committees - Art. 24 II
--- seg-a1379cf7e472e717e84e6307 [machine-unreviewed] ---
PUBLICATION OF THE OPINION OF THE
--- seg-166f4ee3b6ae1b8e167f61dd [machine-unreviewed] ---
WOMEN'S RIGHTS DEFENSE COMMISSION
--- seg-5394c34d2df06d2c462d0871 [machine-unreviewed] ---
I – REPORT
--- seg-0671d64f7507e77b089a0841 [needs-review] ---
The distinguished Deputy Carlos Bezerra presented to the House the proposal at hand, with the aim
of granting a one-hundred-eighty-day maternity leave to employees working on vessels' crews.
--- seg-0b67867d8f7a4f1191f7300b [needs-review] ---
The Project adds Article 392–B to the Consolidation of Labor Laws (CLT) to grant the benefit to pregnant women who work on crews of merchant marine vessels, river, lake, and port navigation vessels, as well as fishing vessels.
--- seg-6321dd82d92526ce5de364f1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
A license can occur at any time, starting seventy days before the delivery. The rest periods, before and after the delivery, can be extended by two weeks, depending on the presentation of a medical certificate to the employer.
--- seg-ec80c8f5b023e3ff49c6ad06 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The proposal also guarantees the employee's transfer to a different role when health conditions require it, and their return to the previous position with equivalent compensation to the average of the salaries received in the six months prior to the conception, and dismissal from work for the time needed to undergo at least six medical consultations and other complementary examinations.
--- seg-8f55316822b23cd762ff571a [machine-unreviewed] ---
No regulatory period, no amendments were presented.
--- seg-1dc1b8eda0382d9b1b53810e [machine-unreviewed] ---
This is the report.

===== PAGE 240 [page-07ee2dea193b6c2a3c5e0fed] =====
--- seg-874738a731219a8f723d070a [machine-unreviewed] ---
240 Tuesday, May 15                  DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-98e49ad9e64accd2dbfaf840 [machine-unreviewed] ---
II - REPORTER'S VOTE
--- seg-c7d25876ea7091c521e6fa36 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 392 of the CLT, currently in force, reads as follows:
--- seg-56c2889fb09767269c31bd72 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 392. A pregnant employee is entitled to a 120 (one hundred and twenty) day maternity leave, without prejudice to her job and salary.

§ 1. The employee, through a medical certificate, must notify her employer of the start date of her absence, which can occur between the 28th (twenty-eighth) day before the delivery and its occurrence.

§ 2. Rest periods before and after the delivery can be extended by 2 (two) weeks each, upon medical certificate.

§ 3. In case of premature delivery, the woman is entitled to the 120 (one hundred and twenty) days provided for in this article.

§ 4. During pregnancy, it is guaranteed to the employee, without prejudice to her salary and other rights:

I - Job transfer, when health conditions require it, ensuring the resumption of the previously held function immediately after returning to work (Insubstantial clause added by Law No. 9,799 of 5/26/1999);

II - Waiver of working hours for the time needed to attend at least six medical consultations and other complementary examinations.

§ 5. (PROHIBITED)
--- seg-595b50195c291fe4a8715a5d [needs-review] ---
It is observed that the initiative of the honorable Deputy Carlos Bezerra innovates labor legislation in favor of the onboard employee, extending the maternity leave period from 120 to 180 days. Other modifications such as the removal from work starting on the 70th day and the guarantee of the 180-day period in case of early termination are adaptations to the proposed extension of the total leave period.
--- seg-92298bd9b9d0818708581e56 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The extension of the maternity leave period to 180 days as mentioned in the bill is justified by the special working conditions of these employees. As the author informs us, "the job requires long displacements and constant exposure to dangers, and often the vessels remain distant from locations with adequate medical assistance." The author's statement is a notoria fact and does not require additional demonstrations or suggest controversies. Therefore, the differentiated treatment for those working in special conditions is justified in relation to the group of workers of the same category or similar. The proposed measure is in full accordance with the principles already enshrined in Article 392 of the CLT (Brazilian Labor Code) regarding the protection of maternity, family, and child.
--- seg-9b41f0b0c3a9cbec4786d220 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Another innovation mentioned in the Project's text concerns the guarantee of equivalent remuneration to the average salary received in the six months prior to conception in case of transfer.

===== PAGE 241 [page-9f413adfc755f077b3c7236b] =====
--- seg-1939ec17788335382f57bdfe [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                        HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                       Tuesday 15 241
--- seg-19a4abf7c93235ee42052156 [needs-review] ---
regarding the calculation of average salary during pregnancy. This point is, however, difficult to understand as the text states that the average should be calculated based on the conception. If the transfer of duties occurred during pregnancy, the salary to be paid cannot be based on the delivery, which has not yet taken place. Nevertheless, we only register our difficulty in reading the proposal at this specific point, as the Commission on Labor, Administration, and Public Service (CTASP) will undoubtedly conduct a more thorough analysis of the text to reconcile it with the entire labor legislation.
--- seg-5ab02fe1b02683a0b187b5ab [machine-unreviewed] ---
In the scope of what this Commission is entitled to analyze, we understand that the proposal has great social value and upholds the principles of protecting motherhood and women's work. In line with the idea proposed by the Project, we suggest an amendment to include fixed platforms in the text. The concept of the law does not encompass such vessels, only those being towed. Therefore, if the platform is fixed, the workers who perform their work there will not be included in this noble proposal.
--- seg-edeb481965f360bfdb045f88 [needs-review] ---
In light of the above, we advocate for the approval of House Bill No. 1.145, 2011, with the attached amendment.

PUBLICATION OF THE OPINION OF THE COMMISSION ON WOMEN'S RIGHTS

I - REPORT

The proposal being reported requires federal public agencies and entities to establish breastfeeding support rooms within their premises, enabling lactating servants to have adequate conditions for milking and storing their milk during working hours.
--- seg-2a4b9a9bea2625bddfdb08c4 [needs-review] ---
According to the proposal, breastfeeding support rooms should be installed in an appropriate area, with the necessary equipment and technical assistance, in accordance with Resolution RDC/Anvisa No. 171 of September 4, 2006, and the Joint Technical Note SAS/MS-ANVISA, drafted based on the aforementioned resolution.
--- seg-887df7848c0e7ed012cf13fa [machine-unreviewed] ---
The deadline for the new law to come into effect is one hundred and eighty days from the date of its publication.
--- seg-6d6b96deb567fb471644114e [needs-review] ---
The project was referred for merit review to the Commission on Labor, Administration, and Public Service (CTASP), which has already approved it, to this committee, and to the Commission on Social Security and Family (CSSF).

Subsequently, the Commission on Constitution, Justice, and Citizenship (CCJC) will need to issue a statement on its constitutionality, legality, and legislative technique.
--- seg-93b8dc29938d69bb6d2a1d37 [machine-unreviewed] ---
No amendments were offered to the proposal.
--- seg-f46f7b8f5b1c85e80f28781e [machine-unreviewed] ---
II - REPORTER'S VOTE
--- seg-e8b4b7bb56806ff75fe6431e [machine-unreviewed] ---
The importance of breastfeeding for a child's development is more than

===== PAGE 244 [page-722373ff02d52428f84df1df] =====
--- seg-494b9a2c2931a990e8155b45 [machine-unreviewed] ---
244 Tuesday, May 15                             CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                                  2018
--- seg-909408eb3842a2660700a86a [needs-review] ---
known. On the subject, the Ministry of Health states:
--- seg-4642da8d3bc93ccde31d2694 [needs-review] ---
"Breastfeeding is the most wise natural bonding, affection, protection, and nutrition strategy for the child, and it constitutes the most sensitive, economic, and effective intervention for reducing child morbidity and mortality." It also allows for a significant impact on promoting the holistic health of mother and baby, and joy for society as a whole. Breastfeeding is much more than just nourishing the child. It is a process that involves deep interaction between mother and child, with repercussions on the child's nutritional status, their ability to defend against infections, their physiology and cognitive and emotional development, and their long-term health, as well as having implications for the mother's physical and mental health."1
The World Health Organization and the Ministry of Health recommend exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months, followed by continued breastfeeding for two years or more. In the initial six months, employees have legally assured maternity leave. After that, there are no legal support instruments for employees who wish to continue breastfeeding.
--- seg-b64b4de58d05a02e47958de6 [needs-review] ---
As noted in the justification of the proposal, nursing mothers who must leave their children for work need to express their breasts during the daily routine to relieve discomfort and maintain milk production. However, in order for milk to be extracted during working hours, it is necessary for the woman to have a suitable place to perform the milking and storage of the milk. In most cases, this location is not available. Therefore, at a good time, the requirement for the installation of breastfeeding rooms in federal public institutions is being discussed. Furthermore, it should be noted that this is a provision of easy implementation and low cost, as the furniture and equipment required basically consist of a collection chair, a sink, and a freezer. In some cases, public agencies and entities will only need to relocate these equipment to an appropriate location. With a quiet and properly equipped environment, women who wish to continue breastfeeding can extract and store their own milk during their working hours. At the end of the workday, they can take the collected milk to their child or even donate it to a milk bank. We understand, however, that in respect of the principle of equality and as a measure of justice,
the bill currently under review should have its scope expanded to ensure this breastfeeding support
structure for women who work in the private sector, as well as for state and municipal servants,
which is why we have decided to present an alternative. We also note what the rapporteur of the matter pointed out in the CTASP regarding:
1. Basic Attention Notebooks - Child Health - Breastfeeding and Complementary Feeding - 2015.

DISPATCH:
TO THE COMMITTEES OF:
FINANCE AND TAXATION (MERIT AND ART. 54, RICD) AND CONSTITUTION AND JUSTICE AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 RICD)
--- seg-714b549425f24bc7e16527cb [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposal Subject to Final Review by the Committees - Art. 24 II
--- seg-1d581c7f01d6019fad0873f5 [machine-unreviewed] ---
PUBLICATION OF THE OPINION OF THE COMMITTEE ON FINANCE AND TAXATION
--- seg-391113e68f34e82cdc553782 [machine-unreviewed] ---
I - REPORT
--- seg-e1bff3838dc73af8fecd423c [needs-review] ---
House Bill No. 3.613, 2012, adds paragraph 5 to Article 12 of Law No. 8.177. 1991, to determine that savings accounts with balances exceeding R$ 50,000 be remunerated exclusively at a rate corresponding to eighty percent of the interest rate corresponding to the SELIC rate, applying- if for deposits made after the entry into force of the law derived from the approval of the proposal.
--- seg-4e062c59955ceb2cbd578670 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The author of the proposal noted in his justification that, under the legislation in force at the time the matter was presented, deposits were remunerated at a fixed interest rate of 0.5% per month – equivalent to 6.17% per year – applied to updated values based on the TR (Reference Rate). At that time, an undesirable asymmetry was observed between the remuneration of the savings account and other investments. The savings returns, combined with the other benefits of this investment mode, made it more attractive, leading to massive transfers of resources and causing significant distortions in the credit offer.

A proposal to remunerate at a rate equivalent to 80% of the SELIC (Central Bank Interest Rate) would thus, according to the proposer, achieve greater balance between the various types of investments and institutions, protecting small savers from the proposed changes.

The matter, subject to the final consideration of the Committees and in ordinary procedure, should be examined by this Committee regarding aspects related to budget and financial compatibility and adequacy, and on the merits, as no amendments were presented. It will then be forwarded to the Commission on Constitution and Justice and Citizenship.
--- seg-adccb735d6960c5745feffc1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
No amendments were offered within the regulatory timeframe.
                  This is the report.

===== PAGE 248 [page-014d41f9c255550390c4a5d9] =====
--- seg-06860ad2f7a75e0c91afa6d2 [machine-unreviewed] ---
248 Tuesday, May 15                         DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                                    2018
--- seg-3dad88348117afa3f48fcf73 [needs-review] ---
II - RELATOR'S VOTE
 
This Committee, in preliminary examination of the merits, is to assess the present proposal regarding its compatibility or appropriateness with the multi-annual plan, the Budget Guidelines Law, and the annual budget, in accordance with the Rules of Procedure of the Chamber of Deputies (RI, art. 53, II).
--- seg-33957e6b98281735de5702d5 [needs-review] ---
The bill proposes that savings accounts with balances exceeding fifty thousand reais be remunerated exclusively by a fee corresponding to eighty percent of the interest rate equivalent to the reference rate Selic. The matter it addresses has no impact on the Union Budget, as it is essentially normative in character, with no direct effect on public revenue or expenditure.

As for the merits, the situation is quite different, given the inconveniences of approving the measure addressed in the bill for the reasons outlined below. Furthermore, we believe that at this moment, the approval of this bill would imply a disregard for principles that should guide the legal order, as well as action by the agents responsible for lawmaking and normative development.

The proposal introduces changes to the rules governing savings1, with the aim of encouraging the saver (with a savings account balance exceeding fifty thousand reais) to consider other types of investment, such as those backed by public debt securities, among others.

It is worth noting that one month after the presentation of the aforementioned bill, the Executive Branch issued MP No. 567, of May 3, 2012, converted into Law No. 12,703, of August 7, 2012. The current legislation establishes that savings account balances will be remunerated by the TR (Reference Rate) plus seventy percent of the Selic rate target, provided that the said rate does not exceed 8.5% per annum. In practice, the savings account, which previously had a monthly valuation of 0.5% plus the Reference Rate (TR), now yields seventy percent of Selic plus the TR. When the Selic rate exceeds 8.5% per annum, the savings remuneration returns to TR plus 0.5% per month.2
--- seg-74c89ac3d23ec21397ac5c2a [needs-review] ---
The formula above contemplates a ratio between the savings remuneration and the Selic rate, at least up to a certain amount. With this, it provides the necessary market balance for other fixed-income securities, by reducing the risk of capital flight from other investments, including public debt securities issued by the National Treasury, which are equally important for the financial market and the financing of investments in the country. This is a significant decision, especially as the current economic scenario, in relation to the trajectory of the benchmark interest rate, currently at 8.25% per annum, is quickly approaching that observed at the time the matter was presented, which coexisted with an interest rate of 7.25% per annum. With
--- seg-e5fba24722745f3bd7e863a5 [needs-review] ---
1 Investing in savings remains the preference of 76% of Brazilians, according to a survey by the Federation of Commerce of
--- seg-a91bb7e5f25f3fa885a4f016 [needs-review] ---
In the state of Rio de Janeiro, in 2016.
It appears that this preference is explained because it is very easy to make applications and redemptions through it, not to mention that the modality
offers low risk and tax-free financial returns, in addition to protection by the Credit Guarantee Fund (FGC).
2 The savings rule changed with the issuance of MP No. 567, of May 3, 2012, when the savings rate was 9% and the
--- seg-8968b737d38f27fed16e4930 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The government of Dilma Rousseff intended to lower them even further. At the time, without the changes made to the savings account, the drop could have compromised the issuance of public bonds by the National Treasury, which are used as loans for the government, as well as other fixed-income investments.

===== PAGE 249 [page-861c11d41d5ee6b1ab5d1171] =====
--- seg-40c2ccd406629418e1bcbbf9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                        HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                      Tuesday 15 249
--- seg-b10d51647b81c80fb55d23e4 [needs-review] ---
in this scenario, with each 1 percentage point cut in the economy's basic interest rate, the Selic, the Monetary Policy Committee (COPOM) triggers the savings account profitability trigger, which then pays less interest whenever Selic is equal to or below 8.5%. Financial market experts also argue that the savings account interest rate should track the movement of the benchmark interest rate, even paying lower rates due to its lower risk compared to government bonds, and because its returns are exempt from income tax and financial operations tax, as well as having the protection of the Credit Guarantee Fund (FGC).
--- seg-ede50f28e741944c1126617e [machine-unreviewed] ---
On the other hand, since the savings account had a fixed return in the past that
did not keep pace with the decline in interest rates, even in a context of consistent interest rate cuts,
as we are observing, with the maintenance of the formula prior to Law No. 12,703 of 2012, the application
in savings deposit accounts would become very attractive, relative to other fixed-income investment
alternatives, such as bank deposit certificates (CDBs) and investment funds, which could lead to a
significant increase in the flow of resources to this modality. The insensitivity of the savings account
return to lower interest rates would thus impose a nearly unbearable burden on borrowers of
residential mortgages, who would not see their rates reduced, even in a scenario where the basic
interest rate of the economy is on a downward trajectory.
--- seg-bd3231d0ef01472ebb35b7da [needs-review] ---
Thus, considering the scenario of reduced liquid capture of savings, which has as a consequence the reduction of values allocated for real estate financing, the eventual approval of the bill, which provides for only 80% of the base interest rate to be savings, in a scenario where the Selic rate tends to remain around 7% per annum in the coming months, could to bring even worse effects on savings performance, compared to the rule set by Law No. 12. 703/2012 causing damage, even in the real estate market.
--- seg-51d5af54831d3e029d1b3971 [needs-review] ---
In conclusion, in our opinion, the Law Project No. 3,613, of 2012, is no longer
appropriate for the current economic situation. The motivation that guided his presentation no longer holds in light of the subsequent approval of Law No. 12,703 of 2012, which ultimately found a more balanced formula for those who allocate their resources in savings accounts, for economic agents operating in the real estate market, and no less important, for borrowers in the housing finance system. In view of the above, we vote against the implication of the proposition in a decrease in revenue or an increase in public expenditure, and there is no need to comment on its financial and budgetary appropriateness. In substance, we voted against the rejection of Bill No. 3.613, of 2012.
--- seg-5e9ac3f467f3714ff7d2e6b3 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Commission Room, November 1st, 2017.
--- seg-f3e7e1811e795ab2f8a46d73 [needs-review] ---

I - REPORT
--- seg-892718e0a207fe881361ea8e [needs-review] ---
Bill No. 7,171, 2014, authored by the distinguished Deputy Mendonça Filho, addresses
the identification of donations and monetary contributions made to natural persons, in campaigns of any
nature or purpose, except those of an electoral nature. From reading the justification of the proposal, it becomes apparent that there is a concern regarding the fact that "the domestic legal framework allows for donations in cash to be made during campaigns of any nature or purpose, without the need to identify the donor, thus preventing any form of state control, and in particular, tax authority oversight." In order to fulfill the objective of allowing for the precise identification of the parts and elements of the donations, the proposal, in its Article 2, determines the opening of a specific bank account for the registration of donations made in favor of the beneficiary, as well as the obligation for banks to identify, in the statements of the respective current account, the donor, with the annotation of the registration number in the Individual Taxpayer's Register (CPF) or in the National Register of Legal Entities (CNPJ), as applicable. The sole paragraph of Article 2 further provides that the extract referred to above, upon request, shall be made available, regardless of judicial authorization. In turn, Article 3 of the proposal establishes the possibility of using, for receiving the donations and contributions referred to in Article 1, a mechanism available on a dedicated website that allows the use of a credit card. Under the terms of the provision, donations must meet two requirements, enumerated in paragraphs: identification of the debtor in the format provided in Article 2 and issuance of a receipt for each donation made.

===== PAGE 252 [page-726e9d493e9084560e79ae8b] =====
--- seg-7c154b88af6a5730a0106de1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
252 Tuesday, May 15                  DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-6475162313c21e83e216e208 [needs-review] ---
Finally, Article 4 determines that the donations and contributions addressed by the law comply with
the provisions of specific legislation, including with regard to accessory tax obligations, without prejudice
to the payment of taxes and other charges due. By order of the Chamber of Deputies' desk, the matter was referred to the Commission on Finance and Taxation (CFT) for analysis of the merits and budgetary and financial appropriateness, and to the Commission on Constitution and Justice and Citizenship (CCJC) for constitutional and legal analysis. In the CFT, no amendments to the bill were presented within the regulatory timeframe. This is the report.
--- seg-3957477438dc3eeeb30cc6d2 [machine-unreviewed] ---
II - REPORTER'S VOTE
--- seg-dcea2bd65c79913a42940239 [machine-unreviewed] ---
In accordance with Article 32, X, "h" of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, this Committee is responsible for examining the "financial and budgetary aspects of any proposals that result in an increase or decrease in public revenue or expenditure, regarding their compatibility or appropriateness with the multi-annual plan, the budget guidelines law, and the annual budget."
--- seg-3a3bde4e2ceab642247d6b02 [needs-review] ---
The project under review regulates the procedures applicable to donations and contributions made to natural persons, except those of an electoral nature. The article there dealt with is limited to establishing the criteria to be followed by the beneficiary and the donor to ensure a higher degree of transparency for these operations. As stated by the proposal author in their justification, the initiative aims to inhibit illegal donations that could fraud the tax system or enable shady operations, providing constituted powers with new control tools. Regarding the merits, following the opinion presented to this Commission by Deputy Edmar Arruda, we initially note that donations constitute a taxable event under state jurisdiction, the Inheritance and Gift Tax (ITCMD), and thus states can provide for the disclosure of information regarding such transactions to the competent authorities. Furthermore, the beneficiary, in his/her income tax declaration, a federal tax, must inform the Federal Revenue about any potential asset increases resulting from a donation. It is possible, however, as Deputy Edmar Arruda himself pointed out, that these primary and secondary tax obligations may not be met, making it relevant to initiate new forms of control over donations.

===== PAGE 253 [page-2e88dfd42f2842df12dea6e2] =====
--- seg-171e6b7890aa82c3ed4b7c55 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                       JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         Tuesday, May 15, 253
--- seg-d1af0c08c58bd754d54a96db [needs-review] ---
That, in our view, justifies the matter being addressed in other legal spheres beyond the tax realm. Mechanisms need to be created to ensure monitoring of donations made to campaigns. Furthermore, I emphasize that the approval of the bill under review will fill a normative gap. Since the Civil Code allows for donations without specifying the use of the donated funds, campaigns could be financed in an unclear manner through these so-called "donations without burden." In other words, someone who wants to donate to a specific campaign could use the figure of a "donation without burden" to implicitly link the donated resources to the campaign, without explicitly stating their intentions.
--- seg-aa4486df888f8946feb5f144 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The approval of a law that establishes stricter rules for making donations linked to campaigns of any kind fills this gap and facilitates the oversight of such donations.
--- seg-abb7e0b744b7ace735134a5f [needs-review] ---
For these reasons, we voted in favor of the budgetary and financial adequacy of the Law Project No. 7,171, of 2014; and, on the merits, for its approval.

II - VOTE
--- seg-aebad00aa5d087cfc696a091 [machine-unreviewed] ---
It is up to this Committee to assess the proposal for its compatibility or appropriateness with the multi-annual plan, the Budget Guidelines Act, and the annual budget, in accordance with the Rules of the House of Deputies (RI, art. 53, II) and the Internal Norms of the Commission on Finance and Taxation of May 29, 1996, which "establishes procedures for examining budgetary and financial compatibility or appropriateness."
--- seg-a01dfe1702315d3095131b42 [needs-review] ---
According to the Internal Regulation, only those proposals that "entail an increase or decrease in public revenue or expenditure" are subject to examination for financial and budgetary suitability or adequacy. In this regard, Article 9 of the Internal Norms, approved by the CFT on 29.05.96, states:
--- seg-7d08178728524bbe6b6b5216 [machine-unreviewed] ---
"Article 9. When the matter does not have budgetary and financial implications, the final vote should conclude that it is not within the Commission's scope to affirm whether the proposal is appropriate or not."
--- seg-e6260537ee9344db2ebfcae7 [needs-review] ---
As previously stated, the PL No. 3.446/2015 proposes to amend Law No. 7.827/1989 to establish that the Constitutional Funds FNO, FNE, and FCO should allocate at least 20% of their total resources to productive activities of mini and small rural producers and micro and small businesses.
--- seg-0e19534e93ee5632769dcee5 [needs-review] ---
From the perspective of budgetary and financial appropriateness, it can be said that setting a minimum percentage (20%) for allocating the total resources of FNO, FNE, and FCO to productive activities for mini and small rural producers and micro and small businesses will not in itself increase the expenditure projections for these Funds.
--- seg-e74eae99fe292f72bf7bd38d [needs-review] ---
Thus, by analyzing PL No. 3.446/2015, we verify that its approval would not affect federal public expenses, as it would not produce an increase in the overall volume of public resources allocated to these Funds and, consequently, in overall expenses planned in the Annual Budget Law.
--- seg-7bce4a04be533d0ed4bf3d97 [needs-review] ---
In light of the above, I vote against implicating an increase or decrease in public revenue or expenditure for Project of Law No. 3,446, 2015, and there is no need to comment on its financial and budgetary appropriateness.

It concerns the practice of the profession of Ceremonialist and its related activities; with the opinion of the Commission on Labor, Administration and Public Service, for approval with a substitute (relator: DEP. WALNEY ROCHA).
--- seg-2106aa4828338a1d115027f8 [machine-unreviewed] ---
MEMORANDUM:
TO THE COMMITTEES OF:

--- seg-14f18176149e869beb6c4444 [needs-review] ---
REVIEW:
Proposal Subject to Final Review by the Committees - Art. 24 II
--- seg-f77488043286f814e592d76b [machine-unreviewed] ---
PUBLICATION OF THE OPINION OF THE
--- seg-1c8f1025d3511f3e56d0c508 [machine-unreviewed] ---
WORK, ADMINISTRATION, AND PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
--- seg-91ddf5e27acf19d86010cc56 [machine-unreviewed] ---
I – REPORT
--- seg-e87a5b516184fdd8e7710a0a [needs-review] ---
Bill No. 5,455 of 2016 establishes requirements for the practice of the professions of
ceremonialist, ceremonial technician, and ceremonial assistant (Articles 2 to 5) and lists the activities
and duties of these professionals (Article 6). Ensure to the responsible professional for the plan, project, or program the right to accompany its execution and implementation to guarantee its accomplishment according to the conditions, specifications, and technical details established (Article 7). Finally, limits the working time of these professionals to a maximum of forty hours per week, allowing for the compensation of hours and the reduction of the working day, through collective bargaining or agreement (Article 8).
--- seg-bc8f0c227bee77e5b4899e27 [needs-review] ---
The proposal, subject to the conclusive consideration by the Commissions in the ordinary procedure, was distributed to the Commission on Labor, Administration and Public Service (CTASP) for merit consideration and to the Commission on Constitution and Justice and Citizenship (CCJC) for analysis regarding constitutionality, legality, and legislative technique.
--- seg-ac03c3f8f4529e10670e1ec6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Upon receiving the project in CTASP and being designated as rapporteur, no amendments were presented within the regulatory timeframe.
--- seg-4aaf0b5a00afaa029031c341 [machine-unreviewed] ---
This is the report.
--- seg-b9924aca4e04c6033409d0a9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
II - REPORTER'S VOTE
--- seg-7dbe2d26dcdc0a6634b6939e [machine-unreviewed] ---
As mentioned by the author of the project, ceremonial professionals have gained importance, which justifies the creation of a specific law to regulate their activities and grant them rights. In this context, we highlight the significance of articles 6, 7, and 8 of the project.
--- seg-57a722f31522f3c5d5b5c724 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 6 deals with professional activities and duties.
--- seg-9e838d878f8a5b8a4bc718a1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 7 ensures the right of the professional responsible for a plan, project, or program to

===== PAGE 260 [page-a90a45eeffb3776943bb7c36] =====
--- seg-3fe5d6eb8d5ec2d08ebf48b0 [machine-unreviewed] ---
260 Tuesday, May 15                   JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                              2018
--- seg-6b89ee03f69132c7b542e902 [machine-unreviewed] ---
to monitor its execution and implementation to ensure it is carried out in accordance with the conditions, specifications, and technical details established. This rule, due to its importance in promoting service quality, is not only a right of the professional but also a measure to protect the recipients of the services.
--- seg-c79ceb4bf9e2937d89c5844c [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 8 deals with the working hours of these professionals, establishing a maximum limit of 40 (forty) hours of work per week, which is deemed suitable for the activities developed.
--- seg-d0f7fd914269914a8a936f50 [machine-unreviewed] ---
However, regarding Articles 2 to 5 of the draft, which deal with training requirements, we understand that they impose unjustifiable restrictions on the freedom of professional practice, a right enshrined in Article 5, inciso XIII, of the Constitution of the Republic, which states: "The free exercise of any work, trade, or profession is guaranteed, in accordance with the qualifications established by law."
--- seg-ea39aaa23afe0637c4b72f1b [needs-review] ---
The aforementioned constitutional provision allows the law to establish professional qualification requirements for certain activities. However, this is only justified in professions that involve serious risks to society. In this regard, it is the understanding established by the Federal Supreme Court, and for the same reasons, several proposals for regulating professions without this potential harm have been vetoed by the President of the Republic. That is what we verified, for example, in Veto Total Message No. 289 of 2015,
regarding the bill to regulate the practice of interior decorator, and in Veto Total Message No. 444 of 2015,
regarding the bill to regulate the professional practice of designer.
--- seg-2cf0434fd71f20a97d4fe12e [machine-unreviewed] ---
Regarding ceremonial activities, we understand that their practice does not pose a risk to society to justify the restrictions provided for in the bill. Therefore, we have drafted an alternative that includes ceremonialists to ensure them rights, but excludes the establishment of the requirements addressed in articles 2 to 5 of the bill.
--- seg-b74a920a4b823532426d999d [machine-unreviewed] ---
As a result of this, given that the elimination of the requirements removes the need to differentiate professionals into ceremonialist, technician, and ceremonial assistant, the substitute deals generically with the profession of ceremonialist, which encompasses all those who perform the activities related to it.
--- seg-5ab5733c427a51933b81cfdc [needs-review] ---
In light of the above, we vote in favor of approving House Bill No. 5.455, 2016, in the form of the attached substitute.
--- seg-d37a59019a7ec570fa6ccda8 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Commission Room, December 8, 2017.
--- seg-ffc4547cac2c36f30a1ce508 [needs-review] ---
Deputado WALNEY ROCHA

Regulates the profession of archaeologist and provides other measures; with the opinion of the Commission on Labor, Administration, and Public Service, for approval, with a substitute (relator: DEP. WALNEY ROCHA).
--- seg-fc80a5041edc132cb7ca32fd [machine-unreviewed] ---

REVIEW:
Proposal Subject to Final Review by the Committees - Art. 24 II
--- seg-057de6970294dfd21e2965af [needs-review] ---
PUBLICATION OF THE OPINION OF THE COMMITTEE ON LABOR, ADMINISTRATION, AND PUBLIC SERVICE
I - REPORT
This Draft Law, from the distinguished Deputy Laura Carneiro, aims to regulate the practice of the profession of archaeologist. The matter was previously reported by Congresswoman Maria Helena. We take the liberty of transcribing partially your report. The proposal has seven chapters divided into 35 articles:
--- seg-9ce3c8d5d89783468ab7cd90 [needs-review] ---
"The first and last deal, respectively, with preliminary arrangements and transitional provisions." The preliminary (art. 1st) merely specifies that the object of the profession of archaeologist consists in performing archaeological activities in any of its activities. The preliminary provisions (arts. 34 and 35) address rules concerning the provisional registration, to be carried out by the Ministry of Labor, until the effective installation of the Councils and the establishment of a rule for the beginning of the norm's validity. Chapter II deals with the profession of archaeologist. Article 2 defines who is qualified for the exclusive practice of the profession. Among them are those with degrees in
                       Archaeology, either from Brazil or abroad with titles validated, postgraduates in areas of
                       concentration related to archaeology with at least 2 (two) consecutive years of scientific
                       activities in the professional field of Archaeology; graduates in other courses who can
                       demonstrate scientific activities in the field of archaeology for a period of not less than 5
                       (five) consecutive years or 10 (ten) years in between; and those who, at the time of the law's
                       promulgation, can prove having completed an archaeology specialization and at least 3
                       (three) consecutive years of scientific activities in Archaeology. Article 3 defines the duties of archaeologists. Among them, we can mention: planning, organizing, managing, directing, and supervising archaeological research activities; identifying, recording, prospecting, excavating, and conducting site surveys; performing analysis, classification, interpretation, and information services.

===== PAGE 265 [page-6d9d870cd0035bb3d9833b45] =====
--- seg-083020e3906a572e496ad963 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                HOUSE OF DEPUTIES DAILY JOURNAL                           Tuesday 15 265
--- seg-0056a6c90b71d51e7d21fda1 [needs-review] ---
archaeological scientist; ensure the proper implementation of legislation regarding archaeological activities in the country; coordinate, lead, supervise, and manage archaeological sectors in government institutions, both direct and indirect, as well as in private organizations; and provide consulting and advisory services in the field of archaeology. Article 4 determines that technical positions in Archaeology in the direct and indirect public administration and in private companies must be filled obligatorily by archaeologists, ensuring the holding of a public contest (Article 5). Article 7 conditions professional practice to registration with the Regional Archaeology Council and the Regional Labor Delegation. The registration will be made upon request from the interested party, accompanied by the documents listed in Article 8. Private entities and public or private institutions, as per Article 9, also need to be registered with the Federal Archaeology Council to engage in activities in this professional field. Chapter III deals with Federal and Regional Councils, a topic that has the greatest extent within the Project. The devices are contained in three sections. The first section, articles 10 to 15, deals with the establishment of the Councils and their common rules of operation. The second section, articles 16 to 18, regulates the Federal Council. The third section, which comprises articles 19 to 21, regulates the composition, duties, and budgets of the Regional Councils. Chapter IV deals with professional practice. Articles 22 to 26 condition the exercise of the profession to the presentation of a professional registration issued by the respective Council as a condition for labor contracts (art. 22), an act conditioned to the presentation of the documents listed in art. 23. Penalties for non-compliance with the provisions of the draft law will be regulated by the internal regulations of the Councils (art. 24), and there is a prohibition (art. 25) for any public, autonomous, para-state, mixed economy, or private entity to carry out activities without adhering to the principles of Archaeology and without the effective hiring of archaeologists. Article 26 establishes the duty of cooperation by Trade Unions and Professional Associations of Archaeology with the Professional Councils. Chapter V deals with issues pertaining to liability and authorship and
               comprises articles 27 to 32. Article 27 makes the identification of field research through visible plates mandatory. Article 28 reserves the copyright for the professional who elaborates the plan, project, or program of Archaeology, and Article 29 stipulates that only the author may alter the work they have produced. In the case of multiple authors (art. 30) and scientific teams (art. 32), the right to co-authorship and the right/duty to accompany the execution of all stages (art. 31) are guaranteed.

===== PAGE 266 [page-581eb11609782e687b8a513a] =====
--- seg-0b19daca889d5e1c6abd2cd8 [machine-unreviewed] ---
266 Tuesday, May 15                   JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-f3392ce907f2236d134605b4 [needs-review] ---
Chapter VI contemplates a general provision (art. 33) that establishes the obligation of Brazilian professionals to participate in a proportion that at least matches half the number of foreign archaeologists active when there is a foreign archaeological expedition or mission. Justifying the measure, the author argues that although our country has around 6,000 archaeological sites, the professional practice of archaeology has not yet been regulated. The pressure for urban expansion and the "need to preserve and rescue past cultural manifestations" indicate that it is necessary to strengthen the professional action of archaeologists. The bill is proceeding through regular procedure and is subject to final review by the Commissions on Labor, Administration and Public Service (CTASP), Finance and Taxation, and Constitution and Citizenship."

Within CTASP, as the regulatory deadline of August 30, 2016, passed, no amendments were presented.
--- seg-b47f8c1f8c754a9783433ff3 [machine-unreviewed] ---
This is the report.
--- seg-3fd7284ddbb15e8a317d6bb7 [needs-review] ---
II - RELATOR'S VOTE
                  As noted in the justification for the bill, the national cultural heritage, consisting of approximately six thousand archaeological sites, is regulated by a single law, Law No. 3,294 of 1961, which considers them property of the Union.
--- seg-e3ec64789f3f6ddff6cc0648 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The exploration, study, and maintenance of this cultural heritage are of unparalleled importance and require the actions of archaeologists, technically skilled professionals, instrumentalized to look into the past and seek still-preserved answers within it.
--- seg-6f0c53fd276e812ae130e867 [machine-unreviewed] ---
It strikes us as strange that such a profession is still not regulated and that access to archaeological sites is not preferably carried out under the effective exclusive supervision of these professionals.
--- seg-b7cd7b9bdc3ac28363db92f6 [needs-review] ---
We cannot forget that archaeological sites are not only exposed to depredation due to unauthorized access, but also subject to the pressures of urbanization that intensified in the mid-20th century.
--- seg-49d6e871ed8386230e906689 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The valorization of professionals and the defense of archaeological cultural heritage are sufficient reasons to recommend the approval of the matter.
--- seg-8d5814be8a09e62a457f0f15 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The project, however, presents some unconstitutionalities and legislative difficulties that need to be addressed. The profession of archaeologist is a function eminently linked to the protection of public heritage. We are unaware, and during the elaboration, our efforts to find any private explorations of archaeological sites were frustrated. There are scientific consultancy services in Archaeology, but there are no business enterprises of archaeological sites.

===== PAGE 267 [page-0f4f3e6089adf5548b1f28bc] =====
--- seg-e65901474eb431aeceed6c0d [needs-review] ---
May 2018                         CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                          Tuesday, May 15, 2018, 267
--- seg-51551dd8b70ba6c8a16f2afb [needs-review] ---
In this regard, we understand that regulating a professional activity, particularly linked to state activities, poses risks to the organization of documentation centers, historical or geographical, organized by other entities within the Federation. The management of these assets can interfere
with the organization of state or municipal services, and federal legislation has limitations regarding
the organization of public services of states and municipalities.
--- seg-f9d2b49f9f39463941b64108 [needs-review] ---
The establishment of a Federal Archaeology Council, as well as the subsequent oversight of professional registration and private or public entities, is clearly unconstitutional. Chapter III and other articles dealing with professional registration cannot stand unless initiated by the Executive Branch.
--- seg-806c51342515c362c144e348 [needs-review] ---
In light of what has been presented, we advocate for the approval of the Law Project No. 5,456, of 2016,
in the form of the attached Substitute.
--- seg-232901c2d6c8e4e8998e9e11 [machine-unreviewed] ---

CHAPTER I

OF THE PROFESSION OF ARCHAEOLOGIST
--- seg-4271e7f95c426bc5a93d1d98 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 1: This law regulates the practice of the profession of Archaeologist throughout the national territory.
--- seg-fc48bee0bcff7063eca2f02f [machine-unreviewed] ---
Art. 2º O The practice of the profession of archaeologist is exclusive:
--- seg-6558b381867a8f06134b3f39 [needs-review] ---
I - holders of a Bachelor's degree in Archaeology from official or recognized institutions by the Ministry of Education;
--- seg-22e59cb8684d28d457420f19 [machine-unreviewed] ---
II - of graduates in Archaeology from foreign schools recognized by the laws of their country of origin, whose degrees have been validated in Brazil, in accordance with the relevant legislation;
--- seg-1bfb0c99ac778b185894de80 [needs-review] ---
III - of post-graduate students from schools or courses properly recognized by the Ministry of Education, with a concentration in Archaeology, with a master's thesis or doctoral dissertation on Archaeology, and with at least 2 (two) consecutive years of scientific activities.

the professional field of Archaeology, duly proven;

have at least 5 (five) consecutive years or 10 (ten) intermittent years of experience in engaging in
scientific activities in the field of Archaeology;
--- seg-e73183ead1f3e9c0c0fad79c [needs-review] ---
V - those who, as of the date of signing this Law, have completed specialized courses in
archaeology recognized by the Ministry of Education, with at least 3 (three) consecutive years of
scientific activities specific to the professional field of archaeology, duly proven.

SUBSTITUTE ADOPTED BY CTASP TO BILL PROJECT #5.456, 2016
--- seg-2afa8bff45845029baf20083 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Regulates the practice of the profession of Archaeologist.
--- seg-4208f117bb7fa62338baaf77 [machine-unreviewed] ---
The National Congress decrees:
--- seg-4d8e5351ec5fd49b419d77fe [machine-unreviewed] ---
CHAPTER I

OF THE PROFESSION OF ARCHAEOLOGIST
--- seg-1de5c837cbfbba54f1fbb119 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 1: This law regulates the practice of the profession of Archaeologist throughout the national territory.
--- seg-06b7358e990c397f798de546 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Art. 2º O The practice of the profession of archaeologist is exclusive:
--- seg-68a8b685b3d722a92c23b318 [needs-review] ---
I - holders of a Bachelor's degree in Archaeology from official or recognized institutions by the Ministry of Education;
--- seg-6da6da51912bff5a38e33db1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
II - of graduates in Archaeology from foreign schools recognized by the laws of their country of origin, whose degrees have been validated in Brazil, in accordance with the relevant legislation;
--- seg-254ba9851c5690ebefdcbc01 [needs-review] ---
III - of post-graduate degrees from schools or courses properly recognized by the Ministry of Education, with a concentration in Archaeology, with a master's thesis or doctoral dissertation on Archaeology, and with at least 2 (two) consecutive years of scientific activities in the field of Archaeology, properly documented;
--- seg-55f8c1eded3f6c577c92a11c [machine-unreviewed] ---
IV - of graduates from other higher education courses who, as of the date of signing this Law,
have at least 5 (five) consecutive years or 10 (ten) intermittent years of experience in engaging in
scientific activities in the field of Archaeology;

===== PAGE 272 [page-33c7c71bdcd7188f83db7f63] =====
--- seg-8b12d4bbf2b4477199d7842c [machine-unreviewed] ---
272 Tuesday, May 15                  DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         2018
--- seg-f4bf04f3b1a7abc69147118b [needs-review] ---
V - those who, as of the date of signing this Law, have completed specialized courses in
archaeology recognized by the Ministry of Education, with at least 3 (three) consecutive years of
scientific activities specific to the professional field of archaeology, duly proven.
--- seg-f690851aadd6ed7290d9a1a3 [machine-unreviewed] ---
§ 1. The verification referred to in items IV and V shall be conducted by the contracting authority or company.
--- seg-a3e21c5aeea1a223c7ea320c [machine-unreviewed] ---
§ 2º O The proof period referred to in the previous paragraph shall not be considered an impediment to the continuation of work by those who are in the process of meeting requirements.
--- seg-14efd9e0ed842d1ea8102d18 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 3. The duties of archaeologists are:
--- seg-3a4d3563e44c7be7373cad50 [machine-unreviewed] ---
I - planning, organizing, managing, directing, and supervising archaeological research activities;
--- seg-180d6cf1f8a3ede88abcf3bb [machine-unreviewed] ---
II - identify, record, prospect, excavate, and conduct surveys of archaeological sites;
--- seg-eddc229611206d39b6a48170 [machine-unreviewed] ---
III - perform analysis, classification, interpretation, and scientific information services of archaeological interest;
--- seg-20f255ab34c182d56b57f08b [machine-unreviewed] ---
IV - Ensure the proper implementation of legislation regarding archaeological activities in the country;
--- seg-dc89b6f7ad8e70d48ab01b72 [machine-unreviewed] ---
V - to coordinate, lead, supervise, and manage the Archaeology sectors in governmental institutions of direct and indirect public administration, as well as in private entities, as provided for in Article 9 of this Law;
--- seg-2b1fda392a2e393e8f4002c9 [machine-unreviewed] ---
VI - providing consulting and advisory services in the field of Archaeology;
--- seg-37617ec24bdc600f6f5b8e21 [machine-unreviewed] ---
VII - Conducting examinations to determine the scientific and cultural value of archaeological interests, as well as their authenticity;
--- seg-57eb2cce57077d6747fb4c02 [machine-unreviewed] ---
VIII - To direct, supervise, and execute training, enhancement, and specialization programs for qualified individuals in the field of Archaeology;
--- seg-df9ba54ac4181d21faa575a1 [machine-unreviewed] ---
IX - to promote the organization of seminars, colloquia, competitions, and exhibitions of national or international scope in the field of Archaeology, ensuring representation therein;
--- seg-6b94d9f0d839ea87564f1897 [machine-unreviewed] ---
X - prepare opinions related to issues of interest in the field of Archaeology;
--- seg-c8242ccb747f7d59aa36a3a5 [machine-unreviewed] ---
XI - Coordinate, supervise, and lead projects and programs in the field of Archaeology.
--- seg-af79860a36a0de94c3fded76 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Art. 4° The hiring, appointment, or performance of technical positions, jobs, or roles

II - RELATOR'S VOTE
                  Deputy Ricardo Izar rightly points out in his bill that individuals suffering from degenerative diseases
present a picture of "gradual tissue damage of an irreversible and progressive nature, usually limiting vital
functions."
--- seg-cb07aa6c188f59988807cdcf [machine-unreviewed] ---
The incidence of degenerative diseases, which has been growing in proportion due to the aging of the population, represents a major public health concern and a tremendous burden on those affected and their caring families.
--- seg-baab0d791e236b375886a51d [machine-unreviewed] ---
The project under review, which demonstrates the sensitivity and concern of the parliament on the subject, aims to grant benefits to sufferers of degenerative diseases.
--- seg-4506f26f76fbdde37930e7d6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Within the thematic competence of CTASP, it is necessary to position itself regarding the merits of the proposed amendment to Article 20, item XI, of Law No. 8,036, of May 11, 1990, which regulates the Fund.

===== PAGE 279 [page-807f3209163b1812432eec47] =====
--- seg-1e3df9d9b79a04c67653b6bb [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                           DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                      Tuesday 15 279
--- seg-9a02d8521da7451b0460603b [needs-review] ---
of Service Time Guarantee, which aims to authorize a new withdrawal hypothesis.
--- seg-569af9011113499a96058f88 [needs-review] ---
However, although we consider the amendment to be fair, we understand that the proposal requires adjustments, as it would not be approved in its current form due to Constitutional Amendment No. 95.
--- seg-88335e416d9078a75d91dbd3 [needs-review] ---
In this context, before we present the reasons that led us to change our opinion, we want to make it very clear that we are strongly against the aforementioned Constitutional Amendment No. 95.
--- seg-f98c0c3d4dc5a075b578eed9 [needs-review] ---
Amendment 95, by setting limits on the preparation and execution of budgets, establishes a dual control for public expenditure in terms of a ceiling: a prior one, at the level of budgetary authorization, and a posterior one, during financial execution. Additional credits cannot expand the amount authorized in the OLA (Article 107, § 5, of the ADCT), except when it comes to an extraordinary credit opened by provisional measure, in the situations provided for in the Constitution.
--- seg-f7d74b5e263c39cf22efd119 [needs-review] ---
With the promulgation of the aforementioned amendment, a new fiscal regulation was established in our legal system, setting limits on public spending until 2036, as well as defining controls over legislative changes that have a budgetary impact. As part of the amendments made by the mentioned Constitutional Amendment, Article 113 of the Transitional and Final Provisions (ADCT) states the following:
--- seg-bd139f646ee08e91bb0d97b3 [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 113. A legislative proposal that creates or alters mandatory expenditure or
                        revenue abandonment must be accompanied by an estimate of its budgetary and
                        financial impact.
--- seg-203f72ab01ff85e6483472f5 [needs-review] ---
The new constitutional precept thus became a fundamental reference for the budgetary and financial adequacy analysis conducted within the National Congress and the other branches of the Union, adding greater reinforcement to the existing legal framework in the Fiscal Responsibility Law and the Budget Guidelines Law.
--- seg-3a525ca583044f7418d8bfb4 [needs-review] ---
The Budget Guidelines Law (Law 13473/2017) establishes in its Article 112:
--- seg-582e025303f14c07d26e8c1c [machine-unreviewed] ---
Article 112. Legislative proposals and their respective amendments, as provided in Article 59 of the Federal Constitution, that directly or indirectly result in a reduction of revenue or an increase in expenses for the Union, shall be accompanied by estimates of these effects in the exercise in which they enter into force and in the two subsequent exercises, detailing the respective calculation memory and corresponding compensation, for the purpose of budgetary and financial adequacy and compatibility with the constitutional and legal provisions that govern the matter.
--- seg-d382bea5b990f017ac7e26c0 [not-required] ---
(...)
--- seg-7638be42d45284f1e19e19b9 [machine-unreviewed] ---

                                     (by Mr. Leo de Brito)

It proposes that the Financial Oversight and Control Commission, with the assistance of the Union Accounts Court (TCU), oversee the use of funds transferred by the National Fund for Development (FNDE) to the municipality of Tarauacá, AC, in 2012, for the construction of a preschool; with a recommendation from the Financial Oversight and Control Commission for its archiving (relator: DEP.).
