PRELIMINARY REPORT
--- seg-9d659b3c8abd7ce2ae80f051 [machine-unreviewed] ---
I – PFC REQUEST
--- seg-bde9dce7f7064a7e03dacf1c [needs-review] ---
Deputy Leo de Brito (PT/AC), based on Articles 60, paragraph I, and 61, paragraph I of the Internal Regulation of this House, submitted a Proposal for Oversight and Control (PFC) to conduct, after hearing the plenary of this committee, an oversight and control act regarding the use of resources transferred by the National Fund for Education Development (FNDE) to the municipality of Tarauacá, in the state of Acre, in the 2012 fiscal year, for the construction of a preschool. The author of the proposal justifies that surveillance and control become necessary due to an accusation brought by the General Attorney's Office of the Municipality of Tarauacá through a Civil Action of Administrative Improbity against the former Mayor MARILETE VITORINO DE SIQUEIRA and some members of her administration. The Action aims to investigate potential crimes of responsibility and acts of administrative improbity,
related to bid-rigging and misappropriation of public funds from Term of Commitment PAC #
202501/2012, entered into with the Ministry of Education, through the FNDE, for the construction of
an educational unit, such as a daycare/preschool. According to the Action, the former Mayor Marilete Vitorino, assisted by her Finance Secretary, Claudio Amim and in
conspiracy with the legal representative of the company CONSTRUTORA VITÓRIA COMÉRCIO E REPRESENTAÇÕES LTDA,
Mr. Raimundo Lima do Nascimento "withdrew" the importance of R$ 218,396.85 (two hundred and eighteen thousand, three hundred and ninety-six reais and eighty-five centavos), claiming it was the first measurement of the work. The document states that although the payment was made for the measurement of a service performed, no actual work was executed. According to the Municipal Prosecutor's Office, "the bad faith and fraud in causing damage to the Treasury are indisputable, as the involved parties, with equal intent, combined efforts to divert the amount of R$ 218,396.85 (two hundred and eighteen thousand, three hundred and ninety-six reais and eighty-five centavos)." Furthermore, the Prosecutor adds that the desire to divert resources is so evident that the performance note related to the contract was issued by the Administration before the competition was even approved, which occurred on August 29, 2012. It is certain that the commitment note was issued on August 27, 2012, two days before the approval and three days before the contract's celebration. Asserts that this inversion of the order

===== PAGE 285 [page-240b7488a443240e785dd256] =====
--- seg-c54413c215c8d2d747b01bc6 [machine-unreviewed] ---
May 2018                       DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         Tuesday 15 285
--- seg-79a5b63804182e4f5d257dcd [needs-review] ---
It appears absolutely illegal, as it precedes the acts of adjudication and homologation, given that the issuance of an engagement note is legally impossible without knowledge of the final outcome of the bidding procedure.

It is also noted in the list of irregularities the omission of the Finance Secretary regarding the retention of values due to Social Security and Service Tax - ISS, facilitating, thus, the incorporation of these values into the contractor's patrimony, to the notable detriment of the public treasury.

Furthermore, the irregularities also involve members of the Tender Commission, who, in the interest of assisting the former mayor in her intentions, orchestrated a dark repertoire of illegalities consisting of "assembling" the preliminary procedure of the competition to evade the legal deadline for publication inherent to the Tender mode; the qualification of a bidder who failed to demonstrate fiscal regularity; the unjust and unrecorded exclusion of qualified bidders from the proposal opening phase, prejudicing the competitive nature of the tender and the nullification of the concluded contract due to the absence of its summary publication.

Therefore, in light of the non-execution of the object of the agreement, coupled with numerous flaws in the financial and budgetary execution course, which characterize violations to the principles that govern the public administration, notably Legality, Morality, and Efficiency, the author proposes this Proposal for Oversight and Control aimed at recovering the public resource in question and holding public agents accountable.

Indeed, the PFC, in accordance with Article 137, caput, in combination with Article 61, Item I, both of the Internal Regulation of this House, was received, numbered as 80, 2016, and referred to this Committee for Oversight and Control.

II – OPPORTUNITY AND CONVENIENCE
This Relator, considering the current nature of the complaint, deems it undeniable that it is both timely and convenient to implement this Proposal for Financial Oversight, which, as explicitly stated by Deputy Leo de Brito, is based on possible irregularities in the allocation of FNDE resources for the construction of a daycare center.

III – COMPETENCE OF THIS COMMITTEE
Article 32, XI, b, of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, in conjunction with the same article's sole paragraph, supports this Committee's competence to exercise financial, budgetary, and patrimonial oversight and control related to FNDE resources, an autonomous entity responsible for implementing educational policies of the Ministry of Education - MEC, in order to investigate possible irregularities in the exercise of its external control competence conferred to the Legislative Branch by Article 70 of the Federal Constitution.

This is because the analysis of federal resources transferred to other public entities falls within the scope of budgetary, financial, and patrimonial oversight, given that it is the Union's responsibility to verify the correct use of its property. In the specific situation of this PFC, the honorable author directly points out irregularities in the use of FNDE resources.

IV – LEGAL, ADMINISTRATIVE, POLITICAL, ECONOMIC, SOCIAL, AND BUDGETARY SCOPE
From a legal perspective, it is necessary to verify if there was a violation, either deliberate or not, of a legal norm, in order to identify the responsible party(ies) and obtain reimbursement for any potential damage to the treasury.

Regarding the budgetary perspective, it is important to analyze if there was misapplication of public resources regarding the budgetary action related to the FNDE.

From economic and social standpoints, according to the justification of this proposal, FNDE resources in the amount of R$ 218,396.85 (two hundred and eighteen thousand, three hundred and ninety-six reais and eighty-five centavos) were released for the construction of a daycare center. However, the author of the PFC argues that the school unit was not built, which would constitute the misappropriation of public funds and an evident detriment to the treasury and society.

===== PAGE 286 [page-1dd03ef0088b9d451b7902d0] =====
--- seg-299949224fcccdaf2cde5c51 [machine-unreviewed] ---
286 Tuesday, May 15                         DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                     2018
--- seg-3192d605c3b443899fac483e [needs-review] ---
The population in light of the non-delivery of the public good. Regarding the administrative focus, it is necessary to monitor the acts of execution and accountability for public resources at issue. Finally, as for the political focus, it is worthwhile to highlight the beneficial effects for society stemming from an inspection action carried out under the auspices of the Legislative Power, which results in the recovery of the public resource in question and the accountability of the involved agents.

- **PLAN FOR IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION METHODOLOGY**

The inspection requested by the honorable Author will be more effective if carried out by the Union Court of Accounts (TCU) through an audit of the application of federal funds from the FNDE allocated to the municipality of Tarauacá-AC, with the aim of investigating possible irregularities in the construction of a day care center, as well as recovering losses to the treasury, as justified in this proposal.

It is worth noting that the Federal Constitution confers upon the Union Court of Accounts (TCU) the role of an auxiliary organ of the Legislative Power to conduct audits and inspections regarding any natural or legal person, public or private, who administers or utilizes Union assets or values, as well as to oversee the application of any resources transferred by the Union through a convention or other similar instrument to municipalities, as per the following provisions:

"Article 70. The accounting, financial, budgetary, operational, and patrimonial oversight of the Union and of entities in direct or indirect public administration shall be conducted by the National Congress through external control, and by each Power's internal control system.

Sole Paragraph. Anyone, whether natural or legal, public or private, who utilizes, collects, keeps, manages, or administers public funds, assets, or values, or for whom the Union is accountable, or who, in the Union's name, assumes monetary obligations, shall be required to provide accounts.

Article 71. The external control, entrusted to the National Congress, shall be conducted with the assistance of the Union Court of Accounts, which shall be responsible for:

...

IV - conducting, on its own initiative or at the request of the Chamber of Deputies, the Federal Senate, a technical committee, or an inquiry, inspections and audits of a financial, budgetary, operational, and patrimonial nature...;

...

VI - overseeing the application of any resources transferred by the Union through a convention, agreement, arrangement, or other similar instrument to States, the Federal District, or municipalities." (Original text without emphasis)

In this regard, the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies stipulates:

"Article 24. Standing Committees, in accordance with their areas of competence, and other Committees, to the extent applicable, shall:

...

X - order, with the assistance of the Union Court of Accounts, the conduct of inquiries, expert examinations, inspections, and audits of a financial, budgetary, operational, and patrimonial nature in the administrative units of the Legislative, Executive, and Judicial Powers, as well as in the direct and indirect public administration, including foundations and institutions established and maintained by the Federal Public Power."

===== PAGE 287 [page-de9515b1dbebd5f30df99faf] =====
--- seg-7c37cbe2e4b3641515311bf4 [needs-review] ---
May 2018                       JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES                         Tuesday, May 15, 2018, 287
--- seg-2e640c60c7989eb235429862 [needs-review] ---
Thus, the implementation of this PFC will be carried out through an audit by the TCU on the use of public funds transferred by the FNDE to the municipality of Tarauacá, in the state of Acre, in the 2012 fiscal year, for the construction of a preschool. The purpose of the audit is to verify if the object of the agreement or similar instrument was executed, as well as any irregularities in its financial and budgetary execution, with a view to recovering the public resource in question and holding the involved agents accountable, if the indicated irregularities are confirmed. Furthermore, it is necessary to determine that the TCU send a copy of the result of the inspection object of this PFC to this Commission, with such copy being available to interested parties at the Commission's Secretariat. On this occasion, this Rapporteur will prepare the Final Report of the PFC in question for the consideration of this Commission. VI – VOTE
In light of the above, I submit my vote in favor of implementing PFC nº 80, 2016, proposed by Honorable Deputy Leo de Brito, as described in the Implementation Plan and Evaluation Methodology presented above.

FINAL REPORT
I - INTRODUCTION
--- seg-0667d5c195d0dd09528c16f1 [needs-review] ---
This is the Fiscalization and Control Proposal - PFC, No. 80 of 2016, authored by Mr. Deputy Leo de Brito, presented to this Commission, which aims to conduct fiscalization and control, through the Union Accounts Court - TCU, in the application of public resources transferred by the National Fund for Educational Development - FNDE to the municipality of Tarauacá, in the state of Acre, in the 2012 fiscal year, for the construction of a preschool. A PFC is instructed with the justifications pointing out the irregular acts committed by the
Municipality of Tarauacá regarding the execution of the object of the agreement or similar instrument,
as well as any irregularities in its financial and budgetary execution. The proposal author states that, in light of allegations of irregularities, it becomes justified
to implement an audit, to be conducted through the TCU, with the aim of investigating them, recovering
public resources spent irregularly, and holding accountable the agents involved, should the alleged
irregularities be confirmed. Finally, it was determined that the TCU send a copy of the inspection result object of this PFC to this Commission for the elaboration of the Final Report, which must be reviewed by this Collegiate. II – IMPLEMENTATION OF PFC
       The Preliminary Report, presented by Deputy Valtenir Pereira, was approved by the Financial Oversight and Control Commission – CFFC on December 7, 2016, with instructions to implement the PFC in accordance with the form and procedure established in Article 24, X, of this House's Rules. Thus, it was established that the

HAVING EXAMINED, reported and discussed these records of the request by the National Congress, prepared by the Fiscalization Financial and Control Commission of the Chamber of Deputies (CFFC), to have the Tribunal oversee the use of funds transferred to the municipality of Tarauacá/AC in 2012 by the National Fund for Education Development, intended for the construction of preschools. THE MINISTERS OF THE COURT OF ACCOUNTS OF THE FEDERAL UNION, MEETING IN A PLENARY SESSION,
                     BASED ON THE REASONING PRESENTED BY THE REPORTER, DECIDE:

                     9.1.4. The Court will convert this request into a special accounting take;
                     9.2. Order the conversion of the records into a special accounting take, in accordance

                     9.3. Declare this request fully met, in accordance with Article 14, IV, of TCU

                     9.4. Inform the interested parties and responsible individuals of this decision. The guiding vote of the above Judgment succinctly describes the object and the measures taken by the oversight conducted by the TCU, within the scope of processo nº TC-036.037/2016-8, as follows:

This is a request from the National Congress drafted by the Commission on Financial Oversight and Control of the Chamber of Deputies (CFFC) through the 251/2016/CFFC-P office of December 13, 2016, in response to the proposal for oversight and control 80/2016, which requested the Court to conduct oversight on the use of resources transferred to the municipality of Tarauacá/AC by the National Fund for Education Development (FNDE) for the purpose of building preschools.

===== PAGE 289 [page-41c53829218dfd8c7baf7d4a] =====
--- seg-dcf70584149a87282e451341 [needs-review] ---
May 2018                 CHAMBER OF DEPUTIES DAILY LOG                     Tuesday, May 15, 2018 289
--- seg-d0566558fc3044894c46a66b [needs-review] ---
The audit team of the Court investigated that R$ 1,856,954.85 was transferred to the municipality through five bank orders, and that the funds would be used for actions within the Proinfância program, as provided for in the PAC 2 commitment term 02501/2012. The object of the agreement was the construction of two daycares/preschools, of which only one was built. However, according to supporting documents obtained by the audit team, the municipality of Taruacá/AC made an advance payment to Construtora Vitória Com. e Rep. A limited company in the amount of R$ 218,396.85, without ever having provided any engineering services for the construction of the second unit of early childhood education. The advance payment made to the contractor, in addition to not having been provided for in the contract
               entered into between the contractor and the municipality, violates the provisions of articles 62 and 63 of Law
               4.320/1964, which prohibit the payment of public expenses without prior regular liquidation. The following parties responsible for this irregularity have been identified by the technical unit: (i) Construtora Vitória Com. e Rep. Ltda., for having issued a tax invoice in the amount of
               R$ 218,396.85, without having provided the construction services of the day care center, (ii) Mr. Cláudio

Amim de Moura, financial secretary of the municipality of Tarauacá/AC, for having subscribed the payment order to settle the tax invoice in the amount of R$ 218,396.85 and (iii) Mrs. Marilete Vitorino de Siqueira, mayor of the municipality of Tarauacá/AC, for having subscribed the
               payment order to settle the tax invoice in the amount of R$ 218,396.85. The audit team also identified an irregularity regarding the lack of performance of the guarantee by the contractor, Construtora Vitória Com. Rep. (presumably meaning "Representative" or "Member of Congress") Ltda., for the construction of the daycare center, as provided for in clause VIII of the bidding document 8/2012. Had the municipality taken the precaution of demanding a 5% guarantee of the
               total contract value, some of the advance payment made incorrectly to the contractor
               could have been recovered. This irregularity, specifically, is attributed to Mrs. Marilete Vitorino de Siqueira,
               mayor of the municipality of Tarauacá/AC, who celebrated the contract 69/2012 with the
               Vitória Construtora Com. Rep. (presumably meaning "Representative" or "Member of Congress") The company, without certifying the fulfillment of the condition stipulated in the tender, which provided for the presentation of guarantees, thus violated Article 41 of Law 8.666/1993. Regarding the daycare center that was built and inaugurated, the audit team identified that FNDE (National Fund for Educational Development) found defects in the work execution, which, according to the documentation collected during field work, had not yet been remedied by the company, Construtora Peres Ltda. The technical unit does not have elements to assess whether the non-conformities of the already built day care center result in damage to the public treasury. However, considering that there are elements for characterizing damage in relation to the non-built daycare center and that the Court may conduct inquiries with the FNDE to obtain the necessary information to quantify the actual value due or estimate it through reliable means in relation to the already built daycare center, the records should be converted into a special audit, in accordance with Article 47 of Law 8.443/1993.
